Gonogo WebSocket API

The WebSocket API of the Gonogo mod: 87 telemetry channels a client subscribes to and 64 commands it sends, each with its payload and what it means, all over one socket.

Building a widget or an Uplink? Use the SDK instead: the Uplink developer docs.

The Gonogo mod's telemetry socket

ws://localhost:8090

Served by the mod inside the running game, by default at localhost:8090; the host and port can be changed per install. Connect to ws://<host>:<port>.

First connection

  1. Open a WebSocket to ws://localhost:8090 and set its binaryType to "arraybuffer": every frame arrives as a binary message holding UTF-8 JSON. The mod sends hello, then game-state.

    {
  "type": "hello",
  "bootId": "5b0d6c2e",
  "modVersion": "1.0.0",
  "contractMajor": 44,
  "contractMinor": 8
}
    {
  "type": "game-state",
  "state": "ready",
  "scene": "FLIGHT"
}

  2. Subscribe to a channel. The mod answers with an event named subscribed, then sends a stream-data frame each time the value changes.

    {
  "type": "subscribe",
  "topic": "vessel.flight"
}
    {
  "type": "event",
  "topic": "vessel.flight",
  "name": "subscribed",
  "keyframeIntervalUt": 30,
  "meta": {
    "source": "system",
    "validAt": 1842006.5,
    "seq": 917,
    "deliveredAt": 1842006.5,
    "vantage": "ground:Kerbal Space Center",
    "quality": 1,
    "active": true,
    "staleness": 0,
    "timelineEpoch": 3,
    "sampleId": 4127
  }
}
    {
  "type": "stream-data",
  "topic": "vessel.flight",
  "payload": {
    "latitude": -0.0972,
    "longitude": -74.5577,
    "altitudeAsl": 72840.31,
    "altitudeTerrain": 72837.02,
    "verticalSpeed": -4.2,
    "surfaceSpeed": 2287.4,
    "orbitalSpeed": 2301.8,
    "gForce": 0.02,
    "dynamicPressureKPa": 0.0004,
    "mach": 7.63,
    "atmDensity": 0.0000012,
    "externalTemperature": 231.4,
    "atmosphericTemperature": 228.9,
    "meta": {
      "source": "vessel:8f2c1d40-97ab-4a2e-9c1f-6d0b3e5a7c11"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "source": "system",
    "validAt": 1842006.5,
    "seq": 918,
    "deliveredAt": 1842006.5,
    "vantage": "ground:Kerbal Space Center",
    "quality": 1,
    "active": true,
    "staleness": 0,
    "timelineEpoch": 3,
    "sampleId": 4127
  }
}

  3. Send a command with a requestId of your choosing. Its answer is a command-response carrying the same requestId. label and topic are required but free; sentAt may be 0.

    {
  "type": "command-request",
  "requestId": "pause-1",
  "command": "time.setPaused",
  "label": "time.setPaused",
  "topic": "",
  "args": {
    "paused": true
  },
  "sentAt": 0
}
    {
  "type": "command-response",
  "requestId": "pause-1",
  "result": {
    "success": true
  },
  "meta": {
    "source": "system",
    "validAt": 0,
    "seq": 919,
    "deliveredAt": 1842006.9,
    "vantage": "ground:Kerbal Space Center",
    "quality": 1,
    "active": true,
    "staleness": 0,
    "timelineEpoch": 3,
    "sampleId": 4127
  }
}

  4. The mod sends every frame as a binary WebSocket message holding UTF-8 JSON, so read each one as bytes. In a browser:

    const socket = new WebSocket("ws://localhost:8090");
socket.binaryType = "arraybuffer";
const text = new TextDecoder();

socket.addEventListener("open", () => {
  socket.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "subscribe", topic: "vessel.flight" }));
});

socket.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
  const bytes = new Uint8Array(event.data);
  if (bytes[0] === 0x9e) return; // a binary-lane frame, see stream-binary
  const frame = JSON.parse(text.decode(bytes));
  if (frame.type === "stream-data") console.log(frame.topic, frame.payload);
});

Frames the mod sends

  • stream-data: a subscribed topic's value
  • stream-binary: a subscribed topic's value as raw bytes, for a channel that uses the binary lane
  • event: something that happened to a subscription
  • command-response: the result of a command
  • command-accepted: the receipt for a delayed command, sent before its result
  • error: a request the mod refused or could not read
  • hello: the first frame on every connection
  • game-state: what the game is doing: loading, ready or no game
  • pong: the answer to a ping

Route on the type field: each frame type fixes it to a constant. A client ignores a type it does not know.

All but stream-binary are WebSocket frames holding UTF-8 JSON that starts with {. A stream-binary frame starts with the byte 0x9E and a lane byte, then a two-byte big-endian header length and a JSON header, and the payload bytes follow the header. The stream-binary frame type describes that header. Only commcast.radio and the channels of an installed Uplink use binary frames, and neither is listed here.

Frames a client sends

  • subscribe: start receiving a channel
  • unsubscribe: stop receiving a channel
  • set-vantage: choose the command centre this connection observes from and commands from
  • claim: ask for the answers to commands sent on an earlier connection
  • ping: ask whether the connection is alive
  • command-request: send one command
  • command-group: send several delayed commands to one craft as a unit

Subscribing

A channel's name is the topic of its frames, or the command of a command-request. The mod sends a channel only after the client has sent subscribe for it, and answers the subscribe with an event named subscribed on that channel. A subscribe to a channel nothing declares is answered with an error frame carrying unknownTopic and the topic instead. A frame emitted while nothing is subscribed is dropped, not queued, so a client that connects and waits receives nothing.

The first stream-data after subscribed can be the channel's last value sent again, with a meta.validAt older than the subscribed event's. Order frames by meta.validAt, not by when they arrive.

Game time

No channel carries the current game time (UT). It is the meta.validAt of the newest frame, and there is no clock channel. In flight, vessel.flight sends a frame about once a second, so its frames keep a clock current. Where nothing changes, as at the Space Center, frames come only on a change or at each channel's Repeats interval: between frames, advance the newest validAt by warpRate from time.warp for each real second, and not at all while its paused is true.

Commands

A command-response says the command ran, or why it did not. It is not the change itself: that arrives on the affected channel's next frame, for time.setPaused the next time.warp frame.

Units

On the wire a quantity is a bare JSON number in the unit its field lists, in commands as well as in telemetry. A unit of 1 is a plain ratio, and count is a number of things. A field that is not a quantity lists what kind of value it holds instead: text is words for a person to read, id is an identifier to match and not to show, flag is a boolean and enum is an enum's ordinal. A field with no unit listed did not declare one.

Enums

Most enums are sent as their integer ordinal. A few, such as errorCode, are sent as a string. Each enum's table shows the value sent, beside the member's name and description. An enum whose members combine as bit flags is an integer, with its members listed on the schema.

Channel properties

Each channel card shows some of these properties, which JSON Schema has no field for. A property that is absent was not stated.

  • Delivery, on a telemetry channel. "Latest value only" (lossy-latest) keeps only the newest value, so a client that falls behind sees the latest state and none of the ones it missed. "Every value, in order" (reliable-ordered) sends every value, in order, and carries occurrences such as flight.started that a client must not drop
  • Delay, on a telemetry channel. "After signal delay" (delayed) means the value is what this connection's command centre knew one signal delay ago (see set-vantage). "Live" (true-now) means it is not delayed, as for a fact on the ground such as whether the SCANsat assembly is installed
  • Held at home, on a delayed telemetry channel: the value is held at the home command centre (the career ledger, the space centre's records) and not aboard a craft. Each command centre receives a change after its own delay to home, so the value it holds is already as current as it can be there, and a client subtracts no further signal delay
  • Samples, on a telemetry channel. "Continuous" (continuous) values change between samples, so a client may draw a line or interpolate. "Holds until changed" (discrete) values hold until the next sample, so a client draws a step. "One per event" (event) is one occurrence per sample, so a client draws points
  • Repeats, on a telemetry channel: the seconds of game time after which the channel sends its value again with nothing changed, so a late subscriber or a reconnect recovers without waiting for a change. Game time runs up to 100000 times faster than real time under time warp and stops while the game is paused, so measure staleness by meta.validAt and not by a real-time timer
  • Empty is an answer, on a telemetry channel: an empty value is a real answer and is sent from the first tick (no target selected, no crew aboard). Without it the channel sends nothing until it has had a real value, so silence means "not yet" and not "none"
  • Takes effect, on a command: "when sent", or "after the signal delay" for a command that travels from the command centre before it runs. The card's description says where it goes
  • Receipt, on a delayed command: when its signal delay is more than zero, a command-accepted frame arrives as the command leaves, and the command-response arrives once it has run
  • No fields, on a schema: the payload is an empty object, as for a command that takes no arguments

Channels not listed here

  • Channels named per subject, such as trackingStation.vessel.<id>.<field>, currency.<id>.<currency> and per-vessel part actions. The mod creates them while the game runs, one set per subject, so they cannot be listed here. Subscribe to one by its full name, with the subject's id filled in
  • Each installed Uplink's own channels and commands, which that Uplink documents

A shared prefix does not put two channels in the same group: trackingStation.catalog is listed here, and trackingStation.vessel.<id>.<field> is named per subject and is not.

Connection frames

Every frame on the socket. Each channel and command below travels inside one of these: telemetry in stream-data, a command in command-request and its answer in command-response.

A client sends

Client sends

command-request

Send one command

A command the client sends: the command id, its arguments, and a request id that the reply carries back.

command is the channel's address and args is that command's own args type. Each command's command-request message fixes both. The answer comes back as a command-response with the same requestId, or as an error frame if the mod refused it or could not read it. label and topic are required but free, and sentAt may be 0.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "command-request"
requestId string

An id the client chooses; the reply carries it back.
command string

The command id, such as vessel.control.setThrottle.
label string

Any text: the mod shows it back, unchanged, beside this command on system.uplink.pending, and never reads it otherwise. Send the command id if there is nothing better. When empty, show command-request.command instead.
topic string

A channel to show beside this command on system.uplink.pending, unchanged; the mod never reads it otherwise. Send "" if there is none.
vantage optional string | null

Per-call vantage override: the command centre id this command dispatches from, which decides its signal delay. Optional: null or empty uses the connection's own vantage (see set-vantage). A command about the space program rather than a craft (tech, strategy, contract) sends "meta", which carries no delay whichever centre the operator has selected; sent from a centre instead, it rides that centre's delay to the home command, which is none for a ground station. A centre that is not active is refused with an unknownVantage error.
seenVesselId optional string | null

The vessel the operator was looking at when the command was pressed: the vesselId of the newest vessel.identity reading the client holds. Optional: null or empty states nothing and the command is not checked against it. A command for the active vessel is refused with wrongState at the press when the game's active vessel is not this one, because the operator's screen runs one signal delay behind the game and a switch inside that delay is not yet visible there. Commands that are not addressed to the active vessel ignore it.
args any

The command's own arguments. Each command's command-request message narrows this to that command's args schema.
sentAt number ut

When the client sent the command, in UT seconds (KSP universal time), the same base as Meta.validAt. Send 0 if you do not need it.

The mod stamps the response's Meta.deliveredAt off its own clock, so a caller timing a round trip measures against its own clock rather than reading this back. The field is carried onto the response's Meta.validAt, which therefore reads 0 on a command response unless the client fills this in.
Client sends

subscribe

Open delivery on a topic

Asks the mod to start sending a Topic to this connection.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "subscribe"

The frame type, always "subscribe".
topic string

The Topic id to start receiving.
Client sends

unsubscribe

Close delivery on a topic

Asks the mod to stop sending a Topic to this connection.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "unsubscribe"

The frame type, always "unsubscribe".
topic string

The Topic id to stop receiving.
Client sends

set-vantage

Select this connection's command centre

Selects the command centre this connection commands from and observes at. It sets both where the connection's telemetry is observed from and where its commands are sent from. The id must name a currently-active command centre, or the request is refused with an unknownVantage error and the connection keeps the vantage it had.

A connection that has never sent one observes at the home command centre (the roster entry whose isHome is true), and follows it if home moves. When no home is identified it observes at the first ground station in ordinal id order, and while no command centre is active at all (the main menu) at none, stamping its frames with an empty vantage. Every frame's meta.vantage says which of these is in force.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "set-vantage"

The frame type, always "set-vantage".
centreId string

The command centre Id to adopt as this connection's vantage.
Client sends

claim

Claim the answers to commands sent on an earlier connection

Names the commands a client is still waiting on, sent after it reconnects to the game: a page reload, a dropped network or a restarted game has closed the connection the commands were sent on, and the answers they were owed have nowhere to go. For each requestId the game holds an answer for, it sends that answer now and forgets it; for each command still in flight it sends the answer to this connection when it comes; for each one it holds nothing for, it sends an error carrying replyNotReceived, so the client can stop waiting. Used by a client that keeps its outstanding commands across a reload, such as a command held for a craft out of contact.

An id is claimed only by the command centre that sent it: send this after set-vantage, and an id sent from another centre is answered as one the game holds nothing for. Answers are never sent to a connection that does not name their id.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "claim"

The frame type, always "claim".
requestIds string[]

The requestId of each command the client still waits on, as it sent them.
Client sends

ping

Ask whether the connection is alive

Asks for a pong, to tell a connection that is quiet from one that is dead. A subscribed connection can be silent for as long as nothing it subscribed to changes, so silence alone says nothing; a ping that goes unanswered does. It is replied to at once and in every scene, changes nothing, and needs no subscription.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "ping"

The frame type, always "ping".
nonce string

Anything the client likes, returned unchanged in the reply pong so it can tell which ping was answered. May be omitted, in which case the reply carries an empty one.
Client sends

command-group

Send several delayed commands to one craft as a unit

Several commands the client sends as one message: they travel together, arrive whole or not at all, are refused together, and run in order within a single physics tick. Each member is an ordinary command-request with its own requestId, and each is answered under that id as if it had been sent alone.

Every member must be a delayed command addressed to the same craft and sent from the same command centre. A group that breaks either rule, or is empty, is refused whole. If any member is refused for any reason, none is sent.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "command-group"

The frame type, always "command-group".
groupId string

An id the client chooses for the group as a whole.
members object[]

The commands, in the order they run.

The mod sends

Mod sends

stream-data

A subscribed channel's value

One Topic sample as the mod sends it: the Topic id, its payload, and the envelope stream-data.meta saying when the payload was true and when it arrived.

topic is the channel's address and payload is that channel's own shape. Each channel's stream-data message fixes both. meta is stamped by the mod on every frame and describes the delivery, not the value: validAt, deliveredAt and staleness are there.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "stream-data"
topic string

The Topic id this sample belongs to.
payload any

The topic's own value. Each channel's stream-data message narrows this to that channel's payload schema.
meta Meta
Mod sends

command-response

The answer to a command

The mod's reply to a command-request, matched to it by command-response.requestId.

result is the command's own reply type, fixed by that command's command-response message. A command that ran and was refused arrives here with success: false and an errorCode. A command the mod could not read is answered with an error frame instead.

There is no command field. requestId is the only link back to the command, and a delayed command's answer can arrive minutes after it.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "command-response"
requestId string

The id from the request this replies to. It is the only link back to the request, and a delayed command's reply can arrive minutes later.
result any

The command's own reply. Each command's command-response message narrows this to that command's reply schema.
meta Meta
Mod sends

command-accepted

The receipt for a delayed command, sent before its result

Sent the moment a command starts its delayed journey, carrying the one-way signal delay it will actually travel. It says the command is on its way and when to expect a reply, never that anything executed.

A client cannot work this out for itself. The delay depends on the craft or place the command is for, and on the command centre it was sent from. A loss deadline sized from the delay a client can see (the active craft's) is wrong for a command addressed to any other node.

Matched to its request by command-accepted.requestId, the client's own id from its command-request, because this frame comes back on the connection that sent the request. Entries on system.uplink.pending carry an id Gonogo assigns instead, since two clients can choose the same request id.

Absent for a command that never waits on the signal delay (one that takes effect when sent, or one whose delay is zero), because there is no flight to wait out. Absent also for a refusal, which sends an error instead. A client must therefore treat "no acceptance yet" as ordinary rather than as an error.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "command-accepted"

The frame type, always "command-accepted".
requestId string

The client's own id, echoed from its command-request.
oneWaySeconds optional number | null s

One-way signal delay from the sending vantage to the node this command is addressed to, as Gonogo knows it at dispatch. It is never re-sent: the sender may never learn of a route change after dispatch.

For a command held and forwarded on a lane it is how long the sending centre's own plan expects it to take to reach the craft, waits included, and absent when that plan knows no route, as for a craft the centre has not heard from yet. It is what the centre believed when it sent, and says nothing of whether the craft is really listening.
predictedReplyUt optional number | null ut

When Gonogo predicts the reply will come back, from the routes at dispatch, waits included. A client times its loss deadline from this when present, since a command held for a window replies long after twice the one-way time. Absent when no route was predicted.
expiresAtUt optional number | null ut

When the command is deleted wherever it is, if it has not run. Absent for a command that is not held at all.
warning optional string | null

What the operator should know about a command that was accepted anyway, as a sentence to show them. Present for a continuous input, a throttle or a control axis, that the sending centre's plan says would have to wait at a node: it is sent, and it is dropped where it would have waited, so it is likely to be lost. Absent otherwise.
Mod sends

event

A named occurrence on a topic, carrying no payload of its own

Something that happened to a subscription, sent on the Topic it happened to.

An event carries no payload of its own: event.name is the whole of what happened, and event.meta describes the delivery as it does on any other frame. The mod sends two names:

  • subscribed confirms a subscribe, once per subscribe. Wait for it rather than for the first stream-data: a channel with nothing to say yet sends the confirmation and then nothing. A subscribe to a channel nothing declares is answered with an error frame carrying unknownTopic and the topic instead
  • timeline-reset says the game quickloaded and time went backwards. It is sent for every Topic the connection holds, and anything built from frames before it should be discarded
FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "event"

The frame type, always "event".
topic string

The subscribed Topic the event happened to.
name string

What happened: subscribed or timeline-reset.
meta Meta

The delivery metadata, as on any other frame.
keyframeIntervalUt optional number | null s

On subscribed, the most game time the Topic's channel lets pass between two samples before it sends one unconditionally, even when the value has not changed. A client judges a quiet change-driven Topic as overdue only once it has been silent longer than this. Absent when the channel declares no keyframe cadence, and on timeline-reset; absent means unknown, never zero.
Mod sends

error

A dispatch that could not be carried, or a bad session request

A request the mod could not carry out: a frame it could not read, an unknown command, a command whose provider has stopped working, a result or payload that could not be written, a subscription to a Topic nothing declares, or a set-vantage naming a command centre that is not active. Nothing about the game was decided, so there is no game reason to report.

A command the game refused is not an error: it ran and said no, and that arrives as a command-response whose result has success: false and an errorCode from CommandErrorCode. That vocabulary never appears here.

error.requestId is set when the error is about a command, and error.topic when it is about a subscription. error.code is a FaultCode, whose full list gives the sentence an operator reads for each. A client's own transport adds its own members to the same field, and the mod never sends those.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "error"

The frame type, always "error".
requestId optional string | null

The id of the command request this error is about, or null.
topic optional string | null

The Topic this error is about, or null.
code FaultCode

Which fault: always a fault, never a refusal, since a command the game refused gets a command-response instead.
message string

The machinery's own account of what went wrong, for a log rather than an operator.
Mod sends

hello

The first frame on a connection, naming the run it reached

The first frame on every connection, sent before anything is asked for. hello.bootId names the run of the mod the connection has reached.

A client that reconnects and reads the id it read before has reached the same run: every meta.timelineEpoch it remembers still counts on from where it was, and only the connection's own state has to be set up again, which is each subscription and, where one was chosen, the vantage (see set-vantage: a new connection starts at the home command centre whatever the last one chose). A different id is another run, whose epochs count from zero, so nothing remembered of the old one can be compared with it.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "hello"

The frame type, always "hello".
bootId string

An opaque id made afresh each time the mod starts its stream, the same on every connection until it next does. Compare it for equality only.
modVersion optional string | null

The mod's release label: v1.4.0 for a release, rc-<sha> for a release candidate. Absent from the frame for a build that carries no label, such as one built from source.
contractMajor number

The major number of the wire contract the mod speaks. A client built for a different major cannot read this stream correctly.
contractMinor number

The minor number of the wire contract the mod speaks. A client built for an older minor misses what the mod added since; a client built for a newer minor asks for what the mod does not yet have.
Mod sends

game-state

What the game is doing: loading, ready or no game

What the game is doing, sent on its own and not through any topic. Sent straight after hello on every connection that has anything to learn, and again at every change.

It is not delayed by signal delay at any command centre: a load is a fact about the game on the machine, not about anything in flight.

While game-state.state is "loading" or "no-game", nothing the stream last said is current. Readings received before the frame are still the latest there are, and none of them is a live one. A "ready" that follows a load which started a new timeline arrives after that timeline's timeline-reset.

A client that reads no game-state frame (an older client, or a host that never sends one) is not wrong, only unaware: it drops a frame type it does not know.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "game-state"

The frame type, always "game-state".
state string

"loading", "ready" or "no-game". A client treats a value it does not know as "ready".
scene string

The scene being loaded while game-state.state is "loading", otherwise the scene that stands: one of KSP's scene names, such as "FLIGHT", "SPACECENTER", "TRACKSTATION", "EDITOR" or "MAINMENU".
Mod sends

pong

The answer to a ping

The answer to a ping.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "pong"

The frame type, always "pong".
nonce string

The ping.nonce of the ping this replies to.
Mod sends

stream-binary

A frame on a channel that uses the binary lane

The JSON header of a binary frame: everything about the delivery except the bytes themselves.

It carries the same stream-binary.meta as stream-data, so a binary delivery is subject to the signal delay, the vantage and the timeline epoch exactly as a JSON channel is, and cannot opt out of the delay. The difference is that the payload is not in the JSON. stream-binary.segments is the length table for the bytes that follow the header.

A frame whose segment lengths do not sum to exactly the bytes remaining after the header is not read: a truncated or over-long frame is dropped with a named reason and never replaced by an empty payload, since zero segments would read as "nothing was transmitted".

FieldTypeUnitDescription
type "stream-binary"

The frame type, always "stream-binary".
topic string

The Topic id this delivery belongs to.
segments number[]

Byte length of each segment, in the order they appear after the header. An empty table is valid and means "nothing this frame"; it is told apart from a broken frame because the sum still matches.
meta Meta

When the payload was true, when it arrived, and where it was observed from, as on a stream-data frame.

alarm 3 telemetry, 2 commands

Alarms set to fire at a game time

Telemetry 3

Telemetry

alarm.activeList

Delivery Every value, in orderDelay LiveSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 3600 s of game time

One SCET alarm (an alarm on the craft's own clock, spacecraft event time) as the game holds it: the alarm.activeList Topic is a bare array of these.

The roster exists so an operator can see which alarms are still set after a reconnect, and so a client can remove an entry it no longer remembers. The roster is held in memory for the game session and is not written to the save: when the session ends it is gone, and a client sets its alarms again. It is a list of what somebody asked for, not a reading of any craft, so the channel is not delayed by signal delay.

Payload ScetAlarm[] 11 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
id string

The client's own id for the alarm, minted where the alarm was created and carried unchanged. Setting an alarm under an id already held replaces it, so repeating alarm.scet.arm is idempotent and a reconnect cannot duplicate a row.
name string

What the operator called it. Echoed so a roster row a client no longer recognises can still be named on screen.
armedBy string

The command centre the alarm.scet.arm command was sent from, as a commandCentre.roster id.

Who asked for the alarm, never where it is read: that is ScetAlarm.vantage. A screen at a different vantage gets this field in full, unlike the condition and target, which would tell it about a craft before the signal delay from that craft has passed (see ScetAlarm.withheld).
vantage string

The place whose knowledge the condition is read against, and therefore the place that decides when this alarm comes due. A commandCentre.roster id ("ground:<name>", "vessel:<guid>"). An empty vantage in the command is resolved to the alarm's own ScetAlarm.subject when the alarm is set.

A vantage that is the subject reads the craft's true state, so the alarm comes due at the instant the condition is met. Any other vantage reads what that place has been told, which is a signal delay old and different everywhere, so the same condition comes due there after that place's signal delay. Every vantage sees the alarm come due; only the time differs.

This is not the sender: ScetAlarm.armedBy says where the command came from and nothing else. An operator at one centre may ask when another centre will know, which where the command entered cannot express.

A vantage is a place, not a connection: two operators sharing a command centre share its knowledge and its result.

This empty-means-subject default belongs to the alarm.scet.arm command.
subject string

What the condition is about: "vessel:<guid>" for a craft, or "game" for something the whole game shares. The same vocabulary meta.source uses.

A time condition is always "game": universal time is the game's, and a clock has no craft to belong to. A threshold names the craft, and this is what stops it re-aiming without notice when the player switches vessels: the game compares this against the meta.source stamped on the payload it read, and a reading about somebody else's craft is ignored.

A threshold on something the save owns rather than a craft is "game" too, such as career.status, and so is one on a Topic an Uplink contributes about the save.
condition optional ScetAlarmCondition | null

What the alarm watches for, as it was set, or null when ScetAlarm.withheld is true.
withheld boolean

Whether this row reached a session whose vantage is not the one that armed the alarm, and so carries only what that vantage may know.

A withheld row keeps ScetAlarm.id, ScetAlarm.armedBy, ScetAlarm.state and ScetAlarm.firedAtUt, and carries ScetAlarm.condition as null and ScetAlarm.name, ScetAlarm.vantage, ScetAlarm.subject, ScetAlarm.onFire and ScetAlarm.actsOn empty: what another place is watching would otherwise reach here faster than light could carry it. A time alarm is never withheld, because a universal time names no craft and is the same instant everywhere.
state ScetAlarmState

Where the alarm has got to: still watching, fired, unreachable or cancelled. See ScetAlarmState.
firedAtUt optional number | null ut

The universal time the alarm fired at, or null until it has fired. On the craft's clock, like ScetAlarmCondition.ut.
onFire ScetAlarmAction[]

What the craft does when this alarm fires, in order. Empty for an alarm that only stops the warp and says so. See ScetAlarmAction.
actsOn string

The craft ScetAlarm.onFire acts on, as "vessel:<guid>", or empty while there are no actions.

The actions run only if this craft is the one being flown when the alarm fires, and are withheld otherwise: a time condition belongs to the game rather than to any craft, so after a vessel switch its actions would otherwise land on whatever happened to be active.

Telemetry

alarm.scet.fired

Delivery Every value, in orderDelay LiveSamples One per eventRepeats every 3600 s of game time

The notice that an alarm judged on the craft's own clock (a SCET alarm, for spacecraft event time) has fired and the warp has been stopped.

Nothing about the craft. It says which alarm fired and when. The stop is immediate, because warp is; the telemetry is not, and stays a signal delay behind. Readings shown beside this notice may still show the craft as it was minutes ago, so a widget should not treat the notice as a reading: what the craft was doing at ScetAlarmFired.firedAtUt arrives with its telemetry.

The other fields say where it was learned and whether its actions were withheld for want of the right craft; neither is a reading of the craft.

The condition is not echoed: for a threshold it would be a claim about the craft ahead of the light that carries it. A client that wants to name the alarm reads the roster.

Payload ScetAlarmFired 4 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
id string

Which alarm, as the ScetAlarm.id it was set under.
firedAtUt number ut

The universal time it fired at, on the craft's clock.
vantage string

The place that learned it, echoing the alarm's ScetAlarm.vantage.

A notice at the subject's own vantage is a fact about the craft at the instant it happened; a notice anywhere else is a statement about what that place has been told, true only there.
actionsWithheld boolean

Whether the alarm held onboard actions and they were withheld because the craft named by ScetAlarm.actsOn was not the one being flown. False for an alarm with no actions.

Says nothing about how the craft responded to an action that was sent. That is a fact aboard the craft, and it reaches the ground the way every other one does, a signal delay later in the craft's own telemetry: this notice travels at once and must not carry it.

Command

alarm.scet.arm

Takes effect when sent

Register an alarm with the game, or replace one already registered under the same ScetAlarmArmArgs.id.

Never delayed by signal delay: setting an alarm changes nothing aboard the craft, so like time.setWarpIndex it is a control on the game, not a signal to a spacecraft. An alarm can therefore be set for an event less than one signal delay away, and during a blackout.

Arguments ScetAlarmArmArgs 7 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
id string

The client's own id for the alarm, echoed as ScetAlarm.id. An id already held is replaced rather than duplicated.
name string

What the operator called the alarm, echoed as ScetAlarm.name.
vantage string

See ScetAlarm.vantage. Empty is accepted and resolved to ScetAlarmArmArgs.subject when the alarm is set, so the alarm is read at its own subject.
subject string

See ScetAlarm.subject. Empty is read as "game".
condition ScetAlarmCondition

What the alarm watches for. See ScetAlarmCondition.
onFire ScetAlarmAction[]

See ScetAlarm.onFire. Non-empty only where the alarm is read at its own subject's vantage and that subject is a craft, or the condition is a time on the game's clock; any other alarm carrying actions is refused rather than accepted with them dropped.
actsOn string

See ScetAlarm.actsOn. A time condition carrying actions must name the craft the operator means them for. A threshold on a craft acts on that craft, so empty resolves to its subject and any other craft is refused.

career 3 telemetry, 9 commands

Contracts, crew hiring, facilities and strategies in career mode

Telemetry 3

Telemetry

career.facilities

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delayHeld at homeSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

The space centre's buildings, each with the level it stands at and the full run of levels it can be upgraded through (its tier count and what each upgrade costs).

When it arrives. A facility's tier count and prices are readable from the building objects, which KSP registers at the space centre, in the editor and in flight. The tracking station reads the tier the save holds against the ladder last read in one of those scenes. Where no ladder has been read there is no reading to take, so this channel goes silent rather than reporting a row of nulls. The last reading stands, dated, and the client marks it as held.

A tier count does not change during a save, so a ladder held from an earlier scene is still true. The tier standing on it can move, and does when the player buys an upgrade, so both travel together and are dated together rather than one being trusted further than the other.

Payload CareerFacilities 1 field
FieldTypeUnitDescription
facilities optional map of CareerFacility | null

A map keyed by SpaceCenterFacility name (e.g. "LaunchPad", "VehicleAssemblyBuilding"), not a fixed record, so enumerate the keys rather than reaching for one you expect to be there. A facility the game cannot report is left out of the map. Never empty on the wire: the channel is absent instead.

Telemetry

career.status

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delayHeld at homeSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

The KSC and career-mode snapshot, in four groups (balances, contracts, strategies, tech). The space centre's buildings are not here: they are on CareerFacilities, which can be held on its own while this channel keeps arriving.

Three states. The whole payload is null in a sandbox save, where there is no career at all. A non-null payload with a sub-group null means career mode is running and that group is unavailable this tick. All four group keys are always present, each nullable, never omitted, so a missing key is a protocol error rather than an absent group.

Every number is nullable and null is never a sentinel: a field is null whenever the raw value is absent or non-finite. The two counts (CareerStrategies.activeCount, CareerTech.unlockedCount) are the only non-nullable numbers, because an empty list counts as zero rather than as unknown.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
balances optional CareerBalances | null

The career's balances (funds, reputation, science). null when none of the three could be read this tick.
contracts optional CareerContracts | null

Active, offered and recently completed contracts. null when KSP's contract system is not loaded this tick.
strategies optional CareerStrategies | null

The save's strategy roster and which strategies are active. null when KSP's strategy system is not loaded this tick.
tech optional CareerTech | null

The tech tree and which of it is unlocked. null when R&D or the part list is not loaded this tick.
meta PayloadMeta

Provenance, and always "game": a career belongs to the save, not to anything flying, so switching vessels cannot change which one is being read.

A SCET alarm compares this stamp against the subject the alarm was set for, and refuses a reading that does not match. "game" is the same token ScetAlarm.subject carries for anything the whole simulation shares.

career.crew.fire

Takes effect after the signal delayReceipt command-accepted when delayed

Fire a hired kerbal, returning them to the applicant pool. Takes a hired kerbal's ProtoCrewMember.name, the same id spaceCenter.crewRoster publishes for each roster entry. Firing costs nothing and returns the kerbal to the applicant pool, so it is reversible: a re-hire brings them back with the same stats. commandCentre 4 telemetry

The command centres in play and the signal delay between them

Telemetry 4

Telemetry

commandCentre.activeVesselDelay

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 1000 s of game time

How far each command centre is from the active craft, one-way, along its own routed path: the delay every ordinary channel reaches that centre at, and the delay a command from it takes to arrive.

Sparse. A centre is listed only when it has a delay of its own. The home centre is never listed: its delay is comms.delay, which also carries the hold through a loss of signal. A centre other than home that is not listed has no route to the craft. Neither absence is a zero, so a client must not quote a delay for a centre that is missing from the list.

A crewed centre that is the active craft is listed at an explicit zero: a craft is no distance from itself.

Each command centre is sent its own. The centres listed are those on the receiving centre's own commandCentre.roster, and each figure is worked out from that centre's own contact plan, as comms.delay is: the receiving centre's own entry and its comms.delay are the same path.

Payload CommandCentreActiveVesselDelay 1 field
FieldTypeUnitDescription
centres CentreDelayEntry[]

Every centre with a delay of its own to the active craft.

Telemetry

commandCentre.roster

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 1000 s of game time

One command centre in the commandCentre.roster channel: a vantage the operator can command from and observe at. The roster is the union of the CommNet home nodes (KSC, Extra Ground Stations, Kerbal Konstructs sites) and crewed control-source vessels.

The Topic payload is a bare array of these entries, like SpaceCenterPoiEntry, one per centre, keyed by CommandCentreEntry.id.

Each command centre is sent its own roster, the centres it knows of. A ground station is on every centre's. A vessel that is a command centre joins a centre's roster when the vessel's own word that it is one has reached that centre, and stays on it until its word that it no longer is, or that it is gone, has: a crew boarding a vessel far away does not put a new centre on your roster before the light of it could arrive. A centre always lists itself.

Payload CommandCentreEntry[] 10 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
id optional string | null

Stable centre id, the one set-vantage.centreId takes: "ground:<name>" or "vessel:<guid>". Every ground station is "ground:<name>", the home one included: which centre is home is CommandCentreEntry.isHome, never a special id. Ground stations that share a name are told apart as "ground:<name>#2", "#3" and so on.
displayName optional string | null

Human-facing name.
kind optional string | null

One of GroundStation, CrewedVessel or Custom: the kind of centre.
bodyIndex optional number | null

Index of the body this centre sits on among the bodies trackingStation.bodies lists; null when unknown or not surface-anchored.
latitude optional number | null °

Body-fixed surface latitude of the centre in degrees, when surface-anchored; null for a moving vessel centre.

Null means "not applicable", not "not computed". A GroundStation always reports coordinates. A CrewedVessel reports them only while landed, splashed or pre-launch, since a point under a craft in flight sweeps at orbital rate and is not a place the centre occupies. So null says the centre is airborne or in space, and a client may act on that rather than treating it as missing data. The one case where an anchored centre reports null is a body that could not be read at all, and then CommandCentreEntry.bodyIndex is null too: the two travel together, so a null coordinate never appears beside a known body.

Always null or non-null together with CommandCentreEntry.longitude.
longitude optional number | null °

Body-fixed surface longitude of the centre in degrees, wrapped to (-180, 180], matching every other geographic value on the wire. Null under exactly the rule CommandCentreEntry.latitude documents, and always null together with it.
active boolean

Whether this centre is a valid command source right now.
isHome boolean

Whether this centre is the home command centre: the one that holds the career ledger.

At most one entry carries it. When the game cannot say which centre is home, as on an install whose ground stations all look alike to it, the first active ground station in ordinal id order carries it in home's place, with CommandCentreEntry.isHomeFallback set: the same centre a connection that has not chosen a command centre starts at. No entry carries it only when the roster holds no ground station at all.

Not the same fact as CommsHop.fromIsHome, which is true of every ground station and so cannot say which one is home.
isHomeFallback boolean

Whether this centre is home only because no home was identified: true on the one entry that carries CommandCentreEntry.isHome in its place, false on every other entry and on an identified home.

A client that shows this centre as home can still tell the operator that it is standing in, and name it, without working out the stand-in itself.
delayQuality optional string | null

Whether this centre can be routed to: "routed" (it has a CommNet node, so a control path can be found, occlusion-aware) or "unroutable" (no CommNet node, so no command path and no delay). No delay is estimated from position alone: commands travel over the relay network, so a centre with no route has no delay to quote.

commandCentre.separation

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 1000 s of game time

How far every active command centre is from every other, one-way, along the routed CommNet path: how long a message from someone at one centre takes to reach someone at another.

Sparse. A pair with no route has no entry, rather than a zero or a sentinel: messages travel over the relay network, so an unroutable pair has no separation to quote. No entry for a pair means the separation is unavailable, which is a different fact from it being large.

Each centre is always paired with itself at an explicit zero, so the one pair that is certain never reads as unavailable.

Each command centre is sent its own. The pairs are between the centres on the receiving centre's own commandCentre.roster, and each figure is the signal delay of the route that centre's own contact plan has open now, so a centre is quoted no separation from a vessel it has not heard is a command centre, and a figure moves when the news that moves it has arrived. Every ground station is the home centre's own antenna, so home is as far from a vessel as its nearest station is.

Payload CommandCentreSeparation 1 field
FieldTypeUnitDescription
pairs CentreSeparationEntry[]

Every ordered pair with a routed path, plus each centre's own zero.

commandCentre.unreachable

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 1000 s of game time

One command centre that was on commandCentre.roster earlier in this session and is not now, in the commandCentre.unreachable channel: a ground station whose node went away, a crewed vessel that lost its crew or was destroyed or recovered.

The Topic payload is a bare array of these entries, one per remembered centre that is currently off the roster, keyed by UnreachableCentreEntry.id. A centre that comes back leaves this channel and rejoins the roster, and a centre that has not been on the roster since the mod started is not listed at all: an absent id is a fact about what is unknown, not about what is reachable.

Each command centre is sent its own: the centres that have left its own commandCentre.roster. A vessel centre that is destroyed or loses its crew is listed here when its own word of that, or its silence, has reached the receiving centre, and UnreachableCentreEntry.lastReachableUt is when it was last on that centre's roster.

commcast 2 telemetry, 5 commands

Messages and groups between command centres

Telemetry 2

Telemetry

commcast.traffic

Delivery Every value, in orderDelay After signal delaySamples One per eventRepeats every 1000 s of game time

One item of commcast.traffic: something said to a group this vantage belongs to, delivered one signal delay after it was said from where it was said.

Addressed, never broadcast. A connection receives only the items addressed to its own vantage. A group's members are addressed as the speaker could see them when it spoke, so a centre added far away starts receiving once word of it has reached the speaker, and a member with no path from the speaker misses what was said.

A stream, not state. Nothing is replayed to a connection that subscribes after an item reached it, as with anything heard on a radio.

Three kinds, by CommcastTraffic.kind:

  • "members": a group opened or grew. CommcastTraffic.members is its whole membership after the change, CommcastTraffic.added who came in
  • "text": a message, CommcastTraffic.id and CommcastTraffic.body
  • "ack": a member acknowledging CommcastTraffic.messageId, addressed to that message's author alone

Telemetry

commcast.transmissions

Delivery Every value, in orderDelay After signal delaySamples One per eventRepeats every 1000 s of game time

One row of commcast.transmissions: a radio transmission this vantage can detect.

Detectable means a signal from the speaker has a routed path to this vantage, the same path its audio would take. The row reaches a vantage at exactly the delay the transmission's audio does, so the instant a transmission begins here is the same whichever of the two is read.

Rows are sent when a keying begins, again at most once a second of game time while it continues (so a connection that subscribes partway through learns of it), and once when it ends. Nothing is replayed to a connection that subscribes after a row reached it.

Detection only. A transmission's audio on CommcastTransmissionRow.topic is addressed to the members of its group only, and this row grants no access to it: a group is joined by invitation, never by a vantage adding itself, whatever it can detect.

comms.commandCentre

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

The comms.commandCentre payload: which command centre the active route ends at as it stands now, so a client can show its own stats against the right name instead of assuming KSC. It is where comms.path's last hop ends: the receiving centre itself, or, for the home centre, whichever ground station the signal reaches first. Shares its id and kind scheme with CommandCentreEntry (the commandCentre.roster entries).

As with comms.path, each command centre is sent its own, made from what that centre has heard.

Every field is null when the centre knows of no open path.

Payload CommsCommandCentre 4 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
id optional string | null

Stable centre key, same scheme as CommandCentreEntry.id: "ground:<name>" or "vessel:<guid>". Null when no remote centre resolved.
displayName optional string | null

The centre's human-facing name. Null when no remote centre resolved.
kind optional string | null

GroundStation or CrewedVessel, as CommandCentreEntry.kind spells them. Null when no remote centre resolved.
bodyIndex optional number | null

Index into trackingStation.bodies of the body this centre sits on. Null when unknown, not surface-anchored, or the centre is a moving vessel.

comms.contacts

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 1000 s of game time

One command centre's contact plan: for each pair of nodes that could hold a link (a ground station and a craft, or two craft), the windows over the coming hours when that centre predicts nothing blocks it and it is within reach.

A prediction, and the receiving centre's own. Every craft is reckoned forward from the last orbit that centre has heard it report, so the plan holds nothing the centre could not know: a distant craft's burn moves the plan one signal delay after it happened, and a craft the centre has never heard of is not in it. Two centres can hold different plans at the same moment, and each session is sent only the plan of the centre it sits at.

The live link the game reports always decides what actually gets through; this says when that link is expected to exist. A pair absent from CommsContacts.pairs was not predicted at all, which is different from a pair listed with no windows: that one is predicted never to be in contact before its CommsContactPair.horizonUt.

Payload CommsContacts 2 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
horizonUt number ut

The universal time the plan reaches to; nothing is predicted past it.
pairs CommsContactPair[]

Every pair predicted, each with its windows.

comms.degrade

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

The comms.degrade payload: how degraded the active vessel's link home is right now, on one fixed scale, as the comms backend in force grades it.

CommsDegrade.level runs from 0, nothing wrong, to 1, nothing usable getting through. It is absent when nothing graded the link, and absent is a third case rather than a low one: "nobody rated this" and "this link is perfect" are opposite instructions to anything choosing a quality, so branch on the absence rather than defaulting it to a number.

Read this rather than deriving a quality from comms.signal. That field is 0..1 too, and it is a different quantity on a stock install than on a RealAntennas one: a range fraction against an antenna curve versus spare room on a data-rate ladder. Nothing on the wire distinguishes them, so 1 - strength is two different quality curves on two saves. This channel names its rule, so a consumer acting on the number can see which grading produced it.

Each command centre is sent its own, with comms.signal and from the same reading of the vessel's radio. A rating is of the vessel's whole path at one instant, so it reaches a centre no sooner than light leaving the farthest node on that path could. Absent until the first reading arrives. Through a blackout it keeps its last value; the disconnect itself reaches a client on comms.link.

Payload CommsDegrade 3 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
modelId string

The grading rule's id; "unknown" when nothing graded the link.
modelName string

The grading rule's display name, so a surface can say which grading is in play.
level optional number | null ratio

The rating: 0 pristine, 1 unusable, absent when unrated. Never outside that range, and never a NaN: an arithmetic that overshot is clamped to the end it overshot, and one that failed to resolve arrives absent.

comms.delay

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

The comms.delay payload: the one-way signal delay to the active vessel, gated by the comms.signalDelay.enabled setting. CommsDelay.oneWaySeconds tells two different "no delay" cases apart by value:

  • null: no measurable CommsPath (no path home, or incomplete hop geometry). There is nothing to measure, so nothing is reported. CommsDelay.source is 0 (None).
  • 0: the delay feature is disabled (comms.signalDelay.enabled = false). A genuine "zero delay applied", not an absence. CommsDelay.source is also 0 (None) here: the two cases share the same Source and are told apart only by whether the value is null.
  • a real number: CommsDelay.source is 1 (SignalDelay), a signal delay computed over the hop geometry of the comms model in use.

One zero names its own reason instead of sharing 0 (None): 2 (NoCommsModel), which is what tells a client that a board showing no path and no relay graph is a save with the CommNet difficulty option off, not a craft in a permanent blackout: the blackout reports null here and connected:false on CommsLink, and this reports 0 and connected:true.

Each command centre is sent its own, and no other centre's. It is the signal delay of the active vessel's path that centre is sent on comms.path, so the two always agree. Where the game routes the vessel's samples to the centre (at home, the vessel's own path to the ground), that path is the game's route and this is the delay the samples arrive by. Wherever the game states no route, it is the path the centre's own plan has, worked out from what the centre has heard of each craft, so the figure moves only once the news that moves it has reached the centre. A zero that is a setting (delay switched off, or a save with no comms network) is sent at once.

Payload CommsDelay 3 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
oneWaySeconds optional number | null s

The one-way signal delay to the command centre, in seconds. Null when nothing is measurable, 0 for a measured or applied zero; this type's summary says which case is which.

Reckoning. Between samples the value is carried forward by re-measuring only the route's first hop, the one with the craft on one end: (route - firstHop + |craft - peer|) / c. The other hops join ground stations and relays that barely move against each other in that time, so their lengths are kept as measured. The craft is propagated on @vessel.orbit, and its peer is placed from @commandCentre.roster, whose body-fixed latitude and longitude need the rotation phase on @trackingStation.bodies.

A first hop that ends at a relay places the relay from its entry on @trackingStation.catalog: the orbit the command centre last heard for it, about the body whose gravitational parameter @trackingStation.bodies carries.

CommsDelay.source is an input because two of its members are a zero that does not mean "no distance": delay switched off, or a save with no comms network. Neither changes as the craft moves, so only 1 (SignalDelay) is carried forward.
source CommsDelaySource

Why CommsDelay.oneWaySeconds has the value it has; see CommsDelaySource.
meta PayloadMeta

The payload's provenance ("vessel:<guid>" or "game").

comms.journey

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

Journey reports for this vantage's commands in the current timeline: where each was held, sent on, stopped or run, as reports from those nodes arrive back here.

Every report has already travelled from the node that made it to this centre, at light speed and through any holds of its own, so a report arrives on this topic when this centre could first know it. Order a command's events by CommsJourneyEvent.atUt, not by arrival: two reports from different nodes travel different routes. A terminal event is never undone by an earlier one arriving late.

A report made here, by this centre, says only what this centre could know. It reports a command held while its own plan says the way is shut, and sent on when its plan says the way is open, whatever the far end is doing; and it reports a command that went unanswered only once twice the signal delay it expected has passed.

Each session receives only its own vantage's events.

Payload CommsJourney 2 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
epoch number count

The timeline these events belong to; events from an earlier timeline are dropped.
events CommsJourneyEvent[]

Every event received so far in this timeline, oldest arrival first, up to a bounded number.

comms.nextLoss

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 1000 s of game time

When the active craft is next predicted to drop out of contact with one command centre, on comms.nextLoss: the first moment its contact plan has no open route between the two, relays included.

A prediction, and the receiving centre's own, made over the comms.contacts plan that centre holds. A craft held in contact by one relay after another stays in contact across a handover, so this is the end of the whole route and never the end of one window. The live link the game reports decides what actually gets through.

Each session is sent only the figure of the centre it sits at.

Payload CommsNextLoss 4 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
ut optional number | null ut

The universal time the plan first has no open route between the centre and the active craft, or null when none is predicted: see CommsNextLoss.basis for which.
basis string

What CommsNextLoss.ut rests on. One of predicted-loss (the plan closes the last open route at CommsNextLoss.ut), no-loss-in-window (in contact through CommsNextLoss.coveredToUt), out-of-contact (no route is open now; the craft's trackingStation.catalog entry says when it is expected back), not-planned (the centre holds no plan that includes the craft) or no-craft (there is no active craft).
coveredToUt number ut

The last universal time the plan reaches. A null CommsNextLoss.ut with no-loss-in-window means no loss before it.
lowConfidence boolean

True while an end of the route was last heard of with its orbit still changing, so the instant is a rough guide until its next report.

comms.path

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

The comms.path payload: the route the active vessel's samples take to the receiving command centre. Ordered hops from the active vessel to the receiving centre itself, or, for the home centre, to whichever ground station the signal reaches first. An empty CommsPath.hops means the centre knows of no path that is open all the way now, which includes a path that would have the signal wait at a relay (comms.route says where it would wait).

Each command centre is sent its own, and no other centre's. Where the game routes the vessel's samples to the centre (at home, the vessel's own path to the ground), the hops are that route, the one comms.delay and the arrival of every sample are timed over. Where the game states no route, they are worked out from that centre's contact plan, which is made of what the centre has heard of each craft, so a hop changes here only once the news of it has reached the centre: a relay that drops out is still on the path until its silence has crossed to you. Predictions (comms.route, held commands, cancel deadlines) are always the plan's. Nothing is sent until the centre has a contact plan or a game route, so the topic is absent, not empty, for the first moments of a session.

The route sent here is the active route: the route this command centre has the active vessel on. The other comms topics use the term in this sense.

Not reckonable: a route changes in steps (a relay drops below the horizon and the whole chain re-solves to different hops), and every reckoning basis moves a continuous quantity.

Payload CommsPath 1 field
FieldTypeUnitDescription
hops CommsHop[]

The hops in order, the first starting at the active vessel and the last ending at the receiving centre, or at a ground station for the home centre. Empty when the centre knows of no open path, never null.

comms.route

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 1000 s of game time

The route a message sent now would take between one command centre and the active craft, in both directions, predicted from that centre's own contact plan: the earliest arrival over every relay, waiting at a node for its next window where that arrives sooner.

A prediction, and the receiving centre's own: it is planned over the comms.contacts plan that centre holds, so it knows of nothing the centre has not heard. The live link the game reports decides what actually gets through.

Every ground station is the home centre's own antenna. Its rows run through whichever station reaches the craft first, as its comms.path does, and a wait for a station's window is a wait at the home centre itself. Every other centre is quoted its own antenna only.

Each session is sent only the rows of the centre it sits at, the two between that centre and the active craft.

Telemetry

comms.signal

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

The comms.signal payload: the active vessel's own reading of its link, from the comms backend in use (stock CommNet, or a replacement an Uplink provides). A strength from 0 to 1 whose meaning depends on the backend: stock CommNet reports KSP's own signal strength for the path, which falls off smoothly towards the range edge of each link and is multiplied across relays, RealAntennas how far up its data-rate ladder the path's links close. CommsSignal.quantity says which, so a client names the figure correctly and does not compare two that are different quantities.

Each command centre is sent its own, the newest reading to have reached it. A reading is of the vessel's whole path at one instant, so it reaches a centre no sooner than light leaving the farthest node on that path at that instant could: it never tells a centre what a relay's link is doing before the relay's own light has. Absent until the first reading arrives. The path it was measured over is the game's, which is not always the active route on comms.path.

A save with the stock CommNet difficulty option off models no link budget at all, so CommsSignal.strength is null there and CommsSignal.quantity is 3 (NoModel).

Payload CommsSignal 5 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
strength optional number | null ratio

Link strength from 0 to 1, in the backend's own terms (see this type's summary), so compare values only within one install. Null when no link state could be read, and where no link budget is modelled.
quantity SignalQuantity

Which quantity CommsSignal.strength is: KSP's signal strength for the path, a position on the data-rate ladder, or a stand-in where no link is modelled. A strength worked out for a path carries the quantity its hops were stated in, and 0 (Unknown) where they disagree.
modelled boolean

Whether CommsSignal.strength is worked out and not measured. A command centre is sent the strength of the active route. Where the active vessel's radio last reported on the active route itself, the reported strength is sent and this is false. Where it reported on another route, or has not reported, the strength is what the backend works out for the active route from what the centre has heard, and this is true. Where nothing can be worked out either, see CommsSignal.otherPath.
otherPath boolean

Whether CommsSignal.strength was measured on a route other than the active route. The active vessel's radio reports the strength of whatever route the game has it on. Where that is not the active route and the comms backend can work nothing out for the active route, the reported strength is still sent, with this set, so it is never read as the active route's own. False whenever CommsSignal.modelled is true, and false for a centre that has no active route yet, which is sent the reported strength as it is.
measuredPath optional CommsMeasuredPath | null

The route CommsSignal.strength was measured on, where that is not the active route. Set whenever CommsSignal.otherPath is true and null otherwise, so a client can name the route the figure belongs to beside the mark that says it is of another path. It is as old as the strength beside it, and names each vessel as the receiving centre last heard it named.

crash.lastCrash

Delivery Every value, in orderDelay After signal delaySamples One per eventRepeats every 3600 s of game time

The last notable crash of the current save. A subscriber that joins late still receives the most recent record, since every value is delivered, in order. Every field is captured from the crashed vessel at the moment of the crash.

It is the crashed craft's own report, so it reaches each command centre at the signal delay of that craft's link as of its last contact, whichever craft is being flown. A centre that had no route to the craft when it crashed is sent nothing; if it saw the craft go, its trackingStation.catalog lists the end, with when and how it learned of it, and nothing of the crew or the parts.

deployed 1 telemetry

Deployed Breaking Ground bases

Telemetry 1

Telemetry

deployed.bases

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

One entry in the deployed.bases Topic payload: a Breaking Ground deployed-science experiment, a science instrument set down on the surface. The Topic payload is a bare array (DeployedEntry[]) or null when Breaking Ground is not installed and no loaded vessel carries a deployed experiment.

Unlike the science.* channels, deployed.bases covers the whole save, not just the active vessel: a deployed cluster is its own ground vessel, so an entry normally describes a vessel other than the active one, named by DeployedEntry.vesselName. An experiment on a vessel that is not loaded is read from Breaking Ground's cluster registry and carries no power or connection sentence. One that belongs to no cluster is listed only while its vessel is loaded.

Every field is nullable, and is null whenever the raw value is absent or could not be read.

Payload DeployedEntry[] 17 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
vesselName optional string | null

Name of the vessel carrying the experiment (KSP's Vessel.vesselName). A deployed cluster is its own vessel, so this is normally not the active vessel's name.
partName optional string | null

Display title of the experiment part (the part's partInfo.title, or its internal name when that is missing).
body optional string | null

Name of the body the carrying vessel orbits or sits on (its orbit's reference body). null when the vessel has no orbit.
situation optional string | null

The carrying vessel's situation, KSP's Vessel.situation enum name (for example LANDED).
biome optional string | null

Biome at the carrying vessel's current position on DeployedEntry.body. null when the body has no biome map.
experimentId optional string | null

The experiment's id (KSP's ModuleGroundExperiment.experimentId).
scienceCompletedPercentage optional number | null %

How far the experiment has progressed, in percent (KSP's ModuleGroundExperiment.ScienceCompletedPercentage).
scienceTransmittedPercentage optional number | null %

How much of the experiment's science has been transmitted, in percent (KSP's ModuleGroundExperiment.ScienceTransmittedPercentage).
scienceValue optional number | null science

The science value KSP reports for the experiment (ModuleGroundExperiment.ScienceValue).
scienceLimit optional number | null science

The experiment's science limit as KSP reports it (ModuleGroundExperiment.ScienceLimit). Compare against DeployedEntry.scienceValue.
powerState optional string | null

ModuleGroundSciencePart.PowerState verbatim: KSP's own words for the power state, for display. Do not branch on this.

It is not an enum name, it is localised prose. The module assigns it from Localizer in UpdateModuleUI(), so the value is in whatever language the player runs KSP in, and it is only written when the part action window refreshes, so it can be a held value. DeployedEntry.power is the field to read.
connectionState optional string | null

ModuleGroundSciencePart.ConnectionState verbatim, for display. Localised prose on the same terms as DeployedEntry.powerState; read DeployedEntry.controllerConnected instead.
power optional DeployedPowerState | null

The cluster's power state, derived from the same facts UpdateModuleUI() itself branches on (DeployedScienceCluster.IsPowered and .ControllerPartEnabled, the module's Enabled and DeployedOnGround) rather than parsed out of the sentence that method writes. This is the field to branch on, not DeployedEntry.powerState.

null when the cluster could not be read at all, which is a third state and must not be read as either powered or unpowered.
controllerConnected optional boolean | null

Whether the experiment is attached to a controller cluster at all, the fact behind DeployedEntry.connectionState's "Connected"/"Not Connected". null when it could not be determined.
powerAvailable optional number | null count

Power units the cluster's parts produce (DeployedScienceCluster.PowerAvailable), against DeployedEntry.powerRequired. Breaking Ground's own integral power scale summed over the cluster's parts: not electric charge, and not a rate. Available at or above required is what makes the cluster powered.

null when the cluster could not be read, on the same terms as DeployedEntry.power. Zero is a real reading a live cluster holds while its panels are dark, so it must not stand in for absence.
powerRequired optional number | null count

Power units the cluster's parts require (DeployedScienceCluster.PowerRequired). Same scale and same null rule as DeployedEntry.powerAvailable, the demand side of the balance.
deployedOnGround optional boolean | null

Whether the experiment part is deployed on the ground (KSP's ModuleGroundSciencePart.DeployedOnGround).

dv 2 telemetry

Delta-v per stage and in total for the active vessel

Telemetry 2

Telemetry

dv.stages

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

One ΔV-producing stage of the active vessel, from the game's own stage simulation: the same numbers the in-game ΔV app shows, with atmosphere, ISP, crossfeed and staging all handled by the game. Only the stages that actually produce ΔV appear, the same set the in-game app lists rather than the raw stage list, so stage numbers can be sparse.

The dv.stages payload is a plain array of these, or null, never a wrapper object. The whole array is null when the stock simulation is not ready or there is no active vessel.

Every field is nullable, and null is never a sentinel: a field is null whenever the raw value is absent or non-finite, so a stage the simulation reports as NaN or Infinity reaches you as null rather than as a number you would have to test.

Carries no meta of its own: provenance rides the envelope (stream-data.Meta), never the payload body.

flight.ended

Delivery Every value, in orderDelay After signal delaySamples One per eventRepeats every 3600 s of game time

An event that is always delivered, in the order it happened, and held back by the signal delay like any value about a craft, sent once per flight when it stops being trackable: recovered, crashed, destroyed or reverted. It shares the delay class of crash.lastCrash and recovery.lastSummary, so an end that a rewind discards before its signal delay has elapsed is never revealed.

A crash or a destruction is the lost craft's own report: it reaches each command centre at the signal delay of that craft's link as of its last contact, whichever craft is being flown, and a centre that had no route to it is sent nothing. A centre that saw the craft go has the end in its trackingStation.catalog.

Debris, flags and vessels of unknown type never end a flight.

The vessel's display name at the end of the flight.

Why the flight ended. When a crash and a destruction are both detected for one loss, the first detected wins.

Telemetry

flight.started

Delivery Every value, in orderDelay After signal delaySamples One per eventRepeats every 3600 s of game time

An event that is always delivered, in the order it happened, and held back by the signal delay like any value about a craft, sent when a new flight begins. A flight is new when its vessel id has not been started before in this game session (a launch, or a first switch onto a vessel), and every vessel active just after a revert or a quickload starts a new flight, even one with the same id.

A client that subscribes while a flight is already open receives that flight's flight.started, carrying its original start FlightStarted.ut. A repeat with an unchanged FlightStarted.ut is the same flight announced again; a new FlightStarted.ut for the same vessel id is a new flight after a rewind.

flightId string

KSP's Vessel.id GUID of the vessel flying this flight, as a string.
vesselName string

The vessel's display name when the flight was announced.
ut number ut

Universal time this flight began: when the vessel was first observed active, or the revert-target UT for a flight started by a rewind.

Delivery Every value, in orderDelay After signal delaySamples One per eventRepeats every 3600 s of game time

An event that is always delivered, in the order it happened, and held back by the signal delay like any value about a craft, sent whenever the active vessel changes after the first observation of the session (docking, undocking, a tracking-station reselect). Which expansions are installed

game.dlc

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay LiveSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

Which KSP expansions ("DLC") are installed. A fact about the install, independent of scene, so a widget can tell "the player has no DLC" from "the DLC is present but nothing is deployed yet" (deployed science, for instance, needs Breaking Ground).
