Telemetry

isru.drills

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

One drill (resource harvester) on the active vessel. The field set is what every ISRU model shares, which is exactly what stock ISRU has: resource, abundance, rate, deploy and running, plus the two identification fields. Anything one provider knows and another does not goes in IsruDrillEntry.extensions.

The isru.drills payload is an array of these. An empty array means the vessel has no drills, never that ISRU is not tracked.

Payload IsruDrillEntry[] 8 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
partId optional string | null

The part's flight id, as a string: the same join key vessel.parts and parts.power use.
partTitle optional string | null

Part.partInfo.title, for display without a vessel.parts join.
resource optional string | null

Resource this drill extracts (e.g. "Ore"). Free text, not a closed enum: whatever the running install's configs and profiles name, as with every resource name in this contract.
deployed optional boolean | null

Drill head deployed. Null for a harvester with no deploy animation, e.g. some asteroid drills.
running optional boolean | null

Actively extracting this tick.
abundance optional number | null ratio

Local abundance of IsruDrillEntry.resource at the drill's current position, 0..1. Stock reads the same resource map the part's right-click menu does. A mod that samples its own abundance reports that instead, and for asteroid or comet mining the remaining-mass ratio of the source rock lands here: the same 0..1 shape from a different source. Null when the backend has no abundance concept for this harvest type.
rate optional number | null units/s

Effective current extraction rate, already abundance- and efficiency-adjusted rather than the static config rate, so it matches what the part's own readout shows. Zero rather than null when IsruDrillEntry.running is false: the drill genuinely extracts nothing, which is a number, not an absence.
extensions optional map of any | null

Per-drill facts the ISRU mod in use reports beyond this shape, keyed by that mod's name. Null for the vanilla backend, which has nothing stock does not already say. A blocking-reason string, an EC draw, an asteroid's remaining mass: all of those belong here rather than as nullable members above.

Commands 7

Command

ksp.launch

Takes effect when sent

Load a saved craft onto a launch site. The craft is identified by LaunchArgs.shipName plus the LaunchArgs.facility it was saved from ("VAB" or "SPH", case-insensitive); Gonogo finds the .craft file itself, so a client never sends a file path. An empty ship name fails with "notFound" and an unrecognised facility with "range", before the game is ever touched.

LaunchArgs.crew is an array of kerbal names (empty to launch unmanned), each assigned to a free craft seat.

Arguments LaunchArgs 4 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
shipName string

The saved craft's name: its .craft file name without the extension, under the save's Ships/VAB or Ships/SPH folder. No such file fails with "notFound".
facility string

"VAB" or "SPH" (case-insensitive). Any other value yields CommandResult.errorCode "range".
site string

The KSP launch site name to launch from, "LaunchPad" by default. Refused unless the sending command centre is in the same planetary system (a planet and its moons) as the site.
crew string[]

Kerbal names to seat, in order. Empty to launch unmanned.

missions 1 telemetry

The active Making History mission

Telemetry 1

Telemetry

missions.active

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delayHeld at homeSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game timeEmpty is an answer

The Making History mission that is running, or has just ended, in the current game. The whole payload is null when there is no mission game, when no mission has been set up, or when the expansion is not installed. The game.dlc Topic (GameDlc) says only whether the expansion is installed; with it installed, a null payload is one of the other two, and nothing on the stream says which. A null payload reaches a widget as a reading whose state is "absent" and which carries no value, so test the state rather than the value for null.

A mission that has ended stays in the payload with MissionStatus.finished true until the game leaves the mission, so a client can show the outcome.

Every field except MissionStatus.objectives is null whenever the raw value is absent or could not be read. Score fields are meaningful only when MissionStatus.scoreEnabled is true: a mission author can switch scoring off.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
name optional string | null

The mission's title, localised.
phase optional string | null

The title of the mission's active node, the step of the mission's flow chart the mission is on now. null when it has no active node.
started optional boolean | null

Whether the mission has started.
finished optional boolean | null

Whether the mission has ended, in success or failure.
succeeded optional boolean | null

Whether the mission ended in success. Meaningful once MissionStatus.finished is true.
scoreEnabled optional boolean | null

Whether the mission awards a score at all.
score optional number | null count

The score earned so far.
maxScore optional number | null count

The most score the mission can award.
objectives MissionObjectiveEntry[]

The mission's objectives in the order its flow chart leads through them. A node that nothing in the flow chart leads to is left out. Empty when it has none.

Telemetry

recovery.lastSummary

Delivery Every value, in orderDelay After signal delaySamples One per eventRepeats every 3600 s of game time

The payload for the recovery.lastSummary channel: the most recent vessel recovery in the current save, as KSP's mission recovery dialog reports it. Every value is delivered, in order, so a late subscriber is sent the last recovery. The recovery-side counterpart of CrashReport.

Published only for a real craft: recovering debris, a flag or a vessel of unknown type publishes nothing. The four breakdown lists can be empty while the totals are present, if KSP's dialog could not be read for them.

A figure the save cannot award is null, never 0: funds and science are null in a Sandbox save (and funds in a Science save). A Sandbox recovery still produces a record, with the craft, where it came down, its parts and its crew, and nothing awarded.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
capturedAtUT number ut

When the recovery was captured, in UT seconds.
vesselName string

The recovered vessel's name, as KSP holds it (ProtoVessel.vesselName).
recoveryLocation string

Where the vessel came down: KSP's own recovery-location string (e.g. "KSC", "Water").
recoveryFactor string

KSP's own recovery-factor display string (e.g. "100%"), the payout multiplier for landing precision.
scienceEarned optional number | null science

Science this recovery earned, as KSP's recovery dialog totals it. Null in a save with no science (Sandbox).
totalScience optional number | null science

The career's science balance as the recovery dialog reports it. Null in a save with no science (Sandbox).
fundsEarned optional number | null funds

Funds this recovery earned, after the recovery factor and any strategy modifiers KSP applies to a recovery. Null in a save with no funds (Science or Sandbox).
totalFunds optional number | null funds

The career's funds balance as the recovery dialog reports it. Null in a save with no funds (Science or Sandbox).
reputationEarned optional number | null rep

Reputation this recovery earned, after any strategy modifiers KSP applies. Null in a save with no reputation (Science or Sandbox), where RecoveryReport.displayReputation is false.
totalReputation optional number | null rep

The career's reputation as the recovery dialog reports it. Null in a save with no reputation (Science or Sandbox), where RecoveryReport.displayReputation is false.
displayReputation boolean

Whether reputation applies to this save: false in Science and Sandbox, where the reputation fields carry nothing meaningful.
scienceBreakdown RecoveryScienceEntry[]

Each science subject recovered, in the order KSP's dialog lists them. Empty when nothing was recovered or the dialog could not be read.
partBreakdown RecoveryPartEntry[]

Each group of recovered parts, in the order KSP's dialog lists them. Empty when the dialog could not be read.
resourceBreakdown RecoveryResourceEntry[]

Each recovered resource, in the order KSP's dialog lists them. Empty when there were none or the dialog could not be read.
crewBreakdown RecoveryCrewEntry[]

Each crew member aboard at recovery. Empty for an uncrewed vessel or when the dialog could not be read.

robotics 2 telemetry, 10 commands

Robotic rotors, hinges and pistons

Telemetry 2

Telemetry

robotics.available

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

A single object (or null when there is no active vessel) whose one field states whether the active vessel carries any Breaking Ground robotic servo. It is its own Topic because the robotics.servos array is null both when the vessel has no robotic parts and when there is no vessel, and a widget needs to tell "no robotics on this craft" from "nothing to show".

Not the same as the Breaking Ground DLC-presence fact (deployed.available): this reflects parts on this vessel, so it is delayed by signal delay, whereas DLC presence is known on the ground at once.

RoboticsAvailability.available is three-state. null means the craft could not be surveyed: a recording that does not carry this field, or a live read where one part could not be read, since "no robotic parts" is a claim about every part. false is the definite "this craft carries none". A client that treats null as false tells the operator there are no robotic parts on a craft that may be full of them.

Payload RoboticsAvailability 1 field
FieldTypeUnitDescription
available optional boolean | null

True when the vessel carries at least one robotic servo, false when it definitely carries none, null when it could not be surveyed.

Telemetry

robotics.servos

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

One entry in the robotics.servos Topic payload, a single Breaking Ground robotic servo on the active vessel. The payload is a bare array of these, or null when there is no active vessel or it carries no servo; read robotics.available to tell those two apart.

ServoEntry.type is the servo kind as a plain string, not an enum. The kinds are "rotor", "hinge", "rotationServo" and "piston", plus "servo" for a servo of a kind not recognised (a part pack's own, or one a later KSP adds), which carries only the readings every servo has.

Open set. The kinds follow KSP's own BaseServo types, so more may appear. Switch on the kinds you can draw and ignore the rest.

Fields that belong to one kind are null on every other kind: angles on hinges and rotation servos, extensions on pistons, and the rpm, output, brake, direction and torque fields on rotors.

Payload ServoEntry[] 19 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
partName optional string | null

The part's display title (KSP's Part.partInfo.title), or its internal name when it has no part info.
partId optional string | null

The part's Part.flightID as a string: unique per part for the life of the flight, so it tells apart symmetric servos that share a name. Null when the part has no flight id yet.
type optional string | null

The servo kind: "rotor", "hinge", "rotationServo", "piston", or "servo" for a kind not recognised. See this type's summary.
servoIsLocked optional boolean | null

True when the servo is locked in place (KSP's BaseServo.servoIsLocked).
servoIsMotorized optional boolean | null

True when the servo has a motor (KSP's BaseServo.servoIsMotorized).
servoMotorIsEngaged optional boolean | null

True when the servo's motor is engaged (KSP's BaseServo.servoMotorIsEngaged).
servoMotorLimit optional number | null %

The motor's torque limit as a percentage (KSP's BaseServo.servoMotorLimit). On a rotor it is a percentage of ServoEntry.maxTorque.
motorState optional string | null

The motor's state text as KSP displays it (BaseServo.motorState). Free text, not a fixed vocabulary.
currentAngle optional number | null °

Current angle in degrees. Hinges and rotation servos only.
targetAngle optional number | null °

Angle the servo is driving to, in degrees. Hinges and rotation servos only.
traverseVelocity optional number | null

KSP's traverseVelocity setting for hinges, rotation servos and pistons. Its unit follows the kind (KSP drives angles for the first two and an extension for a piston), so no single unit is declared.
currentRPM optional number | null rpm

The rotor's current speed in revolutions per minute. Rotors only.
rpmLimit optional number | null rpm

The rotor's rpm limit setting. Rotors only.
normalizedOutput optional number | null ratio

The rotor's normalised output (KSP's ModuleRoboticServoRotor.normalizedOutput). Rotors only.
brakePercentage optional number | null %

The rotor's brake setting as a percentage (KSP's brakePercentage). Rotors only.
currentExtension optional number | null m

The piston's current extension in metres. Pistons only.
targetExtension optional number | null m

The extension the piston is driving to, in metres. Pistons only.
counterClockwise optional boolean | null

Rotor spin direction (rotor entries only, null for every other kind). KSP's ModuleRoboticServoRotor.rotateCounterClockwise: true means the rotor spins counter-clockwise.
maxTorque optional number | null kN

Rotor torque ceiling in kN (rotor entries only, null for every other kind). KSP's ModuleRoboticServoRotor.maxTorque: the scale ServoEntry.servoMotorLimit (a percentage) is a fraction of.

kN is the unit KSP's editor shows for it, although the value acts as a torque on the rotor's joint.

science 6 telemetry, 2 commands

Experiments, the science archive and transmission

Telemetry 6

Telemetry

science.archive

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delayHeld at homeSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

One entry in the science.archive Topic payload: a single subject out of the whole-career R&D archive (ResearchAndDevelopment.GetSubjects()). That is every subject the career has ever collected or recovered, across every mission and every body, not scoped to the active vessel.

The Topic payload is a bare array (ArchiveEntry[]), or null when the save has no R&D to walk (Sandbox mode). A save with R&D but nothing collected yet emits an empty array, so an empty array and null mean different things here.

Distinct from ExperimentBreakdownEntry: that one rolls up the active vessel's currently stored results and is null with no vessel flying; this one is career-wide and streams at the Space Center with nothing flying at all.

Payload ArchiveEntry[] 11 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
subjectId optional string | null

The subject's id (KSP's ScienceSubject.id, in the form experimentId@BodySituationBiome), unique within the array. Joins to ExperimentEntry.subjectId and ExperimentBreakdownEntry.subjectId.
experimentId optional string | null

The experiment id: the part of ArchiveEntry.subjectId before the @.
experimentTitle optional string | null

The experiment's display title from R&D. Falls back to ArchiveEntry.experimentId when the experiment is no longer defined (for example a modded experiment that has been uninstalled).
body optional string | null

The body the subject belongs to, parsed from ArchiveEntry.subjectId by KSP's ScienceUtil.GetExperimentBodyName.
situation optional string | null

The situation part of ArchiveEntry.subjectId (a KSP ExperimentSituations name such as SrfLanded).
biome optional string | null

The biome part of ArchiveEntry.subjectId.
title optional string | null

The subject's display title (KSP's ScienceSubject.title).
science optional number | null science

Science banked for this subject so far.
scienceCap optional number | null science

Max science this subject can ever yield.
remainingPotential optional number | null science

Absolute science still recoverable from this subject (scienceCap - science).
subjectValue optional number | null 1

Region multiplier KSP applies to this subject's yield.

Telemetry

science.experimentBreakdown

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

One entry in the science.experimentBreakdown Topic payload: a per-subject rollup of the stored science results that science.experiments lists one row per result. One row per distinct subject id: several stored results for the same subject (for example two crew reports from the same biome) collapse into one entry with ExperimentBreakdownEntry.dataMits summed across them.

The Topic payload is a bare array (ExperimentBreakdownEntry[]) or null, never a wrapper object. The whole array is null when there is no active vessel or the vessel holds no stored science data; there is no separate empty-array state. Every field is nullable, and is null whenever the raw value is absent or non-finite.

ExperimentBreakdownEntry.biome and ExperimentBreakdownEntry.situation are parsed from the subject id by KSP's ScienceUtil.GetExperimentFieldsFromScienceID, not from the vessel's current position, so a subject collected earlier in the flight keeps its own biome and situation.

Payload ExperimentBreakdownEntry[] 8 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
subjectId optional string | null

The science subject id this row rolls up (KSP's ScienceData.subjectID), unique within the array. Joins to ExperimentEntry.subjectId and ArchiveEntry.subjectId.
biome optional string | null

The biome part of ExperimentBreakdownEntry.subjectId: where the subject was collected, not where the vessel is now.
situation optional string | null

The situation part of ExperimentBreakdownEntry.subjectId (a KSP ExperimentSituations name such as SrfLanded): the situation the subject was collected in, not the vessel's current one.
expTitle optional string | null

Display title of the first stored result seen for this subject (KSP's ScienceData.title).
dataMits optional number | null Mit

Summed ScienceData.dataAmount (mits) across every stored result for this subject.
remainingPotential optional number | null science

Absolute science still recoverable from this subject (scienceCap - science from R&D). 0 in Sandbox (no R&D) and when R&D holds no subject with this id.
valueModel optional string | null

Which value model produced ExperimentBreakdownEntry.remainingPotential, and which unit ExperimentBreakdownEntry.dataMits is really in. See ScienceValueModels.

Stock's rollup is a snapshot: one summed data figure and one "how much is left". A provider with a full per-subject ledger (collected vs retrieved, in-flight split, times completed) projects it down to those two and carries the ledger in ExperimentBreakdownEntry.extensions: stock's pair is a lossy view of the richer set, never the other way round.
extensions optional map of any | null

The provider-namespaced extension bag, per-subject-rollup half. Same mechanism and same rule as ExperimentEntry.extensions.

science.experiments

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

One entry in the science.experiments Topic payload: a single stored science result on the active vessel, held either by the science module that collected it or by a container part. The channel payload is a bare array of these (ExperimentEntry[]) or null, never a wrapper object. The whole array is null when there is no active vessel or the vessel holds no stored science data; there is no separate empty-array state.

One row per stored ScienceData: a module that holds no data produces no row (see InstrumentEntry for one row per module). Every field is nullable, and is null whenever the raw value is absent or non-finite.

Payload ExperimentEntry[] 15 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
partName optional string | null

Display title of the part holding the result (the part's partInfo.title, or its internal name when that is missing).
location optional string | null

"experiment" (still held by the science module that collected it) or "container" (already collected into an onboard science container). KSP keeps no "already transmitted" flag on a result, so this is the closest available "stored vs not yet collected" signal.
experimentId optional string | null

The collecting module's experiment id (KSP's ModuleScienceExperiment.experimentID, for example crewReport). null on a "container" row, where the result no longer sits in its experiment module.
subjectId optional string | null

The science subject this result was recorded against (KSP's ScienceData.subjectID), the join key into ExperimentBreakdownEntry.subjectId and ArchiveEntry.subjectId.
title optional string | null

The result's display title (KSP's ScienceData.title).
dataAmount optional number | null Mit

Size of the stored result in mits (KSP's ScienceData.dataAmount). null under a ExperimentEntry.valueModel whose data is not measured in mits.
scienceValueRatio optional number | null ratio

KSP's ScienceData.scienceValueRatio for this result. Its meaning depends on ExperimentEntry.valueModel: do not compare it across models.
baseTransmitValue optional number | null science

KSP's ScienceData.baseTransmitValue for this result. Its meaning depends on ExperimentEntry.valueModel.
transmitBonus optional number | null ratio

Transmit-value multiplier for this result (KSP's ScienceData.transmitBonus), a bounded ratio.
labValue optional number | null science

KSP's ScienceData.labValue for this result: its value to a Mobile Processing Lab. Its meaning depends on ExperimentEntry.valueModel.
deployed optional boolean | null

Whether the collecting experiment module is deployed (KSP's ModuleScienceExperiment.Deployed). null on a "container" row.
inoperable optional boolean | null

Whether the collecting experiment module is inoperable until reset (KSP's ModuleScienceExperiment.Inoperable). null on a "container" row.
situation optional string | null

The active vessel's current situation, KSP's Vessel.situation enum name (for example LANDED, ORBITING). It describes where the vessel is now, not where the result was collected; the collection situation is encoded in ExperimentEntry.subjectId.
valueModel optional string | null

Which value model produced ExperimentEntry.scienceValueRatio, ExperimentEntry.baseTransmitValue and ExperimentEntry.labValue, and which unit ExperimentEntry.dataAmount is really in. A token from ScienceValueModels, or one it does not list.

This is the one field on the payload that is not simply "what the game says". A provider whose data is not in mits leaves ExperimentEntry.dataAmount null rather than putting another unit's figure in a mits-typed field, and carries the real figure in its own ExperimentEntry.extensions namespace.
extensions optional map of any | null

Per-experiment facts the science mod in use reports beyond this shape, keyed by that mod's name.

Everything a richer science model knows that stock has no concept of belongs here: storage capacity, file-vs-sample, transmit rate, per-unit science rate. Absent from the payload when no provider filled it.

science.instruments

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

One entry in the science.instruments Topic payload: a single ModuleScienceExperiment on the active vessel, as an inventory and status row keyed by InstrumentEntry.partId (the part's flight id, a number the game assigns each part of a flight, written as a string).

Distinct from ExperimentEntry: science.experiments walks the same modules but yields one row per stored result (a module with no data produces no row), whereas science.instruments yields one row per module whether or not it holds data. It is the operability picture (deployed, inoperable, rerunnable, resettable, collectable) an operator needs to decide what to run next.

The Topic payload is a bare array (InstrumentEntry[]) or null when there is no active vessel or it carries no experiment module. Every field is nullable, and is null whenever the raw value is absent.

Payload InstrumentEntry[] 10 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
partId optional string | null

science.lab

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

One entry in the science.lab Topic payload: a Mobile Processing Lab (KSP's ModuleScienceLab) on the active vessel. The channel payload is a bare array (LabEntry[]) or null when there is no active vessel or it carries no lab. Every field is nullable, and is null whenever the raw value is absent or non-finite.

Payload LabEntry[] 13 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
partId optional string | null

The part's KSP flightID as a string: the stable join key for this lab, and what tells one lab from another across samples. null when the part has no flight id yet (KSP's unset value, 0).
partName optional string | null

Display title of the lab part (the part's partInfo.title, or its internal name when that is missing).
dataStored optional number | null Mit

Data currently stored in the lab for processing, in mits (KSP's ModuleScienceLab.dataStored). Compare against LabEntry.dataStorage.
dataStorage optional number | null Mit

The lab's data capacity in mits (KSP's ModuleScienceLab.dataStorage).
storedScience optional number | null science

Science the lab has generated and is holding, not yet transmitted (KSP's ModuleScienceLab.storedScience). While the lab is processing it grows at LabEntry.scienceRate up to LabEntry.scienceCap, so a model carries it forward from there; a lab that is not processing holds it exactly as observed.
scienceCap optional number | null science

The most science the lab holds: generation stops once LabEntry.storedScience reaches it (KSP's ModuleScienceConverter.scienceCap). null when the lab has no converter or it could not be read.
processingData optional boolean | null

Whether the lab is currently processing data (KSP's ModuleScienceLab.processingData).
statusText optional string | null

KSP's own status line for the lab (ModuleScienceLab.statusText), for display. Game-authored prose, so do not branch on it.
scientistCount optional number | null count

Number of crew with the Scientist trait aboard the lab part. 0 is a real reading: a lab with no scientist.
scienceRate optional number | null science/day

Science generated per game day, not per second, at the lab's current stored data (KSP's ModuleScienceConverter.CalculateScienceRate, which scales the per-tick rate to a full day). null when the lab has no converter or the rate could not be read.
isOperational optional boolean | null

Whether the lab can operate right now (KSP's ModuleScienceLab.IsOperational()).
valueModel optional string | null

Which value model produced LabEntry.scienceRate and LabEntry.storedScience, and which unit LabEntry.dataStored and LabEntry.dataStorage are really in. See ScienceValueModels.

A lab is not the same kind of thing under every model. Stock's is terminal: it turns stored data into science per game-day. A provider whose lab is an intermediate pipeline stage (analysing a sample into a transmissible file, which then still has to be sent) produces no science itself, leaves LabEntry.scienceRate null, and carries its own rate in LabEntry.extensions. This tag is what tells that null apart from an idle lab.
extensions optional map of any | null

The provider-namespaced extension bag, lab half. Same mechanism and same rule as ExperimentEntry.extensions.

Transmit a science experiment's data home.

Arguments ExperimentActionArgs

Result CommandResult & object 6 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
success boolean

Whether the command ran. False means the game refused it, and CommandResult.errorCode says why.
errorCode optional CommandErrorCode | null

Why it was refused, null on success. On the wire this is the root's id, so every client can classify it; a refinement's own id travels beside it as CommandResult.reason.
reason optional string | null

The id of the more specific refusal, when there is one, such as example.notManaging, a kind of careerModeRequired. Absent when the refusal is a root. An id this client does not know is still a refusal of kind CommandResult.errorCode.
breach optional LimitBreach | null

The numbers behind the refusal, when the refusal has any: the cap and the count, the tier and the top tier, the price and the balance. Null on success and on every refusal that is not a comparison.

CommandResult.errorCode says which refusal it is and this holds its numbers, as in "16 of 16 active crew".

The same LimitBreach shape a declared gate carries on GateVerdict.breach, so a refusal reads the same whether it came from a gate or from the command's own handler. Omitted from the wire when null.
detail optional string | null

The refusal in the game's own words, when the game had any: the member of ClearToSaveStatus it came back with, Strategies.Strategy.CanBeActivated(out string reason)'s reason, GameVariables.GetEVALockedReason's sentence, a PreFlightTests.IPreFlightTest's GetWarningTitle(), a [Description]-tagged state member's name. Null when the refusal had nothing to quote, and then omitted from the wire, never sent as an empty string.

The text is the game's own, so it is in the game's language.

Prose for a human, never parsed: CommandResult.errorCode is the machine-readable half. The same split, and the same field name, as GateVerdict.detail.
payload optional ScienceTransmission | null

The value the command returns; absent on a refusal.

settings 1 telemetry, 2 commands

The mod's own settings and those of other mods

Telemetry 1

Telemetry

settings.gonogo

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay LiveSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

Every setting the mod and its Uplinks declared, what each holds now, and whether the settings file on the KSP machine holds the same.

The whole model is on one Topic. A client draws a control per row from the row's own description, so a setting an Uplink adds needs no client code of its own.

It is never delayed by signal delay, the time a signal takes to cross between a craft and the command centre (the screen an operator sends commands from): a setting configures the system the operator is sitting at, not a craft.

This is where a client learns whether a save landed. The settings.save command (SaveSettingsArgs) can time out and still land, so read the outcome here, never from the command's reply.

Payload SettingsModel 3 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
rows SettingsRowState[]

Every declared setting, in declaration order: the mod's own first, then each Uplink's.
persistence SettingsPersistence

Whether the values here are the ones the settings file holds.
undeclared SettingsDeclarationFailure[]

Uplinks that are running but whose settings could not be declared this session. Their settings are at their defaults and are not listed in SettingsModel.rows; what the file holds for them is kept as it is.

settings.mod.write

Takes effect when sent

Arguments to settings.mod.write: change one of a host mod's own settings through its Uplink, at once.

Safe to send again: it sets the value named, so repeating one that already landed changes nothing.

Refused, with nothing changed, when the Uplink lists no such setting, when the setting is not writable, when the value is not one its kind can hold, or when the Uplink refuses it. What the mod holds after any of those is on settings.<uplink>.

settings.save

Takes effect when sent

Apply the settings from one Save press together and write the settings file once. Arguments to settings.save: one Save press, applied together and written to the settings file once. Never delayed by signal delay.

Safe to send again. A save sets each row to the value named, so repeating one that already landed changes nothing. That matters because a save that times out may still land.

Refused, with nothing changed, when any row is not declared or any value is not one its row can hold. A save that changes the values but cannot write the file is not refused: the values are in force, and settings.gonogo's SettingsModel.persistence says the file was not written.

changes SettingsChange[]

Every row to change, each with its new value. Rows not listed keep their values.

spaceCenter 7 telemetry

Crew, launch sites and parts available at the space centre

Telemetry 7

Telemetry

spaceCenter.astronautComplex

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delayHeld at homeSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

The Astronaut Complex hire tab, the rolling pool of applicants the operator can recruit, plus the roster-cap context a hire is gated on.

A wrapper object, not a bare array, so the applicant list arrives with the facility's crew cap, the current active-crew count and the hire price, which a hire control needs together. The current roster is on the separate spaceCenter.crewRoster channel. The whole payload is null in sandbox, outside career and with no game loaded, when no applicant pool exists; a career save whose pool is empty sends a non-null payload with an empty AstronautComplexInfo.applicants list.

Kept at the home command centre, like CrewRosterEntry: the one that holds the career ledger, so a screen working from another command centre sees a change after the signal delay from home.

Payload AstronautComplexInfo 4 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
applicants CrewRosterEntry[]

The hireable applicant pool (KerbalRoster.Applicants), sharing CrewRosterEntry's full shape (with CrewRosterEntry.situation always "Applicant") so the Astronaut Complex's applicant and active-crew rows render off one type. Always present (empty, never null) once the payload itself is non-null.
activeCrew optional number | null count

Current active (Crew-type) count (KerbalRoster.GetActiveCrewCount): the number counted against AstronautComplexInfo.crewCapacity. Null when the roster isn't queryable.
crewCapacity optional number | null count

Active-crew cap set by the Astronaut Complex facility tier (GameVariables.GetActiveCrewLimit over the facility's normalised level). A hire is blocked once AstronautComplexInfo.activeCrew reaches it. int.MaxValue (2147483647) at the top facility tier (unlimited); preserved as-is on the wire, never clamped, so the client can render "unlimited". Null when the facility isn't queryable.
nextHireCost optional number | null funds

Funds cost to hire the next applicant (GameVariables.GetRecruitHireCost): one figure for the whole pool, the same for every applicant this tick and rising with the current roster size.

spaceCenter.crewRoster

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delayHeld at homeSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

One kerbal in the spaceCenter.crewRoster channel (the hired-crew roster: KSP's KerbalRoster.Crew, owned crew that is either available or currently assigned to a mission), and the same shape for every entry in AstronautComplexInfo.applicants: one shape for a kerbal whether hired or still a candidate.

The spaceCenter.crewRoster channel is a bare array of these entries, one per crew member keyed by CrewRosterEntry.name. The whole payload is null (not an empty array) when no sample has arrived yet, which tells "no data yet" apart from "zero crew".

Kept at the home command centre, like LaunchSiteEntry: the one that holds the career ledger, so a screen working from another command centre sees a change after the signal delay from home.

Payload CrewRosterEntry[] 18 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
name optional string | null

Kerbal name (ProtoCrewMember.name): the id the hire command resolves against the live applicant pool.
trait optional string | null

Specialisation (ProtoCrewMember.trait): "Pilot"/"Engineer"/"Scientist"/"Tourist".
experienceLevel optional number | null count

Experience level (ProtoCrewMember.experienceLevel), 0 to 5 (0 for a fresh applicant).
available optional boolean | null

Whether the kerbal can be assigned to a flight today.

Branch on this for a yes or no. It is derived from CrewRosterEntry.standing: only Available and Applicant can fly, so a standing added to CrewStanding later reads as unavailable here. An applicant counts as free because nothing blocks hiring one, but it is not yet crew: check CrewRosterEntry.isApplicant before offering one a flight.

A mod that knows better about a kerbal's availability, such as a career mod, may set it outright.
unavailableReason optional string | null

Why the kerbal can't fly, in prose: Assigned reads "On mission", Resting reads "Standing down", and every other blocking standing reads its own name. Empty string when CrewRosterEntry.available is true. A mod that knows better may set the wording.

No date, ever. The end is on CrewRosterEntry.standingEndsAtUt as a ut value, so the client formats it in its own calendar. This is the only text on the payload written as a sentence by the mod, so a client cannot reformat it.
standing optional CrewStanding | null

The kerbal's standing, as the dashboard means it: the field to branch on. The reading of a mod that supplies its own where there is one, otherwise Gonogo's own rule applied to every axis KSP exposes (roster status, applicant and the stand-down flag).

The roster status alone is not enough: an applicant has none, and a kerbal standing down still reads Available there. See CrewStanding.
standingEndsAtUt optional number | null ut

When the kerbal's unavailability lapses, as universal time: the rest period's end for Resting, or whatever end the crew mod in use quotes. Absent when there is no scheduled end, which is most of the time.

Read with CrewRosterEntry.unavailableReason to say why a kerbal cannot fly and until when. The two are separate fields so the client formats the date in its own calendar.
situation optional string | null

CrewRosterEntry.standing's display label: its enum name, or "Applicant" for a hireable candidate. Text for an operator, never a branch: compare CrewRosterEntry.standing instead.
situationOrdinal optional KspRosterStatus | null

KSP's own ordinal: (int)ProtoCrewMember.rosterStatus, typed to KspRosterStatus, whose members mirror KSP's numbering.

The game's field, unchanged; Gonogo's crew commands check against it. It is not the field to branch on: it reads Available for a kerbal standing down. Branch on CrewRosterEntry.standing.

null for an applicant, and that is a real distinction rather than a missing value: an applicant is not in the roster, so it has no RosterStatus at all, and CrewRosterEntry.standing carries 1 (Applicant) instead. Use CrewRosterEntry.isApplicant to tell the two apart. Also null when the capture carried no status.
inactive optional boolean | null

Whether the kerbal is standing down rather than on duty (ProtoCrewMember.inactive): KSP's own field, published beside the derived standing the way CrewRosterEntry.situationOrdinal is.

Not the field to branch on. It is one input to CrewRosterEntry.standing: a kerbal standing down has roster status Available, and this flag is what turns that into 4 (Resting) with CrewRosterEntry.available false. Present on every install.
inactiveUntilUt optional number | null ut

When the stand-down ends (ProtoCrewMember.inactiveTimeEnd), as universal time. Absent when CrewRosterEntry.inactive is false, because the field then holds the end of an earlier rest that is already over.
isApplicant optional boolean | null

Whether this entry is a hireable candidate (ProtoCrewMember.type == KerbalType.Applicant) rather than owned crew. Carried so a client never has to recognise the "Applicant" spelling of CrewRosterEntry.situation to know which channel it is reading.
courage optional number | null ratio

Courage, 0 to 1 (ProtoCrewMember.courage), fixed when the kerbal is hired.
stupidity optional number | null ratio

Stupidity, 0 to 1 (ProtoCrewMember.stupidity), fixed when the kerbal is hired.
experience optional number | null 1

Raw experience points (ProtoCrewMember.experience), 0 for a fresh applicant.
experienceLevelDelta optional number | null ratio

Progress toward the next rank, 0 to 1 (the computed ProtoCrewMember.ExperienceLevelDelta); 1 at max rank (5).
roleDescription optional string | null

The role's stock tooltip description (ProtoCrewMember.experienceTrait.Description): the exact string the in-game Astronaut Complex shows, sourced from Traits.cfg.
descriptionEffects optional string | null

The role's current-rank effects text (ProtoCrewMember.experienceTrait.DescriptionEffects): rank-aware, it changes as the kerbal is promoted. Reflects this kerbal's own rank today only; there is no fetchable "effects at another rank" preview.

spaceCenter.launchSites

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delayHeld at homeSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

One launch site in the spaceCenter.launchSites channel: the stock KSC pad and runway, any Making History sites, and any Kerbal Konstructs sites, which is every launch site the game has registered.

The channel is a bare array of these entries, not a wrapper object and not a single KSC record: KSP has many launch sites, keyed by LaunchSiteEntry.name. The whole payload is null (not an empty array) when no sample has arrived yet, which tells "no data yet" apart from "zero sites". It carries no meta of its own.

Kept at the home command centre, the one that holds the career ledger (see CommandCentreEntry). A screen working from another command centre, which is its vantage, sees a change after the signal delay from home to that centre, and at once when both are on the ground network.

Payload LaunchSiteEntry[] 9 fields

system 1 telemetry, 4 commands

Reference frames, command gates and the uplink queue

Telemetry 1

Telemetry

system.frame

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay LiveSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

The frame the game's own navigation view is expressed in, which is what the player is looking at. A burn given relative to the control frame holds its direction fixed against this frame.

This is not a widget's own read frame, which nothing else sees. It belongs to the game, there is one at a time, and it can be written as well as read (SetControlFrameArgs), so a command centre can put the player's view where a plan is being discussed.

Bodies are named by bodyName, the key of every other body table on the wire, trackingStation.bodies included.

A pulsating frame turns about two groups of bodies, and its origin is defined by the mass of each whole group, so the sets travel as well as the pair. ControlFrame.primaryBodies always leads with ControlFrame.primaryBody: take the heads for the pair, or the sets to compute the frame.

The whole payload is null when the frame could not be read. With stock KSP the frame is always 1 (BodyCentredInertial) about the active vessel's reference body.

Payload ControlFrame 9 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
kind ControlFrameKind

The kind of frame. 0 (Unspecified) for the target frame, which has no kind.
centreBody optional string | null

The bodyName the frame is centred on, or null when it has none. The rotating frames are defined by their pair rather than by a centre.
primaryBody optional string | null

The bodyName a rotating frame turns about. null for the centred frames.
secondaryBody optional string | null

The bodyName a rotating frame is anchored to. null for the centred frames.
primaryBodies optional string[] | null

Every body on the primary side, by bodyName, leading with ControlFrame.primaryBody. null when the head is the whole side, never an empty array.
secondaryBodies optional string[] | null

Every body on the secondary side, by bodyName, leading with ControlFrame.secondaryBody. null when the head is the whole side, never an empty array.
targetFrameSelected optional boolean | null

true when the frame is defined against the current target rather than against a body. This sits beside ControlFrame.kind rather than inside it. Closest approach is computed only in this frame, and apsides do not exist in it. null when the source did not say.
targetId optional string | null

The id of the target vessel the frame is defined against, when it is a target frame; otherwise null.
settableFrames optional ControlFrameOption[] | null

Every frame system.frame.set can put the view in, each named exactly as the command takes it. Empty when the view cannot be moved at all, which is stock; null when the source did not say. Either way there is nothing to offer: a frame not listed here is one the command will refuse.

Commands 4

Command

system.frame.set

Takes effect when sent

Put the view in a different reference frame. Takes the frame to put the view in.

It names the two head bodies, not the sets: where ControlFrame reports PrimaryBodies and SecondaryBodies, the mod that owns the view works out which bodies fall on each side of a pulsating frame.

Refusal is normal: stock KSP's frame follows the active vessel's reference body and cannot be set, so the command fails with ModeUnavailable.

FieldTypeUnitDescription
kind ControlFrameKind

The kind of frame to select.
centreBody optional string | null

The bodyName to centre on. Required for the centred frames.
primaryBody optional string | null

The bodyName a rotating frame turns about. Required for the rotating frames.
secondaryBody optional string | null

The bodyName a rotating frame is anchored to. Required for the rotating frames.
targetFrameSelected optional boolean | null

true to ask for the target frame, which sits beside SetControlFrameArgs.kind rather than inside it.

Result CommandResult

Command

system.gate.check

Takes effect when sent

Asks what a command's gate says about one particular call, from the command centre asking, without sending it. The reply is the GateVerdict a dispatch of the same call would meet.

This answers what system.uplink.gates cannot: a verdict that depends on the arguments the operator has chosen (a launch site, a time warp rate) or on the command centre they are sending from. A control asks when the operator's choice changes, not on every tick, and draws a 1 (Fail) dark with the verdict's own reason. The dispatch remains the authority: nothing here is a permission, and the answer can be out of date by the time the operator presses.

A command with no declared gate answers 0 (Pass). An argument the gate needs and the call leaves out answers 2 (Abstain). A command the host does not know is refused as not found.

Arguments GateCheckRequest 2 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
command string

The command whose gate is asked about, e.g. ksp.launch.
args map of any

The arguments the call would carry, keyed by their wire names. Empty asks about the command with nothing chosen yet.
Result GateVerdict 6 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
outcome GateOutcome

What the gate concluded. Defaults to 0 (Pass).
errorCode optional CommandErrorCode | null

Which refusal, for a 1 (Fail): the same error code a command handler's own refusal carries, so one client sentence serves a declared gate and a handler that got far enough to look.

Set by the evaluator, because only the evaluator knows what it checked: a full pad and an un-upgraded Tracking Station are both a gate saying no, and they are not the same refusal. "modeUnavailable" is what GateVerdict.Fail names for an evaluator that says nothing more. Null on every outcome but a Fail.

On the wire the root's id, with a refinement's own id beside it as GateVerdict.reason, as on CommandResult.
reason optional string | null

The refinement's id when GateVerdict.errorCode is more specific than its root; absent otherwise.
breach optional LimitBreach | null

Set only for a numeric 1 (Fail). Null is the shape a client keys on: an Abstain or an Unknown has nothing to compare, so it must not arrive carrying zeroes that render as a real limit of 0.
detail string

Why, when the outcome carries no numeric comparison: a 3 (Unknown)'s cause, or a discrete prerequisite's name. Prose for a human, never parsed.
missing optional MissingUnlock[] | null

For a "notUnlocked" Fail, each unlock this save is missing: a tech node not researched, or a building below the level it needs. Absent on every other outcome, and on a refusal whose evaluator could not say which unlock it was.

  "label": "system.gate.check",
  "topic": "",

    "command": "<command>",
    "args": {}
  },
  "sentAt": 0
}
Command

system.uplink.cancel

Takes effect when sent

Cancels a held or travelling command, named by its lane number, alone or with every later number this centre had sent on the lane when it was pressed. A lane is the ordered run of delayed commands one centre sends to one craft, and a lane number is a command's place in it. A command this centre is still holding stops at once; for one it has sent, a cancel goes to the craft, stopping the command wherever it is held and refusing it at the craft if it arrives there first. What it stopped arrives as journey reports.

The reply says the cancel was sent, never that the command was stopped. A command sent less than twice its signal delay ago may have been lost on the way, in which case it is still this centre's, but the centre cannot know that yet, so the cancel is sent after it all the same and the command is reported cancelled here only once it is known to have come back.

Arguments UplinkCancelRequest 4 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
epoch number count

The timeline the command was sent in; a cancel naming another timeline is refused.
craft string

The craft its lane runs to, as PendingUplink.craft.
laneSeq number count

Its place on its lane, the ordered run of delayed commands one command centre sends to one craft, as PendingUplink.laneSeq.
andBehind boolean

Whether to cancel every later number on the lane too, up to the newest this centre has sent.

Result UplinkActionReply

target 1 telemetry

What the active vessel can target

Telemetry 1

Telemetry

target.available

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

The list of everything targetable from the active vessel, as the active vessel knows it. Wrapper object { "entries": [ ... ] }, like trackingStation.catalog.

A vessel is on the list once the active vessel has come to know of it, by whichever of three ways tells it soonest: it is within physics range and seen as it is; its radio reaches the active vessel directly, one signal delay of that link ago; or the active vessel's command centre knows of it and has said so over the control route, that route's signal delay ago. Each entry says which (TargetListEntry.source) and how old (TargetListEntry.asOfUt). A vessel with no route home and nothing in range keeps the list it last had: entries age, none is added. A vessel the active vessel has been told is gone leaves the list.

Delayed like the rest of the active vessel's telemetry: a centre reads the list one of its own signal delays after the vessel held it.

Payload TargetAvailable 1 field
FieldTypeUnitDescription
entries TargetListEntry[]

Every current target candidate. Empty, never null, when there is none.

A model can carry part of this list forward: the range to a vessel the active one only knows of, which has no measured TargetListEntry.distance, follows from that vessel's TargetListEntry.orbit and the active vessel's own orbit. Every other field of every entry is the observation.

time 2 telemetry, 2 commands

Game time, warp and pause

Telemetry 2

Telemetry

time.calendar

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay LiveSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

How long a minute, hour, day and year are, and what real-world instant UT 0 is (when the game has one), as the running game defines them.

Every duration on the wire is SI seconds. To express one in days or years, divide by these values rather than by a constant: 21,600 seconds per day is right only for stock KSP on Kerbin time.

Three things change them:

  • Stock, no mods. The game's Kerbin time setting is one a player can turn off, and KSP's own UI then reads in 24-hour days and 365-day years.
  • A planet pack. A planet-pack mod replaces the game's date formatter, the code that prints its clock, so a day becomes 86,400 s and a year 365 days.
  • Anything else. Any mod can put its own calendar behind the game's date formatter.

Whatever the game uses to print its own clock is what this channel carries: each duration is the count of seconds the date formatter gives for a minute, hour, day and year.

It can change mid-session: the Kerbin time setting is reachable from the in-game settings menu at any time.

The whole payload is null when the calendar cannot be read or any of the four durations is missing or not positive, so a consumer never divides by zero. There is no days-per-year field: divide TimeCalendar.yearSeconds by TimeCalendar.daySeconds, which is exact.

Payload TimeCalendar 7 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
minuteSeconds number s

Seconds in one minute, as the game's date formatter defines it. 60 in every known calendar. Always positive.
hourSeconds number s

Seconds in one hour, as the game's date formatter defines it. Always positive.
daySeconds number s

Seconds in one day: 21,600 on stock Kerbin time, 86,400 under Earth time or a planet pack. Always positive.
yearSeconds number s

Seconds in one year: 9,201,600 on stock Kerbin time (426 days), 31,536,000 under a 365-day Earth calendar. Always positive.
epoch optional string | null

The real-world instant UT 0 corresponds to, ISO-8601 in UTC (1951-01-01T00:00:00Z), or null when the running game has no such instant. Never an empty string.

The durations say how long a day is; this says which day it is. Every Units.UniversalTime field is an offset from UT 0, so with an epoch a deadline can be shown as 14 Mar 1957 rather than Y3 D122.

It is read from the date formatter itself. A formatter that models a real calendar holds an anchor date, as a planet-pack mod's does; the stock formatter holds none.

null means the game has no real-world calendar, which is the normal case and is not the same as an epoch of zero. Stock KSP has no real calendar: its own UI prints Year 1, Day 1, and so should every consumer. A planet pack that changes the day length without installing a date-based formatter has no anchor either. Do not render a default anchor for those games.
kerbinTime boolean

Telemetry

time.warp

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay LiveSamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

The game's time-warp and pause state, as separate typed fields.

Current UT is not a field here, nor on any other Topic of the wire contract: meta.validAt stamps every sample with the UT it describes, so the current UT is the meta.validAt of the newest frame.

Warp and pause are game-wide state, not a craft's: the payload's meta.source is "game" rather than "vessel:<guid>", and the Topic emits at the Space Center and Tracking Station as well as in flight, with or without an active vessel.

Payload WarpState 9 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
warpRate number 1

The current time-warp multiplier (KSP's TimeWarp.CurrentRate): 1 is real time, 1000 is game time passing a thousand times faster. A pure ratio, so its unit is the dimensionless "1".
warpRateIndex number

The current rung (one step) of the warp rate table (KSP's TimeWarp.CurrentRateIndex), 0 at real time. Under 0 (High) it indexes WarpState.warpRates.
warpMode WarpMode

Which warp mode is in force, on-rails or physics (KSP's TimeWarp.WarpMode).
paused boolean

Whether the game is paused (KSP's FlightDriver.Pause).
warpRates optional number[] | null

What every on-rails warp rung of this install actually runs at, indexed by WarpState.warpRateIndex, so warpRates[i] is the multiplier time.setWarpIndex (SetWarpIndexArgs) with index = i produces. Null when the game has no warp controller to read it off (no scene that can warp).

The table is configuration, not a constant: Kopernicus and RealSolarSystem both republish it, so a rung stock runs at 100x may run at 10000x on another install. Read the rate here rather than assuming stock's table.
keyframeFloorSec number s

The shortest real time the mod leaves between two periodic keyframes on one channel, in seconds. A keyframe is a full sample sent on a schedule even when nothing changed, so a client can tell a quiet channel from a dead one.

Keyframe cadences are declared in UT, and under warp UT can pass a cadence on every tick, so the mod also waits at least this long in real time. The gap a client sees between two keyframes of a quiet channel is therefore at least keyframeFloorSec × warpRate UT. A client that judges how current a channel is from the gap between its keyframes should allow for that much.
observationQuantumUt optional number | null s

The UT that actually passes between two samples at the current warp rate, in seconds, or null where the host did not report its physics step.

Equal to WarpState.sampleIntervalUt up to 10x warp. Above that the mod samples at most ten times a real second, so this is the game time that passes in a tenth of a real second at the current rate (0.1 s x 100,000 = 10,000 s at 100,000x), or one physics tick where a tick advances the game further than that. Nothing between two consecutive samples was observed, so a line drawn between two samples that differ would claim a path across this span that only a reckoner's model of the value (see the Reckoners page) can support. Two samples further apart than this are a channel that did not change in between.

It changes only when the warp rate does. A client judging a gap reads the quantum in force when the later sample was taken.
sampleIntervalUt number s

The UT between two samples while warp is not thinning them, in seconds: the finest spacing the record ever has, and WarpState.observationQuantumUt at 1x. Constant for the life of the mod.

The chord between two samples this far apart is the resolution every channel is sampled at, and a chart can draw it. Where the quantum is wider, the span beyond this is one the sampling skipped because of warp, and a line across it that no model of the value carries asserts a path nothing observed.
meta PayloadMeta

Telemetry

trackingStation.catalog

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

Every object the receiving command centre knows of, craft and tracked space objects alike, one entry each, wrapped as { "entries": [ ... ] }. Like SystemBodies, it carries no per-payload Meta: that rides the envelope.

Each command centre is sent its own catalog and no other centre's. A centre knows an object in two ways, and an entry is made of both.

By sight: where it is. An object's orbit, its situation and its body are tracked by looking at it, whether or not it has a radio and whether or not it is in contact. That reaches a centre in a straight line at light speed, through no relay, so a burn far away shows here after the distance between the craft and this centre and no sooner. An object with no radio at all (debris, an asteroid, a flag, a crewed craft with no antenna) is known this way only: it is listed, with its name and kind, once light from it has had time to reach this centre, and removed the same delay after it is gone.

By radio: everything else. A craft's crew and its link are its own to say, and arrive over its radio's route at that route's signal delay. A craft that has been seen and not yet heard has no crew count and no link state, which are absent and not zero. Where a craft has a radio its location is as fresh as the newer of the two.

Contact. Whether this centre is in contact with each craft is what has reached this centre: in contact, silent, overdue, lost or gone. Only the home centre declares a craft lost, and a centre shows the declaration once it has reached it.

What can be tracked by sight is the game's own tracking station rule at the station's current level. Where the game lets the station place no object at all, nothing is known by sight and every entry is what was heard.

Commands 2

Command

trackingStation.bodies.statesAt

Takes effect when sent

Ask where a body is at each of a list of instants. Args for trackingStation.bodies.statesAt: where one body is at each of a list of instants, from the propagation provider in use on this install. The instants are the caller's own, such as the departure and arrival times a transfer search tries.

The command centre is the sender's, taken from the connection the command arrives on; there is no field to name another.

A centre body is required, with no default: the reply is expressed relative to it. For a transfer search, name the parent both endpoints orbit; the same request works for a moon system.

BodyStatesRequest.certification is required too: the caller states whether it accepts results past the span the provider vouches for, and a request that does not say is refused.

The result is a conic (two-body) solve, so no ephemeris horizon applies to it.

Arguments BodyStatesRequest 4 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
bodyIndex number

The body, by its trackingStation.bodies index.
centreBodyIndex number

The body the reply is expressed relative to, by the same index. For a transfer search this is the parent both endpoints orbit.
uts number[]

The instants to solve for, in UT seconds. Returned in the order given, so a caller can zip the reply against its own grid without matching on a time it would have to compare as a float.
certification PropagationCertification

Whether this caller accepts a result past the span the provider vouches for. Only 1 (Unbounded) is accepted.

0 (Unspecified) is refused rather than defaulted, and so is 2 (CertifiedOnly), because the request carries instants with no origin to measure a span from.
Result BodyStatesReply 4 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
solved boolean

True when the provider solved every requested instant and BodyStatesReply.states holds them; false when the request was refused, with the reason in BodyStatesReply.refusal.
states BodyState[]

One state per requested instant, in the order asked. Empty when BodyStatesReply.solved is false.
providerId optional string | null

Id of the propagation provider that solved the request, so a reading that looks wrong can be attributed to it. Null on a refusal.
refusal optional string | null

Why the request was refused, in words an operator can act on, when BodyStatesReply.solved is false; null when it is true.

Telemetry

vessel.attitude

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

Pitch, heading and roll of the vessel's control reference, the orientation the pilot steers by, against the local surface up and north, in two named frames.

VesselAttitude.pitch, VesselAttitude.heading and VesselAttitude.roll are the primary frame, with up and north measured at the vessel's centre of mass. VesselAttitude.pitchRootFrame, VesselAttitude.headingRootFrame and VesselAttitude.rollRootFrame measure up and north at the root part's position instead. The orientation is the same in both; the two differ only when the root part sits away from the centre of mass. Without a root part the root frame repeats the primary one.

Absent when the vessel has no reference body. Attitude is not derivable from orbital elements, so it is streamed raw.

Pitch above the horizon, measured at the centre of mass. Degrees, -90 (nose down) to 90 (nose up).

roll number °

Roll, measured at the centre of mass. Degrees, -180 to 180.

As VesselAttitude.pitch, measured at the root part. Degrees, -90 to 90.
headingRootFrame number °

As VesselAttitude.heading, measured at the root part. Degrees, 0 to 360.

vessel.control

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

The active vessel's control state (the stock toggles, SAS mode, throttle, the commanded fly-by-wire axes and the custom action groups). The payload is present whenever there is an active vessel; each field is individually nullable, and null means that input could not be read this tick (for example no flight input state, or no action-group data), never a default.

Each control field that can be changed is paired with its command through its control channel, so the confirmed state and the command that changes it are one handle. The confirmed value lags a command by the round trip, including any comms delay.

VesselControl.throttle is 0..1 nominally, but KSP does not clamp Vessel.ctrlState.mainThrottle: a throttle driven by kOS or another mod can read above 1. The value is passed through unclamped.

Payload VesselControl 20 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
sas optional boolean | null

Whether SAS is on. Changed with vessel.control.setSas.
sasAvailable optional boolean | null

Whether the vessel has a source that can hold SAS on: a Pilot aboard, or a probe core whose SAS tier allows it (KSP's VesselSAS.CanEngageSAS). When false, vessel.control.setSas refuses to turn SAS on, so a client can show the control unavailable before it is pressed; turning SAS off is never refused. Null when the vessel has no autopilot to ask.
sasUnavailableReason optional string | null

Why SAS cannot be turned on, in the words the refusal uses, when VesselControl.sasAvailable is false. Null whenever SAS is available or unknown.
sasMode optional SasMode | null

The SAS hold mode. Changed with vessel.control.setSasMode.
rcs optional boolean | null

Whether RCS is on. Changed with vessel.control.setRcs.
gear optional boolean | null

Whether the Gear action group is engaged (landing gear deployed). Changed with vessel.control.setGear.
brakes optional boolean | null

Whether the Brakes action group is engaged. Changed with vessel.control.setBrakes.
lights optional boolean | null

Whether the Lights action group is engaged. Changed with vessel.control.setLights.
abort optional boolean | null

Whether the Abort action group is engaged. Changed with vessel.control.setAbort.
precisionControl optional boolean | null

Precision-control (fine-control / caps-lock) mode. Mirrors KSP's FlightInputHandler.fetch.precisionMode. Null when there is no active flight scene. Changed with vessel.control.setPrecisionControl.
flyByWire optional boolean | null

Whether the fly-by-wire override is on for this vessel. Changed with vessel.control.setFlyByWire. The override belongs to the craft it was turned on for, so this is false on any other craft even while the override is on elsewhere, and it reads true again only on the craft that carries it. Unlike a client's own record of the commands it sent, it survives a page reload.
throttle optional number | null ratio

Main throttle, KSP's Vessel.ctrlState.mainThrottle: 0..1 nominally, but not clamped, so a mod-driven throttle can read above 1. Changed with vessel.control.setThrottle.
pitch optional number | null 1

The applied pitch axis input, -1..1, from KSP's Vessel.ctrlState.pitch. Null when the vessel has no control state. Set with vessel.control.setAxes.
yaw optional number | null 1

The applied yaw axis input, -1..1, from KSP's Vessel.ctrlState.yaw. Null when the vessel has no control state. Set with vessel.control.setAxes.
roll optional number | null 1

The applied roll axis input, -1..1, from KSP's Vessel.ctrlState.roll. Null when the vessel has no control state. Set with vessel.control.setAxes.
translationX optional number | null 1

The applied translation X input (RCS right/left), -1..1, from KSP's Vessel.ctrlState.X. Null when the vessel has no control state. Set with vessel.control.setAxes.
translationY optional number | null 1

The applied translation Y input (RCS up/down), -1..1, from KSP's Vessel.ctrlState.Y. Null when the vessel has no control state. Set with vessel.control.setAxes.
translationZ optional number | null 1

The applied translation Z input (RCS forward/back), -1..1, from KSP's Vessel.ctrlState.Z. Null when the vessel has no control state. Set with vessel.control.setAxes.
actionGroups optional ActionGroupState[] | null

Every custom action group the vessel has, each named and carrying its own index (see ActionGroupState). Stock KSP yields ten entries (AG1..AG10); an AGX backend may yield up to 250 with the player's own names. Null when action-group data wasn't available this tick; never a partial list. Order is by ActionGroupState.index ascending, but read ActionGroupState.index rather than relying on array position: position does not carry identity here.

vessel.dock

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

The relative position, velocity and coarse orientation between the active vessel's nearest free (undocked) docking port and the targeted docking port, for docking-alignment widgets. The whole payload is absent when docking is not relevant right now: nothing is targeted, the target is not a docking port, or the active vessel has no free port. It is never an old or zero-distance placeholder record, the same convention as VesselTarget.

DockAlignment.forwardDot is the dot product of the two ports' forward (docking-axis) vectors: -1 means the ports face each other head-on (the alignment a dock needs), +1 means they point the same way. It is the raw dot product, so how to show it (for example as a percentage) is up to the widget.

The target port's velocity relative to the own port, m/s.

Metres: DockAlignment.relativePosition's magnitude, provided directly so a widget does not have to derive it every frame.

Dot product of the own port's and target port's forward vectors, -1..1: -1 facing head-on, +1 pointing the same way. Null only when either port's transform was unavailable this tick.

vessel.flight

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

Quantities the game measures, either because they cannot be derived from orbital elements (terrain height, aerodynamic state) or because they are the measured value to check a prediction against (speeds). One field per quantity.

The channel is absent when there is no active vessel or any of its fields could not be read; there is never a (0,0) lat/long placeholder. There is no mission time field: see VesselIdentity.launchUt.

Payload VesselFlight 14 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
latitude number °

Latitude of the vessel's position on its reference body, degrees (KSP's Vessel.latitude). Present means valid: there is no (0,0) no-data placeholder, and absence is the whole channel being unavailable.
longitude number °

Longitude of the vessel's position on its reference body, degrees (KSP's Vessel.longitude, passed through without normalising its range). Same presence rule as VesselFlight.latitude.
altitudeAsl number m

Altitude above sea level, metres (KSP's Vessel.altitude).
altitudeTerrain number m

Height above terrain (AGL, KSP's Vessel.radarAltitude), metres. Not derivable from orbital elements, so it is streamed as measured.
verticalSpeed number m/s

Metres per second (KSP's Vessel.verticalSpeed), signed: negative is descending.
surfaceSpeed number m/s

Speed relative to the ground beneath the vessel, which turns with the body, metres per second (KSP's Vessel.srfSpeed). It can be higher than VesselFlight.orbitalSpeed: far above the synchronous altitude a craft in a prograde orbit moves more slowly than the ground below it turns.
orbitalSpeed number m/s

Speed relative to the parent body's centre, ignoring its rotation, metres per second (KSP's Vessel.obt_speed). This is the speed of the orbit.
gForce number g

Multiples of standard gravity (KSP's Vessel.geeForce).
dynamicPressureKPa number kPa

Dynamic pressure on the vessel, kilopascals (KSP's Vessel.dynamicPressurekPa). 0 outside an atmosphere.
mach number 1

Mach number (KSP's Vessel.mach), dimensionless.
atmDensity number kg/m³

Atmospheric density at the vessel's position, kg/m³ (KSP's Vessel.atmDensity).
externalTemperature number K

Skin/ambient external temperature the vessel is exposed to, Kelvin (Vessel.externalTemperature).
atmosphericTemperature number K

Ambient atmospheric temperature at the vessel's position, Kelvin (Vessel.atmosphericTemperature).

vessel.inventory

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

The stock cargo a vessel's parts are carrying: what is aboard, and in which part.

A kerbal's own inventory is not here: it is on vessel.crew, beside the trait and experience level that decide whether that kerbal can do a job. This channel lists only part-hosted stores.

Each store is reported with its part rather than as one vessel total, because a craft can carry plenty of something while the kerbal who needs it has none. A kerbal has two slots, 40 units of volume and a 65 kg limit, and one slot holds a parachute by default; a cargo container holds far more.

Stock KSP, with or without any Uplink: stock repairs consume stock cargo, so a stock career has inventories worth showing.

Payload VesselInventory 1 field
FieldTypeUnitDescription
stores InventoryStore[]

Every part-hosted inventory on the active vessel this tick, in vessel part-list order. Always present (possibly empty); a vessel-less tick, or one whose holds could not be read, yields a null payload, not an empty list.
