vessel.landing

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

Landing data for the active vessel that needs the terrain map of the body below (slope, roughness and elevation at the touchdown site), plus an atmosphere-aware descent estimate built from the vessel's measured drag. The vacuum ballistic figures (which need no terrain) are not here; a client solves those itself.

The whole payload is absent unless the vessel is descending toward a solid surface: the body must have a solid surface and terrain, and the vessel must be descending towards it within the prediction horizon. So it never carries a leftover reading from orbit, or a 0 from a body with no terrain.

Every field is nullable, and null means that input is unavailable this tick (no terrain fit, not in an atmosphere, and so on), never an unverified 0.

Payload VesselLanding 27 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
outcome optional string | null

Which class of landing readout is valid this tick, so a client can render the state rather than infer it from which fields are null. One of "atmospheric-aware" (the atmospheric descent fields are solved), "terrain-assessed" (no atmospheric solution, but a terrain slope fit exists) or "vacuum-solved" (neither). "no-solution" is part of the vocabulary but not currently produced.
sampleSource optional string | null

Where the terrain fields were sampled this tick: "predicted" (at the mod's predicted touchdown point, the site the vessel is heading for) or "sub-vessel" (directly under the vessel, when there is no touchdown prediction). Show it, so the operator knows whether they are seeing downrange or under-ship terrain. Null when no terrain was sampled.
predictedLatitude optional number | null °

Latitude in degrees of the point the terrain fields were sampled at: the predicted touchdown point, or the vessel's own latitude when VesselLanding.sampleSource is "sub-vessel".
predictedLongitude optional number | null °

Longitude in degrees of the sampled point, on the same terms as VesselLanding.predictedLatitude and always present together with it.
predictedTerrainElevation optional number | null m

Terrain elevation in metres at the sampled point, KSP's CelestialBody.TerrainAltitude(lat, lon, allowNegative: true), so ocean floor reads as negative rather than clamping to 0.
predictedSlopeAngle optional number | null °

Terrain slope in degrees at the sampled point, from a plane fit over sampled heights (so a bowl is not mistaken for an incline). The tip-over risk readout, available while still descending. Null when the plane fit fails.
predictedSlopeHeading optional number | null °

The downhill direction at the sampled point in degrees, 0 north, clockwise: which way the lander falls if it tips. Null when the slope is too slight to give a direction.
predictedRoughness optional number | null m

The residual standard deviation, in metres, of sampled terrain height at the sampled point after the fitted slope plane is removed (so tilt is not counted as roughness), over VesselLanding.roughnessFootprintMeters. The boulder-risk proxy.
roughnessFootprintMeters optional number | null m

The footprint radius in metres that VesselLanding.predictedRoughness was sampled over, so a client can label and grade it.
slopeSampleRadiusMeters optional number | null m

The radius in metres the slope plane-fit samples span.
predictedBiome optional string | null

KSP's biome name at the sampled point (for the vessel's current position, read vessel.surface.biome), from ScienceUtil.GetExperimentBiome. Null when the body has no biome map.
groundTrackDistances optional number[] | null

The distance in metres of each VesselLanding.groundTrackElevations sample along the predicted ground track, signed: 0 is the point on the ground beneath the vessel, positive is toward the predicted site and on past it, negative is behind the vessel. Ascending, the same length as VesselLanding.groundTrackElevations. The strip always holds the ground directly beneath the vessel, with at least one vessel height (and never less than 120 m) of ground behind it, and runs on to the far edge of the footprint of a cone of 60 degrees either side of the vessel's travel vector: where the cone's two edges, in the plane of the vessel's motion, meet the ground. A flat or climbing approach has an edge that never meets it, and that edge is cut at the horizon. The strip also reaches the predicted site and a tenth of its distance past it. The number of samples is fixed, so they are closer together the narrower the strip, which narrows as the vessel descends. Null when no track could be sampled.
groundTrackElevations optional number[] | null

Terrain elevation in metres at each VesselLanding.groundTrackDistances entry, from the body's terrain model (ocean floor reads negative). Null when no track could be sampled.
siteHeights optional number[] | null

A square of terrain elevations in metres around the predicted site, for a top-down view of it: VesselLanding.siteHeightsSize by VesselLanding.siteHeightsSize values row by row, the northern row first and the western column first in each row, so laying them out in that order puts north at the top. The grid is centred on the site and its width is VesselLanding.siteHeightsExtentMeters: wide enough to hold the ground between the vessel and the site, and about the vessel's height of it either side, so it narrows as the vessel descends and closes on the site, and it may be a second old. Null when no site could be sampled.
horizonAngles optional number[] | null

The skyline the vessel sees, for a view from the vessel: 72 values, entry i looking along bearing i * 5 degrees clockwise from north, each the highest angle above the level, in degrees, at which terrain is seen along that bearing out to about 30 km (or the horizon, if nearer). The ground curves away below the level by range / (2 * radius), which is included. It carries the relief beyond VesselLanding.siteHeights, which holds only the ground around the vessel and the site: a view uses it to draw distant hills and to tell far ground from sky. It says nothing of what hides a nearer point, since the grid already holds all the ground between the vessel and the site. Taken from where the vessel was up to a couple of seconds ago. Null when no site could be sampled.
siteHeightsSize optional number | null count

The number of values along each side of VesselLanding.siteHeights. Null when there is no grid.
siteHeightsExtentMeters optional number | null m

The full width in metres that VesselLanding.siteHeights spans. Null when there is no grid.
terminalVelocity optional number | null m/s

Terminal velocity in m/s at the current altitude and configuration, from the measured aggregate drag force against local gravity. An estimate that assumes the current configuration holds (same attitude, no parachute yet to open). Null outside an atmosphere, or when the vessel's parts could not be read.
projectedTouchdownSpeed optional number | null m/s

Projected touchdown speed in m/s under a terminal descent to the ground (terminal velocity scaled to ground-level density). In an atmosphere, use this rather than a vacuum impact speed. Null outside an atmosphere.
atmosphericTimeToImpact optional number | null s

Atmosphere-aware time to impact in seconds, integrating the terminal-velocity profile down the density column. Null outside an atmosphere.
descentRegime optional string | null

The instantaneous descent regime: "at-terminal", "decelerating" or "accelerating". Null outside an atmosphere.
dragToWeightRatio optional number | null 1

The aggregate aerodynamic drag force divided by the vessel's weight (local gravity): the numeric form of VesselLanding.descentRegime. >1 decelerating (drag beats gravity), 1 at terminal, <1 still accelerating. A dimensionless ratio from 0 upward like TWR, not a 0..1 fraction. Null outside an atmosphere, and for a weightless vessel.
parachuteState optional string | null

Parachute state affecting the estimate: "none" (no parachute is staged or open), "armed" (a parachute is staged and waiting to open: a future jump in drag the estimate cannot see, so flag it) or "deployed" (a parachute is open or semi-deployed, so its drag is already in the measurement). Null outside an atmosphere.
parachuteDeployment optional string | null

How far the craft's parachutes have opened, taken from the one furthest along: "none" (the craft carries no parachute), "stowed" (packed, not yet staged), "armed" (staged and waiting for air thick enough to open in), "semi-deployed" (open as a streamer, slowing the craft a little), "deployed" (fully open) or "cut" (every one cut away). Unlike VesselLanding.parachuteState it tells semi-deployed from fully deployed, and a packed parachute from none. Null outside an atmosphere, and when a parachute whose arming could not be read might be the furthest along.
parachuteDeploySafety optional string | null

Whether opening the parachutes not yet open would survive the current speed and air, as the game rates it from the heating a canopy would take: "safe", "risky" (the canopy would heat but hold for a few seconds) or "unsafe" (it would burn through). The worst rating among the stowed and armed parachutes. Null outside an atmosphere, when every parachute is already open or cut, and for a parachute the game does not rate.
parachuteFullDeployAltitude optional number | null m

The height above the ground or the sea at which an armed or semi-deployed parachute opens fully, the greatest when there are several, since that one opens first. Null when none is armed or semi-deployed, outside an atmosphere, and for a parachute the game does not report one for.

vessel.light

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

Whether the active craft is in sunlight now, and the next two instants at which that changes, for a widget that warps to sunrise or sunset or plans around a night pass.

The star counts as hidden when a body between it and the craft covers its centre. A craft in orbit is swept along its patched conic; a landed or splashed craft is carried round by its body's rotation. The instants are universal times, so they hold wherever they are read and need no reckoning between samples.

Whenever no sound answer exists (an open orbit, an orbit of the star itself, no body table yet) the payload is absent or its instants are null with VesselLight.basis saying withheld, never a guess.

Payload VesselLight 5 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
sunlit optional boolean | null

True while the star is above the craft's horizon and no body covers it, false in shadow. Null when the geometry could not be solved this tick.
nextSunriseUt optional number | null ut

The next universal time the craft leaves shadow, or null when it stays lit through VesselLight.sweptToUt, is lit now and no sunrise is predicted, or no prediction was made.
nextSunsetUt optional number | null ut

The next universal time the craft enters shadow, or null when it stays lit through VesselLight.sweptToUt or no prediction was made.
sweptToUt number ut

The last universal time the search reached. A null instant means no change before it.
basis string

What the instants rest on: orbit (the craft swept along its orbit), surface (the craft carried round by its body's rotation) or withheld (no sound prediction, so both instants are null).

vessel.maneuver

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples Holds until changedRepeats every 30 s of game time

The active vessel's planned burns. VesselManeuver.nodes is always an array, empty when no burn is queued, never null.

VesselManeuver.nodes is ordered by execution, earliest ManeuverNode.ut first, and that order is the plan: burn N is flown after burn N-1 and acts on what burn N-1 left behind. There is no ordinal or predecessor field; array position says it. The per-burn patch chain expresses the same linkage again, in a form only a patched-conic planner can produce; see ManeuverNode.patches.

Payload VesselManeuver 3 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
nodes ManeuverNode[] | LockedValue

Every queued burn, earliest ManeuverNode.ut first. Empty when none is queued, never null. A LockedValue while the Tracking Station does not show patched conics, since a craft then carries no solver to hold a node.
planner optional string | null

The id of the maneuver-plan provider in use, or null when there is no planner at all.

Null is not the same as an empty plan, and stock reaches it on its own: an un-upgraded Tracking Station leaves the craft with no solver, so an early-career craft cannot hold a plan at all. Both arrive as Nodes: [], and this field tells "cannot plan" from "nothing planned".

Test only whether it is null. The value is for naming the provider in a readout or a diagnostic, never for special-casing one.

Telemetry

vessel.orbit

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

The active vessel's orbital elements. Elements are the cause; every kinematic quantity (position, velocity, apsides, anomalies, period) is derived by the consumer at its view UT through the propagation capability, and is not streamed here. The one exception is the pair of apsis countdowns under physics, VesselOrbit.timeToAp and VesselOrbit.timeToPe.

The apoapsis and periapsis altitudes are on the current patch, patches[0].apA and patches[0].peA, in metres above the body's mean radius.

Units: VesselOrbit.sma in metres; VesselOrbit.inc, VesselOrbit.lan and VesselOrbit.argPe in degrees; and VesselOrbit.meanAnomalyAtEpoch in radians. The degrees/radians split is KSP's own and is kept so every value matches KSP's Orbit.

A coast moves only VesselOrbit.meanAnomalyAtEpoch and VesselOrbit.epoch, by Kepler propagation; the other elements are constants of the orbit. A burn moves every element, by powered integration from vessel.propulsion, the firing stage's propellant in dv.stages and trackingStation.bodies. A reckoning's modelled list says which paths its model moved, and a consumer wanting a whole modelled orbit overlays those on the observed payload.

Payload VesselOrbit 15 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
referenceBodyIndex number

Index into trackingStation.bodies of the body this orbit is around.
sma number m

Semi-major axis, in metres.
ecc number 1

Eccentricity. Below 1 for a closed orbit, 1 or above for an escape trajectory.
inc number °

Inclination, in degrees (KSP's Orbit.inclination).
lan optional number | null °

Longitude of ascending node, degrees; null only when absent, never NaN and never 0 as a stand-in. An equatorial orbit still has one.
argPe optional number | null °

Argument of periapsis, degrees; null only when absent, never NaN and never 0 as a stand-in. A circular orbit still has one.
meanAnomalyAtEpoch number rad

Mean anomaly at VesselOrbit.epoch, in radians, not degrees, matching KSP's Orbit.meanAnomalyAtEpoch. Reckonable by Kepler propagation, from VesselOrbit.sma, VesselOrbit.mu, VesselOrbit.horizon and trackingStation.bodies, and under a burn by powered integration with the other elements.
epoch number ut

The reference epoch of VesselOrbit.meanAnomalyAtEpoch, as a universal time in seconds (KSP's Orbit.epoch). Reckonable with VesselOrbit.meanAnomalyAtEpoch by the same model.
mu number m³/s²

The reference body's standard gravitational parameter (GM), so the elements propagate without a separate body lookup.
timeToAp optional number | null s

Seconds from this sample's validAt until the craft next reaches apoapsis on the orbit these elements describe, as KSP computes it (Orbit.timeToAp). Carried only while the craft is under physics (meta.quality Loaded): on rails the same figure follows exactly from the elements, and the field is null. Also null on a hyperbolic orbit, which has no apoapsis. Never a sentinel in place of null.

True at validAt. A client at a later instant subtracts the elapsed time, wrapping by the period once the apsis has passed.
timeToPe optional number | null s

Seconds from this sample's validAt until the craft next reaches periapsis, as KSP computes it (Orbit.timeToPe). Carried under the same rule as VesselOrbit.timeToAp: only while meta.quality is Loaded, null on rails. On a hyperbolic orbit it is null once the periapsis has been passed, since there is no next one. Never a sentinel in place of null.
encounter optional OrbitEncounter | LockedValue | null

The next sphere-of-influence transition on the current trajectory. Null when there is none (the common case), never a sentinel. A LockedValue while the Tracking Station does not show patched conics, since the game then computes no transition at all.
patches OrbitPatch[]

The vessel's future-orbit patch chain. Element 0 is the current patch (the same elements as the fields above, restated in OrbitPatch's shape so a client walks one list), followed by any later sphere-of-influence patches KSP's patched-conic solver has already resolved. Always an array, empty rather than null when there is no chain.
horizon PropagationHorizon

How far ahead these elements may be propagated before they stop being trustworthy. Never null: a producer that does not state a horizon leaves it 0 (Unspecified), which reads as unpropagatable.

A client cannot compute this: it depends on the perturbation environment (which bodies are near, how massive, how far), so it arrives on the sample. It rides here, beside the elements, because a horizon and the elements it bounds share one validAt; carried separately, a client could hold one sample's elements beside another's horizon.
meta OrbitPayloadMeta

Payload provenance. Source is "vessel:<guid>" for the active vessel; Quality is Loaded under physics and OnRails otherwise.

vessel.orbit.truth

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

KSP's own maintained state vector for the active vessel (Orbit.pos and Orbit.vel), relative to the body it orbits. Read vessel.orbit for altitude and velocity.

Absent when the state vector or the frame flag could not be read.

VesselOrbitTruth.frameRotating says which frame the vectors are in, and a comparison must gate on it. When it is false they are in the fixed, non-rotating frame the orbital elements are defined against, and are directly comparable to a Kepler propagation of those elements. When it is true (KSP switches to this below a body's inverseRotThresholdAltitude: low orbit, atmospheric flight, landed) they are in a frame co-rotating with the body's spin, and differ from a fixed-frame propagation by a rotation about the polar axis that grows with time.

Payload VesselOrbitTruth 4 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
position object

Position in metres relative to the body the vessel orbits, KSP's Orbit.pos, in the frame VesselOrbitTruth.frameRotating names.

To check element-to-position math, compare against the reported value, never a reckoned one: reckoning applies the same Kepler propagator being checked, so it agrees with itself by construction.

Fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
x number m
y number m
z number m
velocity object

Velocity in m/s relative to the body the vessel orbits, KSP's Orbit.vel, in the frame VesselOrbitTruth.frameRotating names.

Fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
x number m/s
y number m/s
z number m/s
frameRotating boolean

The reference body's CelestialBody.inverseRotation: true when VesselOrbitTruth.position and VesselOrbitTruth.velocity are in a frame co-rotating with the body, false when they are in the fixed inertial frame.

vessel.propulsion

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

The active vessel's mass and thrust, the inputs to thrust-to-weight and burn-time figures. Mass is in tonnes and thrust in kN, so thrust / (mass · g) is a thrust-to-weight ratio directly.

TWR, maximum TWR and a vessel-level burn-time estimate are derived by the client from these fields, and are not streamed here.

Payload VesselPropulsion 8 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
totalMass number t

The vessel's total mass including resources, in tonnes (KSP's Vessel.totalMass).
dryMass number t

The vessel's mass without resources, in tonnes: the sum of every part's Part.mass.
currentThrust number kN

The thrust every engine on the vessel is producing now, in kN (the sum of ModuleEngines.finalThrust). Zero when nothing is firing.
availableThrust number kN

The thrust the vessel can produce right now, in kN: the maximum thrust (ModuleEngines.GetMaxThrust) of every engine that is ignited and not flamed out. A shut-down or flamed-out engine contributes nothing, so this is not the vessel's rated maximum.
massFlow optional number | null kg/s

The propellant every running engine is drawing now, in kg/s: the sum of each ignited, unflamed engine's ModuleEngines.requestedMassFlow, scaled by the share of that request its tanks met (propellantReqMet). Zero when nothing is firing.

With VesselPropulsion.currentThrust and VesselPropulsion.totalMass this is the whole of a burn's mass budget: the vessel's mass at a later instant is the mass now less this rate over the interval, so a burn can be carried forward with its rising acceleration rather than a constant one.

Null when the engines cannot be read: an on-rails or packed craft has no running modules to sum, and a zero there would claim the engines are cold.
thrustStartedUt optional number | null ut

UT the craft's current continuous period of thrust began, or null when it is not under thrust as of the last measurable reading.

An observation instant. It says when something was seen to be true, which is a different kind of UT from a plan's ManeuverNode.Ut or an orbit's epoch, although all three carry the same unit. Subtracting this from a planned instant compiles and means nothing; measure a duration from it only against the client's own view clock.

It is repeated on every frame until it changes, not sent once when thrust starts, so a client that missed a frame still sees it.

Held, not cleared, while thrust is unmeasurable (an on-rails or packed craft has no parts to read). Otherwise switching away from a burning craft would read as its engines quitting.
lastThrustEndUt optional number | null ut

UT the craft's most recent period of thrust ended, or null when no period of thrust has been observed to end since this craft became the subject. Same observation-instant reading as VesselPropulsion.thrustStartedUt.

Set here with a null VesselPropulsion.thrustStartedUt, it says the engines ran and have stopped, which no other field can say. VesselPropulsion.currentThrust at zero reads the same for a craft that never lit, and vessel.control.throttle is where the pilot left the lever, which stays at full through a flameout, a dry tank and an unlit stage.

It does not say why the engines stopped, and no reading can. A burn paused to be re-planned and a burn abandoned produce the same instant, because the difference between them is whether the operator comes back, which has not happened yet. A consumer may report that thrust ceased with delta-v owed; it may not report a shortfall.

vessel.resources

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

What the active vessel carries, keyed by resource name, each with its current amount and capacity. Every message holds the whole map. No value is ever a sentinel such as -1.

Only these stock resources are reported: LiquidFuel, Oxidizer, SolidFuel, MonoPropellant, ElectricCharge, XenonGas, Ore and Ablator.

Absence.

  • Key absent from VesselResources.resources: structural: this vessel does not carry the resource at all (its capacity is zero). Changes only on staging/docking.
  • Key present, {current: 0, max: > 0}, carried but currently empty (a real, meaningful reading, not an error).
  • Whole channel absent: no vessel at all, the same convention as every other vessel.* channel.

Because every emission is the full map (the channel carries the whole map, never a delta), a key disappearing between two emissions is itself a real structural statement (the vessel stopped carrying that resource, e.g. a tank was staged away), never an ambiguous "did it change or did the stream just drop it".

Carries amounts only, no flow or rate: a vessel-total flow would be a number that is not the game's own.

A map keyed by KSP resource name (e.g. "LiquidFuel"): enumerate the keys rather than reaching for one you expect. Empty, never null, for a vessel carrying none of the reported resources.

vessel.target

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

The active vessel's current target only. VesselTarget.relativePosition/VesselTarget.relativeVelocity both use the one Vec3 shape.

VesselTarget.orbit reuses VesselOrbit itself (not a separate "target orbit" shape), so a client propagates a target the same way as the active vessel, at the same time. Its nested VesselTarget.meta is stamped with the same subject (the active vessel producing this sample), not the target's; VesselTarget.vesselId and VesselTarget.bodyIndex carry the target's own identity.

A null payload means nothing is targeted, the common case, never a zero-distance or zero-vector record.

The target's name as KSP gives it (ITargetable.GetName()). Empty string when none was read.

What kind of thing is targeted. Never 3 (Position).

The target's own stable id, populated when VesselTarget.kind is 0 (Vessel) (KSP's Vessel.id guid) or 4 (Part) (the owning vessel's guid). The same opaque id trackingStation.catalog' roster and SetTargetArgs.vesselId use, so a widget can hand it straight back into a re-target command with no extra lookup. Null for a body or other target; see VesselTarget.bodyIndex for the body case.

The target's trackingStation.bodies index, populated only when VesselTarget.kind is 1 (Body), matching SetTargetArgs.bodyIndex. Null for any other target, or when the body name could not be resolved against trackingStation.bodies this tick.

The target part's KSP Part.flightID: populated only when VesselTarget.kind is 4 (Part) (a docking port), scoped by VesselTarget.vesselId (which carries the owning vessel's guid in the Part case). Null for every other kind. A widget reads this pair straight off vessel.target and hands it back into SetTargetArgs.partId to re-target the same port.

Telemetry

vessel.thermal

Delivery Latest value onlyDelay After signal delaySamples ContinuousRepeats every 30 s of game time

The active vessel's thermal rollup, its hottest part, heat shield and engine. Each ratio is null when no part had a valid maximum temperature this tick, never 0, so "no valid part" and "coldest possible part" stay distinct.

The whole payload is null when the vessel has no parts at all, a different, coarser absence than an individual null ratio. For every part's temperatures rather than a rollup, see vessel.parts.

Payload VesselThermal 10 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
maxSkinTempRatio optional number | null ratio

The highest skin-temperature ratio (skinTemperature / skinMaxTemp) of any part this tick; 1 is at the limit. Not necessarily VesselThermal.hottestPart's. Null when no part had a valid (> 0) skinMaxTemp, never 0.
maxInternalTempRatio optional number | null ratio

The highest internal-temperature ratio (temperature / maxTemp) of any part this tick, which is VesselThermal.hottestPart's; 1 is at the limit. Null when no part had a valid (> 0) maxTemp, never 0.
hottestPart optional ThermalHottestPart | null

The part with the highest internal-temperature ratio. Null when no part qualified, the same condition as a null VesselThermal.maxInternalTempRatio.
heatShieldTemp optional number | null K

Hottest heat-shield part's internal temperature (K, raw: the part carrying a ModuleAblator, Part.temperature). Null when the vessel carries no ablative heat shield this tick.
heatShieldFlux optional number | null kW

The same heat shield's ablative heat flux (ModuleAblator.flux, kW). Null when the vessel carries no ablative heat shield this tick.
hottestEngineTemp optional number | null K

Internal temperature (K) of whichever part carrying a ModuleEngines or ModuleEnginesFX module has the highest internal-temperature ratio. Null when the vessel carries no engine part with a valid maxTemp this tick.
hottestEngineMaxTemp optional number | null K

That same engine part's max internal temperature (K, raw). Null under the same no-engine-parts condition as VesselThermal.hottestEngineTemp.
hottestEngineTempRatio optional number | null ratio

That same engine part's internal-temperature ratio (temperature / maxTemp). Null under the same no-engine-parts condition as VesselThermal.hottestEngineTemp.
anyEnginesOverheating optional boolean | null

True when any engine part's internal-temperature ratio is at or above 0.9. False, not null, whenever the vessel has an engine part and none crosses it; null only alongside a null VesselThermal.hottestEngineTempRatio, when no engine part with a valid maxTemp was found this tick.
meta PayloadMeta

The payload's provenance, "vessel:<guid>" for the active vessel.

vessel.control.setAxes

Takes effect after the signal delayReceipt command-accepted when delayed

Drive the held control axes of the fly-by-wire override. Takes a partial update of the held fly-by-wire override. Every field is nullable, and only the fields you set change their held value, so one axis can be driven on its own without disturbing the others.

Every value is -1..1 and analog: a value between the ends gives a proportional input (for example proportional RCS from a mapped analog stick). A value outside -1..1 is clamped rather than refused. The trims are re-applied every frame alongside the axes while the override is on, so SAS does not overwrite them.

Held values only act on the vessel while the override is on (see vessel.control.setFlyByWire); values set while it is off are held and take effect when it is turned on. The command fails when there is no active vessel or the vessel cannot currently be controlled. The applied axes read back on vessel.control.

Arguments SetControlAxesArgs 9 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
pitch optional number | null 1

Pitch input, -1..1. Null leaves the held value unchanged.
yaw optional number | null 1

Yaw input, -1..1. Null leaves the held value unchanged.
roll optional number | null 1

Roll input, -1..1. Null leaves the held value unchanged.
x optional number | null 1

Translation X input (RCS right/left), -1..1. Null leaves the held value unchanged.
y optional number | null 1

Translation Y input (RCS up/down), -1..1. Null leaves the held value unchanged.
z optional number | null 1

Translation Z input (RCS forward/back), -1..1. Null leaves the held value unchanged.
pitchTrim optional number | null 1

Pitch trim, -1..1. Null leaves the held value unchanged.
yawTrim optional number | null 1

Yaw trim, -1..1. Null leaves the held value unchanged.
rollTrim optional number | null 1

Roll trim, -1..1. Null leaves the held value unchanged.

vessel.control.setFlyByWire

Takes effect after the signal delayReceipt command-accepted when delayed

Turn the fly-by-wire override on or off. Unlike the other vessel.control.* commands this is not a one-shot actuation: KSP resets the raw control axes every physics frame, so while the override is on the mod re-applies the held axes and trims (set with vessel.control.setAxes) every frame.

Turning it on resumes the held values (0 until an axis has been set). Turning it off stops the override and resets every held axis and trim to 0, so control returns to the player and SAS with nothing left over. Turning it on fails when there is no active vessel or the vessel cannot currently be controlled; turning it off is never refused for control reasons.

Arguments SetFlyByWireArgs 1 field
FieldTypeUnitDescription
enabled boolean

true turns the override on, false turns it off and resets the held axes and trims to 0.

vessel.control.stage

Activate the next stage.

Arguments NoCommandArgs

Result CommandResult & object 6 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
success boolean

Whether the command ran. False means the game refused it, and CommandResult.errorCode says why.
errorCode optional CommandErrorCode | null

Why it was refused, null on success. On the wire this is the root's id, so every client can classify it; a refinement's own id travels beside it as CommandResult.reason.
reason optional string | null

The id of the more specific refusal, when there is one, such as example.notManaging, a kind of careerModeRequired. Absent when the refusal is a root. An id this client does not know is still a refusal of kind CommandResult.errorCode.
breach optional LimitBreach | null

The numbers behind the refusal, when the refusal has any: the cap and the count, the tier and the top tier, the price and the balance. Null on success and on every refusal that is not a comparison.

CommandResult.errorCode says which refusal it is and this holds its numbers, as in "16 of 16 active crew".

The same LimitBreach shape a declared gate carries on GateVerdict.breach, so a refusal reads the same whether it came from a gate or from the command's own handler. Omitted from the wire when null.
detail optional string | null

The refusal in the game's own words, when the game had any: the member of ClearToSaveStatus it came back with, Strategies.Strategy.CanBeActivated(out string reason)'s reason, GameVariables.GetEVALockedReason's sentence, a PreFlightTests.IPreFlightTest's GetWarningTitle(), a [Description]-tagged state member's name. Null when the refusal had nothing to quote, and then omitted from the wire, never sent as an empty string.

The text is the game's own, so it is in the game's language.

Prose for a human, never parsed: CommandResult.errorCode is the machine-readable half. The same split, and the same field name, as GateVerdict.detail.
payload optional number | null

The value the command returns; absent on a refusal.

vessel.invokePartAction

Takes effect after the signal delayReceipt command-accepted when delayed

Fire one button of one part's right-click Part Action Window, the remote-control equivalent of the player clicking it in-game.

It acts on a part aboard the craft, so it waits on the signal delay, like vessel.control.* and the robotics commands.

It has no state field, unlike the other actuation commands (see ServoSetEnabledArgs). KSP models these as buttons with no settable value, and the button's own label is what changes ("Deploy" becomes "Retract"). Read the result back from vessel.partActions.<flightId>, which reports the new set of buttons one signal delay later.

Arguments InvokePartActionArgs 2 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
partId string

The part's flight id, as a string: the same id PartActions.partId and VesselPart.id carry, so a widget sends back the id it already holds. An id that no longer resolves (the part was staged away or undocked, or the vessel unloaded) fails with "notFound" rather than doing nothing.
eventName string

The PartActionEntry.name of the button to fire (BaseEvent.name, the stable code id, never the localized PartActionEntry.label). An event name the part no longer offers fails with "modeUnavailable": the part is there but that button is not, where a missing part fails with "notFound".

vessel.target.set

Takes effect after the signal delayReceipt command-accepted when delayed

Set the active vessel's target. Takes a discriminated union, written as SetTargetArgs.kind plus the fields that kind uses. SetTargetArgs.vesselId is the stable vessel id, never an array index, and a vessel id and a body index travel in separate fields so they cannot be confused.

A request missing a field its kind needs, or with 2 (Other), fails with "notFound", as does a well-formed request that matches no live vessel, part, body or position.

Arguments SetTargetArgs 6 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
kind TargetKind

What kind of thing to target; decides which of the other fields are required.
vesselId optional string | null

The target vessel's guid. Required when SetTargetArgs.kind is 0 (Vessel), and also when it is 4 (Part), where it names the vessel that owns the target part (a part id is unique only within its vessel).
partId optional number | null

The docking port's KSP Part.flightID, looked up among the parts of the vessel named by SetTargetArgs.vesselId. Required when SetTargetArgs.kind is 4 (Part); null for every other kind.
bodyIndex optional number | null

The body's trackingStation.bodies index, the same index VesselOrbit.referenceBodyIndex uses. Required when SetTargetArgs.kind is 1 (Body), and also when it is 3 (Position), where it names the body SetTargetArgs.latitude and SetTargetArgs.longitude are measured on.
latitude optional number | null °

The target position's latitude, in degrees. Required when SetTargetArgs.kind is 3 (Position) (a surface point picked on a map, e.g. a spaceCenter.pois entry's coordinate).
longitude optional number | null °

The target position's longitude, in degrees. Required when SetTargetArgs.kind is 3 (Position).

Shared types

Types that more than one channel uses, or that a field refers to. A type that one channel alone uses is shown in that channel's card.

ActionBinding

object

One action-group binding in VesselPart.actionBindings: a single part action and the named action groups it fires with. ActionBinding.groups are the KSPActionGroup enum member names (SAS/RCS/ Brakes/Gear/Light/Abort/Stage/ Custom01...) the action's Flags bitmask decodes to (None excluded).

Fields 3 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
action string

The action's label in the part's right-click menu: BaseAction.guiName (e.g. "Toggle", "Extend Panel").
groups string[]

Named KSPActionGroup groups this action is bound to (e.g. ["SAS","Custom01"]). Never empty: an action bound to no group is not emitted. Display labels, and possibly incomplete; see ActionBinding.groupsMask.
groupsMask number

BaseAction.actionGroup's raw [Flags] bitmask, the whole of it. KspActionGroup names the bits.

A mask rather than an ordinal because KSPActionGroup is a flags enum: one action can fire with several groups. Prefer it to ActionBinding.groups, which lists only the groups this build knows by name, so a group KSP adds is missing from the names but present in the mask.

ActionGroupState

object

One custom action group: its number, its display name and its live state. Stock KSP has ten anonymous custom groups; Action Groups Extended (AGX) gives the player up to 250 groups they name themselves ("Solar Panels", "Science Bay"), so identify a group by ActionGroupState.index and label it with ActionGroupState.name, never by its position in a list.

Custom groups only. The stock singletons (SAS, RCS, Gear, Brakes, Lights, Abort) have their own VesselControl fields and their own commands (vessel.control.setGear and so on).

Fields 3 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
index number

1-based group number: the same number vessel.control.setActionGroup takes. Stock KSP: 1..10 (KSPActionGroup.Custom01..Custom10). An AGX backend may report indices up to 250. Do not assume 10 groups, nor that the indices are dense or sorted.
name string

Human display name. Stock KSP has no per-group naming, so stock groups are named "AG1".."AG10". With AGX installed, the player's own names.
state optional boolean | null

Whether the group is currently engaged. null means the backend knows this group exists (it has an index and a name) but could not read whether it is engaged: it does not mean the group is disengaged. Treating null as off draws an off toggle for a group whose state nobody knows, and toggling from that reading commands the wrong way.

AtmosphereEntry

object

A body's atmosphere, present on a BodyEntry only when the body actually has one (null otherwise, never an all-null placeholder).

Fields 5 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
depth optional number | null m

Atmosphere height, metres (CelestialBody.atmosphereDepth); null when absent.
hasOxygen optional boolean | null

Whether the atmosphere is breathable / oxygenated (CelestialBody.atmosphereContainsOxygen); null when absent.
seaLevelPressure optional number | null kPa

Sea-level pressure, kPa (CelestialBody.atmospherePressureSeaLevel); null when absent.
pressureAltitudes optional number[] | null

Altitudes of the AtmosphereEntry.pressures samples, metres above sea level, ascending from 0; null when the stream does not report a profile. Same length as AtmosphereEntry.pressures. Fixed for the session.

Spacing is chosen per body rather than fixed, because the shape varies enormously: RSS Earth's table runs to 94 km and Saturn's to 1,270 km. Points are placed so that linear interpolation of log pressure between neighbouring samples stays within about 1% of the game's curve, up to 48 points per body. Interpolate in log pressure, not linearly.

The table ends six decades below sea level, not at AtmosphereEntry.depth. Above that the game's own curve is a cubic plunging into a hard zero at the ceiling, which no interpolation in log space can follow and which carries no pressure worth stating. A consumer draws to the last sample and takes AtmosphereEntry.depth as where the air formally ends.
pressures optional number[] | null

Pressure at each AtmosphereEntry.pressureAltitudes entry, kPa, as the game's own CelestialBody.GetPressure returns it; null when the stream does not report a profile.

Sampled rather than modelled because the exponential P0·exp(-h/H) a client can build from sea-level pressure and a scale height is not what KSP evaluates, and CelestialBody has no scale-height field to build it from. A body with atmosphereUsePressureCurve set follows a tabulated curve, as stock's own atmospheres and RealAtmospheres-style packs do; against the RSS Earth curve the exponential is out by a factor of sixteen at altitude. The sampled values are correct for stock and for any planet pack.

Rounded to six significant figures. The curve path evaluates in float32 inside Unity's own AnimationCurve, so more digits would be inventing precision, and six is far below the 1% spacing tolerance.

BodyEntry

object

One celestial body in the SystemBodies tree: an explicit parent-index tree, with null rather than a numeric sentinel for any missing value. There is no eccentric anomaly field; solve it from BodyEntry.orbit at the time you need it.

Fields 18 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
name optional string | null

Body name (e.g. "Kerbin"); null when the game has not populated it.
index number

This body's position in the list, stable for the session and the key BodyEntry.parentIndex and CatalogEntry.bodyIndex refer to. Never null.
parentIndex optional number | null

Index of the body this one orbits; null only for the root star, never a sentinel like -1.
radius optional number | null m

Mean radius, metres; null when the game does not have it yet (never 0 or -1 as a stand-in).
orbit optional OrbitEntry | null

Orbital elements about the parent body; null only for the root star, which has no parent to orbit. Exact at any instant while BodyEntry.horizon is Unbounded and Analytic, so a figure computed from them alone is not a guess.
horizon PropagationHorizon

How far BodyEntry.orbit may be carried forward, and what kind of prediction that is. Never null, and the same PropagationHorizon a craft's elements carry: UntilUt is an absolute UT here exactly as it is there.

Under stock it is always Unbounded and Analytic: a body rides a fixed conic about a fixed parent, so where it is at any UT can be computed from BodyEntry.orbit, with no drift to bound.

Under an n-body physics mod a body's elements drift like a craft's: they are the conic osculating an integrated ephemeris at the sample instant, and extrapolating them past this horizon places the body where no model put it. The horizon then comes from that mod, through IBodyEphemerisHorizon, and differs from body to body.
gravParameter optional number | null m³/s²

Standard gravitational parameter μ = G·M, m³/s² (KSP CelestialBody.gravParameter). Null when the game has not populated it.
mass optional number | null kg

Body mass, kilograms (CelestialBody.Mass). Null when the game has not populated it.
surfaceGravity optional number | null g

Surface gravity in multiples of g₀ (CelestialBody.GeeASL), verbatim. Null when the game has not populated it.

This is the configured value, not a derived one: KSP computes mass and gravParameter from it (Mass = Radius² · (GeeASL · PhysicsGlobals.GravitationalAcceleration) / G), so reconstructing it as μ/r²/g₀ runs the game's arithmetic backwards and can only lose precision.
hillSphere optional number | null m

Hill-sphere radius, metres (CelestialBody.hillSphere).

Null for the root star, where KSP's own value is double.PositiveInfinity and there is no parent to be bound by.

Use this rather than computing it: KSP's expression is a·(1−e)·(m/M)^(1/3), while the textbook form carries a factor of three under the root, a·(1−e)·∛(m/3M), which comes out about 31% smaller than the game's.
sphereOfInfluence optional number | null m

Sphere-of-influence radius, metres (CelestialBody.sphereOfInfluence); null when absent.
rotationPeriod optional number | null s

Sidereal rotation period, seconds (CelestialBody.rotationPeriod); a negative value denotes retrograde rotation. Null when absent. A body rotates exactly when this is finite and non-zero; there is no separate flag.
initialRotation optional number | null °

The body's rotation angle at UT 0, degrees (CelestialBody.initialRotation); null when absent.

The phase that BodyEntry.rotationPeriod's rate is measured from, and the pair is what makes a body-fixed coordinate into a place: the angle at any UT is initialRotation + 360 · ut / rotationPeriod, and turning a latitude/longitude by it gives a position in the same frame this payload's orbital elements are measured in. The turn is about the reference +Z pole alone, so no separate spin axis is needed.

Zero is a real value, not a stand-in: a body whose prime meridian happens to face the reference direction at UT 0 reports it.
tidallyLocked optional boolean | null

Whether the body is tidally locked to its parent (CelestialBody.tidallyLocked); null when absent.
atmosphere optional AtmosphereEntry | null

Atmosphere descriptor; null when the body has no atmosphere (CelestialBody.atmosphere is false), never an all-null placeholder.
hasOcean optional boolean | null

Whether the body has a liquid ocean (CelestialBody.ocean); null when absent.
description optional string | null

KSP's per-body flavour text (CelestialBody.bodyDescription); null when absent. May be a raw, unresolved #autoLOC... localization tag, which is not text to show.
isHome optional boolean | null

Whether KSC and the launch sites sit on this body (CelestialBody.isHomeWorld); true on exactly one body, null when absent. The authoritative home-body marker: a client locates home by this flag, never by index.

At a commitment CareerStrategy.factor f the figure is initialCostReputationMin plus f times (initialCostReputationMax minus initialCostReputationMin), f held to 0..1, as KSP's Strategy.FactorLerp computes it.

How many discrete positions the commitment slider has, KSP's Strategy.FactorSliderSteps.
canActivate optional boolean | null

Whether KSP would allow this strategy to be committed to right now. null means the question could not be put at all, which is not a refusal: CareerStrategy.activateBlockedReason then says why no check could run rather than naming a rule the strategy broke.
activateBlockedReason optional string | null

KSP's own wording for the rule that refused, or an installed career mod's wording for a rule of its own, or an account of why the question could not be put when CareerStrategy.canActivate is null. Empty when activation is allowed.
activateVerdictSource optional string | null

Which route produced CareerStrategy.canActivate: "screened" when KSP's own check ran, "derived" when the same rules were checked one at a time because the Administration Building was shut, or when the strategy is already active, and "none" when there is no verdict to carry.

"derived" always accompanies a refusal and never a yes. The game stops at its first refusal, so a rule that refuses off-screen would have refused on it; but one rule counts the career's running strategies on that screen and cannot be checked anywhere else, and permission needs every rule to pass. A strategy no rule refused therefore arrives with no verdict and "none" rather than as allowed.

Never enable an activation control from a "derived" verdict: it can only refuse. Whether a strategy without a verdict may be committed is decided by career.strategy.activate itself, which runs every check again at the moment it executes and refuses in the game's words or as unreadable rather than guessing.
canDeactivate optional boolean | null

Whether KSP would allow this strategy to be ended right now, KSP's Strategy.CanBeDeactivated. false with a reason beginning "eligibility check failed: " when the check itself threw.
deactivateBlockedReason optional string | null

KSP's own wording for why the strategy cannot be ended, or the failed check described in CareerStrategy.canDeactivate. Empty or null when deactivation is allowed.
effect optional string | null

KSP's text describing what the strategy does while active, Strategy.Effect.

The universal time the place this entry gives was true at: when the vessel said it, or when the light the centre saw it by left it. Null exactly when CatalogEntry.placeSource is.

Whether this centre is in contact with the craft, as this centre knows it. Null where no word of any route to the craft has ever reached this centre, which is always the case for an object with no radio.

This is the field that answers "is this centre in contact": InContact means the craft's signal reaches this centre now. CatalogEntry.commsConnected answers a different question, whether the craft has a control link home at all, which it can have while this centre is out of its reach.
lastContactUt optional number | null ut

The universal time this centre last knows it had a link to the craft: now, while in contact. Null when it knows of none.
expectedReturnUt optional number | null ut

The universal time this centre expects to hear the silent craft again: when the ground predicts a link will reopen, plus the light-time from the craft to this centre. Null while in contact, when the ground has no prediction, and at a crewed centre, whose own line to the craft the ground's geometry does not predict.
overdueAfterUt optional number | null ut

The universal time past which the craft is overdue at this centre: CatalogEntry.expectedReturnUt and the allowance the ground gives a late return. Null exactly when CatalogEntry.expectedReturnUt is.
declaredLostUt optional number | null ut

The universal time the home centre declared the craft lost, once that declaration has reached this centre. Kept after a declaration is withdrawn, beside a CatalogEntry.contact that is no longer 3 (Lost). Null when no declaration has reached this centre.
crew optional CatalogCrew | null

What this centre knows of the craft's crew: CatalogEntry.crewCount is as of CatalogEntry.lastContactUt, and is known only while the centre is in contact. For a destroyed craft it is lost when the centre heard the end over a link and presumed lost when it only saw it. Null when the crew this centre last heard of is none or unread, and when no word of any route to the craft has reached it.
endSource optional RosterPlaceSource | null

How this centre learned the craft was destroyed: heard, from its last report over a link, or seen. A destroyed craft stays listed, with CatalogEntry.contact 4 (Gone), until the player dismisses it with trackingStation.catalog.dismiss. A recovered craft, one docked into another, and debris, flags and other objects nobody flew leave the catalog when they go. Null while this centre knows of no end.
endedUt optional number | null ut

The universal time of the report or sighting that told this centre the craft was destroyed. A centre that had no line to the craft when it went sees it gone only when its place next comes into view, so this can be later than the destruction itself. Null exactly when CatalogEntry.endSource is.

One ordered pair in the commandCentre.separation channel: how far CentreSeparationEntry.from is from CentreSeparationEntry.to, in one-way seconds along the routed CommNet path.

Both ends are command-centre ids from commandCentre.roster, so a pair is a ground station against another ground station, a crewed craft against a ground station, or two crewed craft: a crewed control-source vessel is a centre like any other.

Fields 3 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
from string

The centre the separation is measured from, as a roster Id.
to string

The centre the separation is measured to, as a roster Id.
oneWaySeconds number s

One-way signal time along the routed path between the two.

ClosestApproach

object

Next closest approach between the active vessel and its current target, computed by the orbit model in use (stock two-body Kepler by default, an n-body physics mod's when one is installed), so an n-body physics mod can supply the true encounter rather than a Kepler approximation.

Because it comes from the same provider as the trajectory, the encounter and the trajectory it lies on are always the same physics. Null on VesselTarget when there is no target, no frame the provider can reach both objects in, or no encounter inside the window it was asked about.

Fields 2 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
time number ut

Universal Time (seconds) of the minimum separation at or after the sample's UT.
distance number m

Separation (metres) at ClosestApproach.time.

CommandErrorCode

enum

The root refusals: the closed set every client can switch on. Each says what kind of refusal it was, and so whether waiting, changing the craft, or doing something in the game is what makes a retry worthwhile.

A producer that can say more names a refinement of one of these, a code written owner.name that travels beside the root's id in the reply's reason; the root still travels, so nothing a client does with a root depends on knowing the refinement.

Fields 21 values
ValueNameDescription
"noVessel" NoVessel There is no active vessel to act on.
"modeUnavailable" ModeUnavailable The requested mode or state is not available, and the game gave no more specific reason.
"range" Range An argument was out of its valid range.
"notFound" NotFound The referenced entity (a node id, a vessel or body target, a craft name) did not resolve.
"planNotOwned" PlanNotOwned The maneuver plan is owned by a trajectory planner other than the game's own, such as a mod that plans its own burns, so a node written there would never be flown. The command is refused and nothing is written. The owning planner is on the wire as the planner field of the vessel.maneuver payload.
"limitReached" LimitReached A capacity is full: the Astronaut Complex holds its cap of active crew, a facility holds its cap of anything else countable. A retry succeeds only once something changes, such as a kerbal leaving the active roster. The breach field of the reply carries the numbers, so a client can say "16 of 16".
"alreadyAtMaximum" AlreadyAtMaximum The thing is already at the top of an upgradeable scale, so there is nothing above it to move to. An example is the Launch Pad at tier 3 of 3. Not "limitReached": a cap that is full can be freed; a maximum tier cannot be exceeded by any action at all.
"insufficientFunds" InsufficientFunds The command costs more than the funds on hand. The breach field of the reply carries the cost as Actual against the balance as Limit, so the client can say how short and in the operator's own currency rendering.
"insufficientScience" InsufficientScience The command costs more science than is banked. Separate from "insufficientFunds", as the game keeps science and funds separate currencies. The cost is the one the game itself would charge, with every modifier applied.
"careerModeRequired" CareerModeRequired The save is not a career save, so this command's whole subsystem does not exist here. A permanent property of the save, not a state that may change, so a client can hide the control rather than show it refused.
"wrongScene" WrongScene The game is in a scene this command cannot run from. The detail field of the reply names the scene when the producer had one.
"wrongState" WrongState The entity is not in a state this transition applies to: an already-active strategy asked to activate, an already-researched node asked to unlock, a contract asked to accept when it is not offered, an assigned kerbal asked to be sacked, a spent experiment asked to deploy. The detail field of the reply can carry the state in the game's own words.
"notClearToProceed" NotClearToProceed Right command, wrong moment: the flight is not in a state that permits it yet, and will be later. The game gives five such reasons: in atmosphere, under acceleration, moving over the surface, about to crash, on a ladder; and a revert or a scene change can also be switched off by the save's own difficulty settings. The game's reason is on the detail field of the reply. Also returned by the command that sets a SCET alarm (an alarm on the craft's own clock, spacecraft event time) when the command centre it names as its vantage cannot be checked, because the game has not yet reported any command centre: at the main menu, and in the first moments after a save loads. The same command refuses a vantage that is known and inactive with "range" instead, because that one does not resolve by waiting. Any other command naming an inactive vantage fails with the unknownVantage fault. Distinct from "wrongState", which is about the entity and does not resolve by waiting.
"capabilityMismatch" CapabilityMismatch The part or vessel does not have the capability this command needs: a rotor asked for a target angle, an unmotorised servo asked to drive, a part with no such action, an action present but inert, an autopilot mode this craft cannot hold. Nothing an operator waits for. The craft would have to be different for this to work, which is why it is not "notClearToProceed" and not "wrongState".
"noConnection" NoConnection There is no usable link for what this command needs to send. The vessel has no antenna that can carry the payload, such as a science transmission.
"notUnlocked" NotUnlocked The capability exists in the game but this save has not unlocked it: fuel transfer, custom action groups, flight planning, EVA, the maneuver tool. Each switch follows the level of the building that owns it. Distinct from "limitReached", which is a number against a number. This is a switch that is off, and the fix is an upgrade rather than making room.
"siteOccupied" SiteOccupied Another vessel is on the launch site. The game's own words for it ride on the detail field of the reply.
"facilityDamaged" FacilityDamaged The facility this command needs is destroyed or damaged.
"insufficientResource" InsufficientResource The command consumes a countable item and there are not enough of them aboard. The command's handler decides how many are needed. This code says only that there were too few, never which item. Separate from "insufficientFunds" and "insufficientScience": a physical item cannot be bought. Not "limitReached", which is a capacity that is full. This is a store that is empty.
"unreadable" Unreadable The command's handler could not read the state it needed, so the question went unanswered. Nothing about the craft, the save or the moment was established, and the refusal is no judgement about the command. Unlike "capabilityMismatch", this says nothing about what the craft can do. Waiting does not by itself make it succeed, but sending the command again asks the question afresh, and that is the only sound next move. The detail field of the reply names what could not be read when the handler had a name for it.
"outOfReach" OutOfReach The command acts at a place, and the command centre it was sent from is not in that place's planetary system, so it has no authority there: a launch from a pad in another planet's system. This refuses the sender, not the moment, so no amount of waiting makes it succeed. Sending from a centre in the place's own system does. The detail field of the reply names the centre and the place, and the system each is in, so an operator learns which centre to send from. Distinct from "noConnection", which is a link that cannot carry the command. A centre may be perfectly linked to the place and still have no authority over it.

CommandResult

object

What every command returns. A refused command has CommandResult.success false and a typed CommandResult.errorCode saying why, so a client never matches on message text.

This is the result of a command that returns no value. A command that does returns the same fields with its value beside them, as payload on the wire.

Fields 5 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
success boolean

Whether the command ran. False means the game refused it, and CommandResult.errorCode says why.
errorCode optional CommandErrorCode | null

Why it was refused, null on success. On the wire this is the root's id, so every client can classify it; a refinement's own id travels beside it as CommandResult.reason.
reason optional string | null

The id of the more specific refusal, when there is one, such as example.notManaging, a kind of careerModeRequired. Absent when the refusal is a root. An id this client does not know is still a refusal of kind CommandResult.errorCode.
breach optional LimitBreach | null

The numbers behind the refusal, when the refusal has any: the cap and the count, the tier and the top tier, the price and the balance. Null on success and on every refusal that is not a comparison.

CommandResult.errorCode says which refusal it is and this holds its numbers, as in "16 of 16 active crew".

The same LimitBreach shape a declared gate carries on GateVerdict.breach, so a refusal reads the same whether it came from a gate or from the command's own handler. Omitted from the wire when null.
detail optional string | null

The refusal in the game's own words, when the game had any: the member of ClearToSaveStatus it came back with, Strategies.Strategy.CanBeActivated(out string reason)'s reason, GameVariables.GetEVALockedReason's sentence, a PreFlightTests.IPreFlightTest's GetWarningTitle(), a [Description]-tagged state member's name. Null when the refusal had nothing to quote, and then omitted from the wire, never sent as an empty string.

The text is the game's own, so it is in the game's language.

Prose for a human, never parsed: CommandResult.errorCode is the machine-readable half. The same split, and the same field name, as GateVerdict.detail.

Who is speaking, as the speaking client describes itself. A speaker is the screen sending a message, and a listener is a command centre in the group it is sent to. Shown to listeners and trusted for nothing else: the vantage a thing was said from, the command centre its connection works from, is always the one the mod resolved for the connection that said it, never a field here.

CommsContactPair

object

Two nodes and the windows the plan predicts contact between them.

Fields 6 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription

One end, in the commandCentre.roster vocabulary: "ground:<name>" or "vessel:<guid>".

The last instant predicted for this pair: the plan's horizon, or sooner where either end's motion cannot be trusted that far ahead.

Every window of contact up to CommsContactPair.horizonUt, in time order. Empty when none is predicted.

The stretches in which either end could turn an idle dish to the other and carry a message, in time order: the dish has no contact on its own aim then, the turned dish would close the link, and the other end could already receive. A message held at the turning node may use one; nothing else does. Empty when no dish would be turned or the backend turns none.

True while either end was last heard of with its orbit still changing. It is reckoned on the orbit it reported mid-burn, which it has since left, so these windows are a rough guide until its next report.

The degree of control a vessel currently has, the controlSource axis of CommsConnectivity. The game's control level collapsed to three tiers: partial covers both crewed and uncrewed partial control, and whether a crew is aboard shows on CommsConnectivity.hasLocalControl instead.

CommsDelaySource

enum

Why CommsDelay.oneWaySeconds has the value it has.

Fields 3 values
ValueNameDescription
0 None No delay measured: either there is no measurable path (the value is null) or delay is switched off (the value is 0).
1 SignalDelay A signal delay computed over the route's hop geometry.
2 NoCommsModel Zero, because this save models no comms network at all: the stock CommNet difficulty option is off, so there are no ground stations, no relay graph and no path to measure a signal delay over. Control reaches a craft directly, from anywhere, instantly. Not the same as a null CommsDelay.oneWaySeconds, which means there is a comms model and it can measure nothing right now: a blackout. A save with no comms model reports this alongside connected:true, and its channels keep arriving with nothing held back; a blackout reports null and they stop.

CommsHop

object

One ordered hop toward home in the active vessel's path. Per-hop RealAntennas facts are not fields on this shared shape: the forward band rate rides the RealAntennas Uplink's own realantennas.hopRates channel (a per-hop annotation keyed by these same node ids, joined onto the route client-side), and the other RealAntennas per-hop facts ride CommsHop.extensions under "realantennas".

A ground station carries its own name in CommsHop.from and CommsHop.to, not a shared "home" label, and an install with RealAntennas can have a dozen of them. Two consecutive samples that each show a one-hop direct link, one to Kourou and one to Canberra, are a handoff between stations, not one station whose range changed.

Fields 9 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
from string

The node id at the end of the hop nearer the vessel, in the same id space as CommsNetworkNode.id: a vessel's persistent id for a craft, the station's own name for a ground station.
to string

The node id at the end of the hop nearer home, in the same id space as CommsHop.from.
fromIsHome boolean

True when the CommsHop.from end is a ground station.
toIsHome boolean

True when the CommsHop.to end is a ground station.
kind CommsHopKind

0 (Home) when either end is a ground station, otherwise 1 (Relay). One value for the whole hop, so read CommsHop.fromIsHome and CommsHop.toIsHome for which end.
distanceMeters optional number | null m

Straight-line distance the signal crosses on this hop, in metres. Null when the hop's geometry is not known, never 0.
strength optional number | null ratio

What this hop's link is worth at the distance it crosses, from 0 to 1, in the comms backend's own terms (see CommsSignal). On comms.path it is worked out for this hop of the active route, from what the receiving command centre has heard of the two ends' antennas, so it is a model and not a measurement. Null when the backend states no strength for the hop, or the centre has not heard enough to work one out.
quantity optional SignalQuantity | null

Which quantity CommsHop.strength is, as the comms backend stated it for this hop. Null exactly when CommsHop.strength is.
extensions optional map of any | null

Per-hop facts the comms mod in use reports beyond this shape, keyed by that mod's name. A RealAntennas install fills Extensions["realantennas"] with band, tech level, modulation, encoder, required Eb/N0, beamwidth, EC draw and the reverse-direction rate, typed by the RealAntennas client's own RealAntennasHopExt.

On comms.path a hop carries the facts the active vessel's radio last reported of that same hop, as the receiving command centre heard them, and a report reaches a centre no sooner than light from the farthest node on the path it was measured over. A hop of the active route the centre has heard no report of carries the facts the backend works out for it, from what the centre has heard of the two ends' antennas, or none where the backend states none.

CommsOcclusionBody

object

One body's occlusion geometry, as the comms model in use resolves it. CommsOcclusionBody.index matches BodyEntry.Index on trackingStation.bodies (both are CelestialBody.flightGlobalsIndex), so a consumer joins the two without name-matching.

Both radii ride the wire: CommsOcclusionBody.radiusMeters is what the rock measures and CommsOcclusionBody.occludingRadiusMeters is what the backend treats it as. Carrying both keeps the difference visible (and the multiplier derivable) without asking any consumer to apply one.

Fields 5 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription

The body's CelestialBody.flightGlobalsIndex: the join key onto BodyEntry.Index in trackingStation.bodies.

The body's name, e.g. "Kerbin"; null when unread. Display only: join on CommsOcclusionBody.index.
radiusMeters number m

The body's own mean radius (CelestialBody.Radius). 0 when the radius has not been read yet, and then CommsOcclusionBody.occludingRadiusMeters is 0 too: the body blocks nothing.
hasAtmosphere boolean

Whether the body has an atmosphere, which selects the multiplier a scaled-radius model applies. false when unread.
occludingRadiusMeters number m

What the comms model in use treats as blocking a radio path through this body.

The kinds of reference frame a control frame can be: the five frame types an n-body physics mod offers, plus 0 (Unspecified).

Per-flight statistics accumulated across the whole flight up to the crash, CrashReport.flightStats. Maxima and distances are sampled from the active vessel at the telemetry cadence, so they are approximate, and since the flight was last loaded: a quickload or a revert starts them again. A vessel that was never sampled, such as one that crashed while another was flown, reports null for every accumulated value; its mission time and lift-off are read at the crash.

How the flight ended. Always "CATASTROPHIC_FAILURE" on a crash record.

The highest surface speed (Vessel.srfSpeed) reached while not splashed down, in m/s. Flight over water counts; only samples taken while splashed are excluded.

Whether the mission has ended. Always true on a crash record.

The highest g-force (Vessel.geeForce) sampled during the flight, in g.

The highest altitude above sea level (Vessel.altitude) sampled during the flight, in metres.

Distance travelled relative to the surface, in metres: surface speed integrated over UT between samples. A gap of more than 10 s between samples (a warp jump, a quickload) is skipped rather than integrated.

Mission time (seconds since launch) at the crash, Vessel.missionTime read as it was destroyed.
highestSpeed optional number | null m/s

The highest surface speed (Vessel.srfSpeed) sampled during the flight, in m/s.

Horizontal distance travelled over the surface, in metres: horizontal surface speed integrated over UT between samples, with the same 10 s gap rule as CrashFlightStats.totalDistance.

true once the vessel's mission clock has started, i.e. it has left the launch site, as read at the crash.

What a kerbal's place on the books is, as the dashboard means it: this contract's own vocabulary, not a mirror of any game enum.

The roster-status members line up with KspRosterStatus in meaning but not in numbering, so never cast one to the other. 1 (Applicant) is a standing KSP expresses as a KerbalType rather than a RosterStatus, and it sits in one enumeration with the rest so "what is this kerbal's standing" is one value.

Behind spaceCenter.crewRoster[].standing, and it is the field to branch on; see CrewRosterEntry.situationOrdinal for what the raw KSP ordinal beside it is still good for.

Order. The numbering is the reading order: sorted by value, a crew list reads free to fly, then committed, then off the books. A new member is inserted at its place in that order rather than appended, so a member's number can change between versions: never store or compare a raw number, compare members by name through the generated enum.

6 Missing Missing: KSP's own Missing roster status, kept separate from 5 (Dead).

FaultCode

enum

Why a command, or any other request, could not be carried: nothing about the game was decided. The refused/failed split is the kind of code, not a judgement a client makes: a refusal (CommandErrorCode) says the game said no, this says the machinery did not get that far, and a retry may work.

Closed, and declared only here: the error codes an Uplink adds are refusals, refinements of a CommandErrorCode root, never faults.

A command that was sent and never answered is neither a refusal nor one of these: no answer ever comes.

Fields 23 values
ValueNameDescription
"invalidEnvelope" InvalidEnvelope A frame of a known type that could not be read, including a command-request whose args do not fit the command. Only that call is refused; the command stays available.
"unknownEnvelopeType" UnknownEnvelopeType A frame whose type this build does not recognise.
"unhandledEnvelope" UnhandledEnvelope A frame that parsed as a type this build has nothing to do with.
"binaryFrameNotAccepted" BinaryFrameNotAccepted A binary frame sent up the socket, which nothing accepts.
"commandUnavailable" CommandUnavailable A command that is unknown or unavailable, or whose handler threw. A handler that threw leaves its command unavailable for the session.
"mainThreadTimeout" MainThreadTimeout A command the host could not run in time: it was handed to the game's main thread and the game did not take it before the host stopped waiting, as during a scene load. Nothing was decided, and the command may still run later.
"resultSerializationError" ResultSerializationError A command that ran and whose result could not be written.
"unknownTopic" UnknownTopic A subscription to a topic nothing declares.
"payloadSerializationError" PayloadSerializationError A topic whose payload could not be written.
"unknownVantage" UnknownVantage A set-vantage, or a command's vantage, naming a command centre that is not active. A vantage is the command centre a view is taken from or a command is sent from. The command that sets a SCET alarm (an alarm on the craft's own clock, spacecraft event time) is the exception: it refuses an inactive vantage with the range refusal instead.
"commandExpired" CommandExpired A held command reached its expiry, or its place on the lane passed, before it could run. A lane is the numbered sequence of commands to one craft, which the craft settles in number order.
"replyNotReceived" ReplyNotReceived No reply came home before the centre gave the command up: it left, and nothing was heard from the craft, a relay or a report in all the time one could have taken. The command may have run, and its answer may be waiting at a craft that has no link home; the centre cannot tell which.
"groupRefused" GroupRefused A command sent in a group was not sent because another command in the same group was refused, or because the group itself could not be sent. A group goes whole or not at all, so every member is refused with this one, and the message names the member that decided it.
"groupStopped" GroupStopped A command sent in a group did not run because an earlier command in the same group failed at the craft. The earlier commands stay done, since a game action cannot be taken back; the message says which ran.
"commandCancelled" CommandCancelled A cancel stopped the command before it ran.
"undoneByLoad" UndoneByLoad A game load started a new timeline while the command was on its way, and the save it loaded does not carry the command, so it will not run. A quickload to before the command was sent is the common case. A command the loaded save does carry stays on its way and is answered as usual.
"continuousInputWouldWait" ContinuousInputWouldWait A continuous input, a throttle or a control axis, was dropped at a node, a ground station or relay on the route to the craft, because the link onward was down there and it would have had to be held until it came back. Held and sent on later it would arrive as a run of out-of-date values, so a node that cannot send it on at once drops it. It was accepted with a warning when it was sent, and this is the news of its loss, arriving at the command centre that sent it once a report from that node could have reached it at light speed.
"undelivered" Undelivered The transport held the command for a link that never came back, and has stopped retrying. It never left this machine.
"disposed" Disposed The client was shut down while the command waited for an answer.
"sendQueueFull" SendQueueFull The transport's queue of commands waiting for a link is full, so this one was not queued.
"peerDisconnected" PeerDisconnected A station's link to the main screen dropped while the command was on it.
"noClient" NoClient The main screen had no connection to the mod to relay a station's command over.
"unclassified" Unclassified A rejection that carried no code a client could read, such as a throw from inside a handler on the client.

GateOutcome

enum

What a command gate concluded about one precondition: passed, failed, could not be decided from the arguments supplied, or could not be decided from the game's state.

Fields 4 values
ValueNameDescription
0 Pass Nothing blocks this.
1 Fail Blocked, with the comparison that says why.
2 Abstain Cannot be decided from the arguments supplied, because one it needs is missing. Not a refusal: a client that treats this as blocked disables every argument-dependent control permanently.
3 Unknown Decidable in principle, but the live state needed is missing, e.g. a facility KSP does not track under the name declared. Distinct from 2 (Abstain) because nothing further the caller supplies will resolve it, and distinct from 0 (Pass) because an unreadable limit is not the same as no limit.

InboundFrame

StreamData | StreamBinary | EventMsg | CommandResponse | CommandAccepted | ErrorMsg | Hello | GameState | Pong

Every frame the mod sends, told apart by type.

  • stream-data: a subscribed topic's value
  • stream-binary: a subscribed topic's value as raw bytes, for a channel that uses the binary lane
  • event: something that happened to a subscription
  • command-response: the result of a command
  • command-accepted: the receipt for a delayed command, sent before its result
  • error: a request the mod refused or could not read
  • hello: the first frame on every connection
  • game-state: what the game is doing: loading, ready or no game
  • pong: the answer to a ping

Each one fixes type to a constant, so a JSON Schema validator selects the right one from type alone. The discriminator beside this is the AsyncAPI Schema keyword, a plain string naming that property. It is not OpenAPI 3's discriminator object, so propertyName and mapping do not apply here. stream-binary is described by its JSON header; see the document description for the bytes that follow it.
