ManeuverFrame

enum

The basis a planned burn's delta-v components are expressed in. Read this before interpreting a burn vector: a basis this contract does not recognise gives components that cannot be labelled.

Fields 2 values
ValueNameDescription
0 RadialNormalPrograde KSP's own maneuver-node basis: radial-out, normal, prograde, taken against the patch the node sits on at its own UT.
1 Unknown A frame this contract does not recognise.

ManeuverNode

object

One planned burn: named delta-v components in a named frame (ManeuverNode.frame), with the burn's impulsive instant and, when a burn time is modelled, its start and end.

ManeuverNode.ut is the impulsive instant a stock node has; ManeuverNode.ignitionUt and ManeuverNode.cutoffUt are the finite burn's start and end. When no burn time is modelled those two are absent, never equal to each other or to ManeuverNode.ut: an absent duration means "not modelled", while a zero duration with a thrust would mean infinite acceleration.

Fields 10 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
id string

Stable, opaque id: the nodeId that vessel.maneuver.update and vessel.maneuver.remove take. It round-trips into those commands whether the node was created through vessel.maneuver.add or placed by hand in the map view. A live capture always carries one; the empty string appears only on a node replayed from a recording that carries no ids.
ut number ut

The instant of the burn's impulsive equivalent: the one instant a zero-duration model has, in UT seconds. Stock's ManeuverNode.UT is exactly this.

It is not the ignition time: a finite burn starts before this and ends after it. ManeuverNode.ignitionUt and ManeuverNode.cutoffUt carry those two instants directly, so there is no "UT minus half the burn time" convention to guess.
ignitionUt optional number | null ut

When the engines light, in UT seconds, or null when nothing supplies a burn-duration model for this craft.

Null is a real reading, not a failure. Stock computes a burn time only for a loaded vessel, so a queued burn on an unloaded craft has no ignition time rather than a guessed one.

Never set equal to ManeuverNode.ut as a stand-in, so "when to light the engines is not known" stays distinct from "this burn is instantaneous".
cutoffUt optional number | null ut

When the engines cut, in UT seconds, or null on the same terms as ManeuverNode.ignitionUt. Burn duration is CutoffUt - IgnitionUt; there is no separate duration field.

Not in general Ut plus half the duration: that symmetry holds only while the craft's mass is constant, and a long burn changes it.
frame optional ManeuverFrame | null

The basis ManeuverNode.dvRadial/ManeuverNode.dvNormal/ ManeuverNode.dvPrograde are expressed in. Null only on a node replayed from a recording that does not carry it, on the same terms as ManeuverNode.id. Do not read null as the stock basis.
dvRadial optional number | null m/s

First delta-v component in ManeuverNode.frame's basis, in m/s (radial under the stock basis). Null only if KSP's own dv component was non-finite (NaN/Infinity) this tick; the node is still sent, never dropped because one component came back bad.
dvNormal optional number | null m/s

Second delta-v component in ManeuverNode.frame's basis (normal). Null only if KSP's own dv component was non-finite this tick, as for ManeuverNode.dvRadial.
dvPrograde optional number | null m/s

Third delta-v component in ManeuverNode.frame's basis (prograde under the stock basis). Null only if KSP's own dv component was non-finite this tick, as for ManeuverNode.dvRadial.
dvTotal optional number | null m/s

Magnitude of the burn's delta-v, in m/s. Null only if KSP's own dv magnitude was non-finite this tick, as for ManeuverNode.dvRadial.
patches OrbitPatch[]

This node's post-burn patch chain: element 0 is the orbit the vessel is on immediately after the burn (KSP's own ManeuverNode.nextPatch), followed by any later SOI-transition patches, built the same way as VesselOrbit.patches but starting from the node's own nextPatch. Always an array, never null: empty when the solver has not produced a post-burn patch yet (a just-added node mid-tick).

How one burn links to the next. A burn's input trajectory is the patch in the previous burn's chain whose PatchEndTransition is 4 (Maneuver), equivalently the one whose EndUt equals this burn's ManeuverNode.ut. For the first burn it is the craft's own vessel.orbit. Every chain is a suffix of the previous one, but the number of patches skipped varies with how many SOI crossings fall between the two burns, so counting positions is not the rule and gets it wrong the first time a crossing appears.

KSP re-parents strictly sequentially: inserting a burn ahead of an existing one re-derives every later chain, so a burn's input is always the previous burn's result.

Patched conics only. A stock plan is a sequence of conics joined at SOI boundaries. A planner that integrates has no such boundaries and leaves this empty while still describing a valid burn, so an empty chain is never a malformed node.

Meta

object

The envelope every stream sample, event and command reply carries: where it was observed from, when it was true in the game, when it was delivered, and how current it is.

Fields 11 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
source string

The node the sample was read from.
validAt number ut

When the payload was true in the game, in seconds of KSP universal time, the same base every *Ut field on every payload uses. This is the instant a reading is "as of", and the one a client compares against the current UT to decide currency.
seq number

A number that rises by one with every frame the mod sends.
deliveredAt number ut

When the mod handed the message to the transport, in the same universal time seconds as Meta.validAt. The two differ by the signal delay the vantage is under, so subtracting one from the other is how old the payload was when it arrived, and they are equal on a zero-delay link.
vantage string

The place the payload was observed from: a commandCentre.roster id, "meta" for an instant-class topic no distance applies to, or empty when the connection is at no command centre because none is active.
quality optional Quality | null

Whether the payload's subject is under physics: 1 (Loaded) while KSP simulates the craft, when its orbital elements are osculating and a conic cannot be advanced from them, and 0 (OnRails) while it coasts. Copied from the payload's own meta.quality, which only vessel.orbit states; absent from the wire on every other Topic.
active boolean

Always true on a frame the mod sends.
staleness Staleness

How current the sample is.
timelineEpoch number

Generation counter for the current timeline: 0 when the mod starts, incremented once for every quickload or rewind. Carried on every envelope, streams and command responses alike, so a sample from an abandoned pre-rewind timeline can be told apart. A client compares it against its own last-seen epoch to detect a rewind, rather than inferring one from a backward validAt jump, which a reordered or coalesced delivery could mask.
gapSinceUt optional number | null ut

The Meta.validAt of the last sample on this topic that precedes a known break in the record, set only on the first sample delivered after that break and null on every other sample.

Non-null is a positive claim, not an absence: data existed between this universal time and the carrying sample's own Meta.validAt, and it is gone. Two things produce one. A blackout recording that overran its storage bound had its oldest span dropped, so the replay resumes mid-hole. A channel that does not record at all (a session fact, never aboard the craft: see ChannelDeclaration.Recordable) has no replay, so its first post-blackout sample carries the whole outage as the gap.

A client draws it as a break rather than joining across it: a line interpolated through an outage looks like data. Omitted from the wire when there is no gap, as Meta.quality is when unstated.
sampleId optional number | null

Which recorded sample the payload is. Every delivery of one sample carries the same number, including the copy sent again when a client subscribes or resubscribes, and two samples recorded on one node never share one, even with the same instant and an identical payload. A client tells a repeated delivery from a repeated event by it: two frames with equal Meta.timelineEpoch and Meta.sampleId are the same sample.

Set on every stream-data frame and binary frame header, and omitted from the wire on events and command replies, which are not recorded samples. Unrelated to Meta.seq, which numbers frames rather than samples.

OrbitEntry

object

A body's Keplerian orbital elements, present on every BodyEntry except the root star. Each element is independently null when its value is absent or non-finite, never a NaN token on the wire. Every orbit has a defined node and periapsis, an equatorial or circular one included, so a null OrbitEntry.lan or OrbitEntry.argPe is a genuine absence and never stands for either shape.

Units follow KSP's own, which are mixed: OrbitEntry.sma in metres; OrbitEntry.inc, OrbitEntry.lan and OrbitEntry.argPe in degrees; OrbitEntry.meanAnomalyAtEpoch in radians; OrbitEntry.epoch in UT seconds. There is no eccentric anomaly field (see BodyEntry).

OrbitPatch

object

One conic segment of a vessel's future trajectory, a patched-conic "patch" in KSP's own sense (Orbit.nextPatch/previousPatch). A patch carries everything needed to propagate and draw it with no trackingStation.bodies join: its Keplerian elements, KSP's own already-computed shape fields (OrbitPatch.peA, OrbitPatch.apA, OrbitPatch.semiLatusRectum, OrbitPatch.semiMinorAxis), its body's gravitational parameter (OrbitPatch.mu) and the transitions at each end.

Bodies are carried twice. OrbitPatch.referenceBodyIndex and OrbitPatch.closestEncounterBodyIndex are the identity, the trackingStation.bodies index every other body reference in this contract uses (VesselOrbit.referenceBodyIndex among them). OrbitPatch.referenceBody and OrbitPatch.closestEncounterBody are the body's name, for display.

OrbitPatch.lan, OrbitPatch.argPe and OrbitPatch.meanAnomalyAtEpoch are null when KSP's value for them is undefined, as VesselOrbit.lan and VesselOrbit.argPe are, and the patch is still sent. A patch with a null element cannot be propagated, so a client that propagates one declines to, and does not substitute a value.

An open patch (OrbitPatch.ecc of 1 or more) is sent like any other, with OrbitPatch.period and OrbitPatch.apA null. Its mean motion is sqrt(Mu / |Sma|^3).

Fields 21 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription

Semi-major axis in metres, KSP's Orbit.semiMajorAxis. Negative on an open patch.

Eccentricity, KSP's Orbit.eccentricity: below 1 for a closed patch, 1 or more for an open one, as on a flyby or an escape.

Inclination in degrees, KSP's Orbit.inclination.

Longitude of the ascending node in degrees, KSP's Orbit.LAN. Null when KSP's value is undefined (NaN).

Argument of periapsis in degrees, KSP's Orbit.argumentOfPeriapsis. Null when KSP's value is undefined (NaN).

Mean anomaly at OrbitPatch.epoch in radians, KSP's Orbit.meanAnomalyAtEpoch. Null when KSP's value is undefined (NaN).
epoch number ut

The universal time at which OrbitPatch.meanAnomalyAtEpoch holds, KSP's Orbit.epoch.
period optional number | null s

Orbital period in seconds, KSP's Orbit.period. Null on an open patch (OrbitPatch.ecc of 1 or more), which has no period; always finite and positive on a closed one.
startUt number ut

Universal time at which the trajectory enters this patch, KSP's Orbit.StartUT.
endUt number ut

Universal time at which the trajectory leaves this patch, KSP's Orbit.EndUT.
patchStartTransition TransitionType

How the trajectory enters this patch, KSP's Orbit.patchStartTransition.

How the trajectory leaves this patch, KSP's Orbit.patchEndTransition. 1 (Final) when it does not leave it.
peA number m

Periapsis altitude above OrbitPatch.referenceBody's mean radius in metres, KSP's Orbit.PeA.
apA optional number | null m

Apoapsis altitude above OrbitPatch.referenceBody's mean radius in metres, KSP's Orbit.ApA. Null on an open patch (OrbitPatch.ecc of 1 or more), which has no apoapsis.

Semi-latus rectum in metres, KSP's Orbit.semiLatusRectum.

Semi-minor axis in metres, KSP's Orbit.semiMinorAxis.

Name of the body this patch orbits, as trackingStation.bodies names it. For display; OrbitPatch.referenceBodyIndex is the identity.

Name of the body this patch's trajectory most closely encounters, KSP's Orbit.closestEncounterBody; null when there is none. For display; OrbitPatch.closestEncounterBodyIndex is the identity.

Parent body's standard gravitational parameter (GM), read off the same body the elements are relative to, so a patch can be propagated from what it carries, as VesselOrbit.mu does for a vessel's own orbit.

Null only on a patch read off a recording that does not carry it, on the same terms as ManeuverNode.id. Never 0.

Body this patch orbits, as its trackingStation.bodies index (KSP's CelestialBody.flightGlobalsIndex). This is the identity, where OrbitPatch.referenceBody is the display name, and it is the key every other body reference in this contract uses (VesselOrbit.referenceBodyIndex, VesselTarget, TargetAvailable, VesselIdentity.ParentBodyIndex).

Null only on a patch read off a recording that does not carry it, as for OrbitPatch.mu. 0 is a real index (the star), so null is the only absent value.

PhysicsMode

enum

The active vessel's physics-simulation regime, derived from KSP's own Vessel.loaded and Vessel.packed flags. It is a discrete enum in its own right, not a quality band on OrbitPayloadMeta.quality. A widget that switches propagation or dead-reckoning strategy reads it to know whether the craft is on-rails conics, a packed cluster, or a fully physics-simulated vessel.

Mapping:

  • !loaded ⇒ 0 (OnRails): the vessel is unloaded, its motion is pure on-rails conic propagation, no PhysX at all.
  • loaded && packed ⇒ 1 (Packed): loaded into the scene but still packed (rails-following near the active vessel, not yet unpacked into full physics).
  • loaded && !packed ⇒ 2 (Unpacked): fully physics-simulated (off-rails).

3 (Unknown) covers a raw value this contract does not recognise (same convention as SasMode and VesselType).

Fields 4 values
ValueNameDescription
0 OnRails Not loaded: pure on-rails conic propagation, no physics simulation.
1 Packed Loaded into the scene but still packed, following rails near the active vessel.
2 Unpacked Loaded and unpacked: fully physics-simulated, off rails.
3 Unknown A raw value this contract does not recognise.

PropagationCertification

enum

Whether a caller accepts a result past the span the provider vouches for. It chooses certification, not which model runs: both values get the same model from the same provider.

0 (Unspecified) is zero and means nothing was chosen, so a default value never grants the permissive setting.

Fields 3 values
ValueNameDescription
0 Unspecified Nothing was chosen. A request carrying this is refused rather than given a default.
1 Unbounded Return a result wherever the solver can reach, past any horizon. For a planning search, such as a transfer grid, which asks a two-body question about future instants on purpose.
2 CertifiedOnly Return results only across spans the provider vouches for, and decline past them. For an operational prediction, such as when a link will be reacquired, where a time read off an unvouched arc would look certain without being so.

PropagationDepartureKnot

object

The largest distance the published conic may be from the path anywhere between the sample instant and PropagationDepartureKnot.untilUt.

Each knot is a running maximum, so reading the list as a step function is a cap at every instant even though the drift itself is not monotonic.

Fields 3 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
untilUt number ut

The last UT this knot covers.
metres number m

The largest position drift up to PropagationDepartureKnot.untilUt, in metres.
metresPerSecond number m/s

The largest velocity drift up to PropagationDepartureKnot.untilUt, in m/s.

PropagationHorizon

object

The window over which an element set is authoritative, as stated by whichever propagation provider produced it.

Measured from the sample's observation instant, not from VesselOrbit.epoch. Epoch is the mean-anomaly reference epoch and can sit far from when the sample was taken.

Fields 4 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
kind PropagationHorizonKind

How far the elements may be carried forward. When 2 (Until), PropagationHorizon.untilUt says where the window ends.
trajectoryKind TrajectoryKind

What kind of trajectory these elements describe: a conic that is the path, or a snapshot of an integrated one.

The horizon says how far a client may extrapolate; this says whether a conic is the right renderer at all, and the one cannot be inferred from the other. An analytic provider reports 1 (Unbounded), and so may an integrating provider where perturbations are small and the horizon is genuinely long. A client that reasons "unbounded, therefore analytic" draws a closed conic for an integrated trajectory: right at the sample instant, wrong as a path.

To identify the provider for diagnostics, read system.uplinks, which carries each Uplink's id, version and availability.
untilUt optional number | null ut

The last UT these elements are authoritative for. Set if and only if PropagationHorizon.kind is 2 (Until); null otherwise, never a sentinel standing in for "forever".
departure optional PropagationDepartureKnot[] | null

How far the published conic may be from the path, at most, ahead of the sample instant: a step function of knots in ascending PropagationDepartureKnot.untilUt. A client at some UT takes the first knot whose UntilUt is at or after it.

Null when the provider stated no error, in which case no interval is drawn about the conic. It is never an empty list and never zeros standing in for "not stated". Set only when PropagationHorizon.kind is 2 (Until), and the last knot's UntilUt then equals PropagationHorizon.untilUt.

PropagationHorizonKind

enum

How far an element set may be carried forward.

0 (Unspecified) is 0, so a producer that does not set the horizon gets the refusing value rather than the permissive one.

1 (Unbounded) is a claim, made by a provider that genuinely has no limit (an analytic two-body solver). It is its own value rather than an infinite PropagationHorizon.untilUt, so "forever" never has to be recognised as an extreme number.

Fields 3 values
ValueNameDescription
0 Unspecified No provider stated one. Treat as unpropagatable.
1 Unbounded Authoritative for all future UT: an analytic solver with no horizon.
2 Until Authoritative until PropagationHorizon.untilUt.

Which kind of condition this is, and so which of the other fields carry meaning. The rest are left at their defaults and ignored.

The instant the alarm is set for, as a universal time on the craft's clock rather than on the clock the command centre is reading. For a 3 (TopicInstant) it is the instant the simulation last read from the Topic, written by it and ignored on arm.

The difference between the two is the one-way signal delay, which changes as the craft moves. This field is the instant itself, compared against the game's own clock every tick, so it stays right however the distance changes between setting the alarm and its firing.

A Topic and a path into it address a reading the way the wire does, so an operator can point at a value they can already see on screen.
fieldPath string

Threshold and topic instant: the dotted path to the value inside ScetAlarmCondition.topic's payload ("altitudeAsl", "relativePosition.x"). Empty addresses the payload itself, which is never a number, so it never matches.
op ScetAlarmThresholdOp

Threshold only: how the reading is compared to ScetAlarmCondition.threshold.
threshold number

Threshold only: the number the operator chose, in whatever unit ScetAlarmCondition.fieldPath is published in.

It has no unit of its own: the same field is metres for one alarm and kilonewtons for the next. To render it, use the unit of the field it names, from that channel's schema.
sustainSeconds number s

Threshold and contract parameter: how long the condition must hold, in seconds, before the alarm fires. Zero fires on the first reading that matches.

Warp is stopped at the first match, not at the fire. A condition that matches once and then stops matching has therefore still stopped the warp.
contractId string

Contract parameter only: the contract's id, as career.status.contracts.active carries it.
parameterTitle string

Contract parameter only: the objective's title within that contract, matched exactly. The first objective with the title is the one watched.
targetState KspParameterState

Contract parameter only: the state the objective must reach.

ScetAlarmConditionKind

enum

Which kind of condition a SCET alarm watches for.

Every alarm has a vantage (see ScetAlarm.vantage), so a kind says only what is watched. A threshold follows a dotted path to a number; a contract parameter, which sits in a list no path can index, finds its contract and objective by id and title.

Fields 4 values
ValueNameDescription
0 Time An instant on the craft's own clock, as a universal time.
1 Threshold A value aboard the craft crossing a number the operator chose, compared against the reading the game actually holds rather than against the one the command centre has been told. Only the game can check this. A time alarm needs only a clock, which a client has; a threshold needs the craft's true state, which reaches the ground a signal delay late and by then no longer says whether the craft is above 100 km now.
2 ContractParameter One objective of one contract reaching a state the operator chose, as career.status.contracts reports it. Level rather than edge, like the threshold: an objective already in its target state when the alarm is set is a condition that holds. An objective that finishes its contract, completing or failing it, is read from the recently completed or failed contracts, so it still comes due. A contract that finished with the objective in another state, or that left the career any other way, makes the alarm 2 (Unreachable).
3 TopicInstant A Topic's own universal time, followed as it moves: the warp stops ScetAlarmCondition.leadSeconds before the instant the Topic currently publishes and the alarm fires when the clock reaches it. The instant is read again on every tick, so an alarm on "the next project to finish" re-aims by itself when a shorter project overtakes the one it was following, with nobody watching and no client to re-arm it. While the field is absent or null the condition is unmet and the alarm stays armed. Always judged on the craft's own clock, at the subject's vantage.

ScetAlarmState

enum

Where a SCET alarm has got to.

1 (Fired) is reached once and stays: an alarm whose condition keeps holding does not stop the warp again.

Fields 4 values
ValueNameDescription
0 Armed Watching. The condition has not been met.
1 Fired The condition was met, warp was stopped, and the notice went out.
2 Unreachable The condition can never be met: the craft a threshold or a followed instant watches no longer exists, or a contract objective's contract finished with it in another state or left the career. A time condition never reaches this: it has no subject to lose, because universal time belongs to the game. Show such a row as dead rather than as pending.
3 Cancelled The player switched to a different craft before the alarm came due, so it will never fire. An alarm belongs to the craft being flown when it was set, whatever its condition reads, and a switch ends every alarm still watching. A kerbal on EVA counts as the craft they stepped out of.

ScetAlarmThresholdOp

enum

How a threshold condition compares the reading to the operator's number.

The same six the client's own alarm list offers, so an alarm set on the command vantage and the same alarm set on the craft's clock mean the same thing and can be checked against each other at zero delay.

Fields 6 values
ValueNameDescription
0 GreaterThan Reading is greater than the threshold.
1 GreaterThanOrEqual Reading is greater than or equal to the threshold.
2 LessThan Reading is less than the threshold.
3 LessThanOrEqual Reading is less than or equal to the threshold.
4 Equal Reading equals the threshold exactly. Rarely what is wanted on a continuous value: readings are samples, and under warp they are thousands of game-seconds apart, so a craft can pass straight through the value without one landing on it. An inequality is almost always the condition an operator means.
5 NotEqual Reading differs from the threshold. The inverse of 4 (Equal), and just as much a knife edge on anything continuous.

ScienceTransmission

object

A science result the craft has started sending home, as science.experiment.transmit returns it: when the stream began at the craft and how long the transmitter needs to send all of it. The result has left the craft at ScienceTransmission.startedAt plus ScienceTransmission.streamSeconds, and it lands one signal delay after that.

Absent from the reply when the backend cannot say, as a modelling mod that drains results continuously cannot. A client then has nothing to draw the transmission from, which is the truth: an absent transmission is never a zero-length one.

Fields 5 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
subjectId string

The research subject's id (ScienceSubject.id), the same key currency.<guid>.science credits it under.
title string

The result's human title, e.g. "Crew Report from Kerbin's Shores".
startedAt number ut

Universal Time at the craft when the transmitter was handed the result.
streamSeconds number s

How long the transmitter takes to send every packet, from its packet size and interval. It takes at least this long: a transmitter starved of charge holds between packets, and one already busy sends this after what it is holding.
dataAmount number Mit

The amount of data sent.

ServoSetEnabledArgs

object

Switch a robotics servo or rotor motor or lock on or off. Args shared by every robotics boolean actuation (robotics.servo.setMotor/setLock and robotics.rotor.setMotor/setLock): an absolute state to apply, never a toggle, like every other actuation command (see SetEnabledArgs). Keyed by ServoSetEnabledArgs.partId, the flightID string parts.robotics publishes.

The part's flight id, as a string: the id each parts.robotics entry carries.
enabled boolean

The state to apply: for setMotor, true engages the part's motor and false disengages it; for setLock, true locks the part and false unlocks it. setMotor on a servo with no motor fails with "capabilityMismatch".

SetEnabledArgs

object

Switch SAS, RCS, landing gear, brakes, lights, the abort group or precision control on or off. Args shared by every plain on/off actuation command (setSas, setRcs, setGear, setBrakes, setLights, setAbort, setPrecisionControl): an absolute state to apply, never a toggle. Under signal delay a toggle that arrives after unknown intervening changes would race them, so there are no toggle commands.

Fields 1 field
FieldTypeUnitDescription
enabled boolean

true to switch the system on (or fire abort), false to switch it off.

SettingsPersistence

object

Whether the settings file holds what is in force.

Fields 4 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
state SettingsPersistenceState

Where the settings in force stand against the file.

The path of the settings file on the KSP machine.

The UT of the last save that wrote the file, or null when none has this session.
reason optional string | null

SettingsPersistenceState

enum

Where the settings in force stand against the settings file.

Fields 5 values
ValueNameDescription
0 Saved The file holds these values: it was read at start-up, or the last save wrote it.
1 MemoryOnly The last save could not write the file. The values are in force for this session only and revert when KSP restarts; SettingsPersistence.reason says why.
2 Recovered The file was missing, empty or damaged at start-up, and its backup was read instead. Anything saved after that backup was taken is lost. Clears at the next successful save.
3 Defaults No settings file exists yet: a first run, every setting at its default until the first save.
4 Unreadable A settings file exists but neither it nor a backup could be read, so every setting is at its default. Clears at the next successful save, which replaces the unreadable file.

SignalQuantity

enum

Which quantity a signal strength from 0 to 1 is. Two backends that both report "0 to 1" are not saying the same thing, and a figure is only comparable with another of the same quantity.

Fields 4 values
ValueNameDescription
0 Unknown Nothing says which: the hops of a worked-out path disagree, or a read failed.
1 RangeFraction KSP's signal strength for the path, the figure the game's own signal readout shows: each link's strength falls off smoothly towards the edge of its range, and a path's is the product of its links', so relays compound. Stock CommNet's. Not the share of range left: a link with 59% of its range left reads about 63%.
2 DataRateHeadroom How far up its data-rate ladder the path's links close: 1 at the top rate, one rung less for each halving of the data rate, 0 where a link does not close, multiplied across the path's links. RealAntennas'.
3 NoModel The save models no comms network, so there is no link to grade and the strength is null.

Situation

enum

A vessel's flight situation, KSP's Vessel.situation (the Vessel.Situations enum) in this contract's PascalCase spelling. 8 (Unknown) stands for a value this contract does not recognise, such as a situation added by a later KSP version.

Fields 9 values
ValueNameDescription
0 Landed Resting on the surface of a body (KSP LANDED).
1 Splashed Floating on water (KSP SPLASHED).
2 PreLaunch On the launch pad or runway and not yet launched (KSP PRELAUNCH).
3 Orbiting In a closed orbit that does not intersect the surface or atmosphere (KSP ORBITING).
4 Escaping On a trajectory that leaves the current body's sphere of influence (KSP ESCAPING).
5 Flying In the atmosphere and off the ground (KSP FLYING).
6 SubOrbital Above the atmosphere on a trajectory that meets the surface or atmosphere again (KSP SUB_ORBITAL).
7 Docked Docked to another vessel (KSP DOCKED).
8 Unknown A situation this contract does not recognise.

Staleness

enum

How current a delivered sample is, as the mod knows it (a client infers the rest from its own heartbeat tracking).

0 (Fresh) is a sample delivered on its own schedule. 1 (Held) and 2 (LastBeforeBlackout) are catch-up grades for a late or reconnecting subscriber. 3 (Recorded) is different in kind from all three: the sample is exact as of its own Meta.validAt, it simply did not travel at the time it was taken. It was held aboard through a loss of signal and dumped on acquisition, so it arrives long after the instant it describes, and its Meta.deliveredAt is the real arrival, not validAt + light-time.

Fields 4 values
ValueNameDescription
0 Fresh Delivered on its own schedule. An old validAt on a Topic that sends only on change is still fresh.
1 Held Sent to a subscriber that joined while contact was lost, and taken after contact was lost.
2 LastBeforeBlackout Sent to a subscriber that joined while contact was lost: the last sample that got out before contact was lost.
3 Recorded Recovered from the subject's own recorder: taken while it was out of contact, replayed on reacquisition. Precisely dated and never a guess, but not a live reading, and never the subject's current state.

TargetKind

enum

Coarse classification of what vessel.target points at: a vessel, a celestial body, a part of a vessel (a docking port), or 2 (Other) for anything not classified more finely (a waypoint, for instance). A more specific kind may be added later; treat an unrecognised value as 2 (Other).

3 (Position) is used only as an input to vessel.target.set (see SetTargetArgs.latitude and SetTargetArgs.longitude): a map-picked latitude and longitude that no live KSP target object backs, so it never appears as vessel.target's own reported VesselTarget.kind.

Fields 5 values
ValueNameDescription
0 Vessel A vessel. VesselTarget.vesselId carries its guid.
1 Body A celestial body. VesselTarget.bodyIndex carries its trackingStation.bodies index.
2 Other Anything not classified more finely, such as a waypoint. Carries no id.
3 Position A surface latitude and longitude, used only as a vessel.target.set input and never reported.
4 Part A part of a vessel: in practice a docking port (ModuleDockingNode, which implements ITargetable). Identity is the owning vessel's VesselTarget.vesselId guid plus the part's VesselTarget.partId (KSP Part.flightID): a part id alone is not globally unique, only within its vessel.

TargetKnowledge

enum

How the active vessel comes to know of another vessel on target.available, which is also how old what it knows can be.

Fields 3 values
ValueNameDescription
0 InRange The other vessel is within physics range of the active vessel, which sees it as it is.
1 DirectLink The other vessel's radio reaches the active vessel directly, so what is known of it is one signal delay of that link old.
2 CommandCentre The active vessel's command centre knows of the other vessel, by tracking it or by hearing from it, and has told the active vessel over its control route. What is known is as old as the centre's own knowledge plus that route's signal delay.

TargetListEntry

object

One entry in the target.available list: anything the active vessel could set as its target right now. Built from KSP's ITargetable (Vessel / CelestialBody / ModuleDockingNode all implement it) and classified by concrete type into a TargetListEntry.kind plus its stable id, so a modded ITargetable appears as 2 (Other). The stable id per kind (TargetListEntry.vesselId guid / TargetListEntry.bodyIndex / TargetListEntry.partId flightID) is the same id SetTargetArgs takes, so a widget hands an entry straight back into vessel.target.set with no lookup.

Fields 15 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
kind TargetKind

What sort of target this is, which says which id field is set: TargetListEntry.vesselId for a vessel, TargetListEntry.bodyIndex for a body, TargetListEntry.partId (with TargetListEntry.vesselId) for a part.
name string

Clean display name (KSP GetDisplayName(), falling back to GetName()).
vesselId optional string | null

Stable vessel guid: set for 0 (Vessel), and the owning vessel for a 4 (Part). Null otherwise.
bodyIndex optional number | null

Index into trackingStation.bodies: set for 1 (Body). Null otherwise.
partId optional number | null

KSP Part.flightID: set for 4 (Part) (scoped by TargetListEntry.vesselId). Null otherwise.
vesselType optional VesselType | null

Vessel type: set for 0 (Vessel) / 4 (Part) (the owning vessel's type). Null otherwise.
situation optional Situation | null

Flight situation: set for 0 (Vessel). Null otherwise.
distance optional number | null m

Distance from the active vessel, as of the last emission. A coarse sort aid for a picker, not a live readout: it moves every tick but is only refreshed on the channel's slow periodic re-send, and a change in it alone does not trigger an emission. Live distance for the current target comes off vessel.target. Null when a position was not available this tick.
isCurrent boolean

True when this entry is the active vessel's current target (FlightGlobals.fetch.VesselTarget) right now.
source optional TargetKnowledge | null

How the active vessel knows of this vessel: see TargetKnowledge. Set for 0 (Vessel) and for a 4 (Part), which is always in range. Null for a body, whose place is an ephemeris and not something learned.
asOfUt optional number | null ut

The universal time what is known of this vessel was true at: now for one in range, and otherwise when the newest word or sighting of it the active vessel holds was made. The vessel's TargetListEntry.situation and TargetListEntry.orbit are as of this instant. Null for a body.
unchangedToUt optional number | null ut

The universal time up to which the vessel is taken not to have changed since TargetListEntry.asOfUt. A vessel says so when its state changes, so a link that is up and silent is word that it has not. This is worked out from silence and not heard, so an age counted from it is shown as modelled.

For a vessel known over a direct radio link (1 (DirectLink)) that is up, it is now less that link's signal delay.

For a vessel known through the command centre (2 (CommandCentre)), it is what the centre knew one control-route signal delay ago, which is what the active vessel has been told. Where the centre then held the vessel's link as up, it is the latest moment a word could have left the vessel and, by the centre's own plan of the route at that moment, relays and waits for a window included, already have reached the centre. It is never later than the centre's moment less the time the vessel's last word was measured to take. Where the centre had planned no route for the vessel yet, the larger of that measured time and the plan's straight line stands in for the route.

It does not claim the vessel is unchanged now, or that its link is up now: it is the centre's belief, as old as the control route is long, resting on the centre's plan and on the link as the centre last heard it. A word the plan has still on its way is not counted, so the figure can stand well short of the centre's moment less the signal delay, and it is null until some word sent after TargetListEntry.asOfUt would have arrived.

It stops advancing once the link it rests on is held as down, or the control route drops, and is null again once newer word arrives. Null for a vessel in range, a part and a body.
via optional string | null

The display name of the command centre that told the active vessel of this one, for 2 (CommandCentre). Null otherwise.
orbit optional OrbitEntry | null

The vessel's orbit as of TargetListEntry.asOfUt, so its place now can be worked out from where it was last known to be going. Null for a vessel not on an orbit, one whose orbit the active vessel has not been told, a part and a body.
orbitBodyIndex optional number | null

Index into trackingStation.bodies of the body TargetListEntry.orbit is around. Null wherever TargetListEntry.orbit is.

object

TrajectoryKind

enum

What kind of thing an element set describes: a closed-form conic, or a snapshot of an integrated path.

0 (Unspecified) is 0 for the same reason as 0 (Unspecified): a producer that does not set the field gets the value that withholds rather than the one that permits.

Fields 3 values
ValueNameDescription
0 Unspecified No provider stated one. Treat the shape as unknown.
1 Analytic A closed-form conic. The orbit is that conic, so a conic renderer is exactly right and stays right for as long as the horizon allows.
2 Integrated A numerically integrated path. The osculating conic on the wire is a snapshot of it, true at the sample instant and never the path itself, so a client that draws a closed ellipse from it is drawing something the craft will not fly.

UplinkActionReply

object

The reply to system.uplink.cancel (UplinkCancelRequest, stop a delayed command still on its way to the craft) and to system.uplink.resend (UplinkResendRequest, send a held or overdue command again). It reports what the command centre that asked did, not what happened at the craft; that arrives later as comms.journey reports (CommsJourneyEvent). A lane here is the ordered run of delayed commands one centre sends to one craft, and a lane number is a command's place in it (PendingUplink.laneSeq); it is not the lane byte of a binary frame.

Fields 3 fields
FieldTypeUnitDescription
throughSeq number count

For a cancel, the last lane number it covers. It can be higher than the lane number the client saw, when another screen sent on the lane in the meantime. For a send again, the lane number the request named.
id string

For a send again, the new copy's id, which its journey reports name; empty for a cancel.
expiresAtUt number ut

The universal time after which the cancel, or the new copy, is dropped if it has not reached the craft. Both travel to the craft like any delayed command.

Console

This console talks to the Gonogo mod's socket inside the running game, not to the app or its container. With KSP running on this computer it connects straight from this page, at localhost:8090 by default.

A browser blocks a page served over https from reaching a game on another computer. For that, save this page and open the saved file.
